translation: n. 类型，种类 | vt. & vi. 打字
original_sentence: What type of film is shown on each poster?
readingExamples: What type of film is shown on each poster?
Which film type do you like best?
definitionEn:
(1) n. a group of people or things that share particular qualities or features and belong to a larger group; a kind, sort or category
(2) n. a person of a specified nature or character; someone regarded as a representative example of a group
(3) v. to write something using a keyboard, as on a computer or typewriter
(4) n. printed letters or characters; the small metal blocks bearing raised letters formerly used in printing

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （某类型的）典型代表；符合某性格特征的人
uncommonMeanings.example: He was not the type to give up: however fierce the storm, he kept rowing, his knuckles white against the oars and his eyes fixed on the distant shore. （读后续写·人物性格·坚毅刻画）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （印刷用的）铅字，活字；印刷字体
uncommonMeanings.example: In the museum's dim light, rows of worn metal type slept in their wooden trays — silent letters that had once thundered the news of an entire century. （读后续写·博物馆·历史沉思）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 测定（血液等）的类型；分型
uncommonMeanings.example: Before the transfusion could begin, the nurse hurried to type the injured driver's blood, knowing that every lost second narrowed his chance of survival. （读后续写·急救·紧张场景）

posExamples.sentence: Standing before the shelf of paperbacks, Grandpa asked what type of story I loved best, and I whispered 'the kind where the lonely boy finally finds a home' — never guessing he had lived exactly that tale. （读后续写·祖孙对话·情感铺垫）
I am writing to ask what type of documents are required for the student exchange programme, since the notice on the board only mentions a passport without listing the other materials. （应用文·咨询信）

It would be unfair to judge people by a single type of intelligence, for the classroom that treasures only test scores may quietly overlook the artist, the athlete and the born leader sitting in its very rows. （议论文·多元智能·教育公平）
Late into the night she typed the final line of her application essay, then leaned back and let out a breath she felt she had been holding for weeks. （读后续写·备考·心理释放）

wordForms.noun: type（类型）; typist（打字员）; typing（打字）
wordForms.other: typewriter（打字机）; typecast（把…定型于某类角色）; -type（构词后缀：某类型的，如 blood type）

idioms.translation: 是某人喜欢（或欣赏）的类型
idioms.example: Quiet, bookish and endlessly patient, the new librarian was exactly the type of friend Lucy had longed for all through her lonely first term. （读后续写·校园友谊·遇见知己）

idioms.idiom: not be the type to do sth
idioms.translation: 不是那种会做某事的人
idioms.example: Mr. Reed was not the type to boast, so when he quietly mentioned he had once saved a drowning child, the whole staffroom fell silent with new respect. （读后续写·人物揭示·谦逊）

idioms.translation: 不出所料地；本性难移地
idioms.example: True to type, the stubborn old fisherman refused every offer of help and set out alone, convinced that the sea owed no man an easy passage. （读后续写·人物性格·固执）

collocations.phrase: a type of / this type of
collocations.example: This type of film, blending real history with heartfelt human stories, does far more than entertain — it quietly teaches a generation who it is. （议论文·影视的教育意义）
The exhibition displayed different types of traditional crafts, from delicate paper-cutting to bold blue-dyed cloth, each whispering the wisdom of the hands that made it. （应用文·活动介绍）

collocations.phrase: all types of / every type of
collocations.example: Our reading club welcomes all types of learners, whether you devour thrillers overnight or savour a single poem for a week. （应用文·社团招新）
When the doctor announced that only his rare blood type could save the stranger, the shy teenager rolled up his sleeve without a moment's hesitation. （读后续写·无私奉献）
No personality type is destined for success or failure; what truly matters is whether one learns to turn weaknesses into unexpected strengths. （议论文·成长与性格）

collocations.translation: …型的人（坚强型／沉默型／运动型）
collocations.example: Beneath his sporty, easy-going manner, Jack was actually the sensitive type, feeling every unkind word far more deeply than anyone guessed. （读后续写·人物反差）
She typed her password in with trembling fingers, praying that the results of the long-awaited examination would finally appear on the glowing screen. （读后续写·查分·紧张）

collocations.translation: 把（草稿等）打印成正式文稿
collocations.example: After the meeting, I offered to type up the minutes so that every classmate could receive a clear record of what our club had decided. （应用文·活动记录）
Scientists have developed a new type of biodegradable plastic that dissolves harmlessly in seawater, offering fresh hope in the fight against ocean pollution. （议论文·科技与环保）

synonyms.example: What kind of person leaves a warm coat on a stranger's shivering shoulders and slips away before a word of thanks can reach him? （读后续写·善意·设问）
synonyms.usage: kind 最口语、最常用，指"种类"时与 type 几乎通用；type 略正式，还兼有"典型代表"及"打字"等义，kind 无此扩展

synonyms.example: The judges placed her documentary in a category of its own, unable to compare such raw honesty with the polished entries around it. （议论文·评价标准）
synonyms.usage: category 强调经严格划分的"正式类别"，多用于分类、评奖、学术语境，比 type 更书面、更系统

synonyms.example: He was the sort who remembered every classmate's birthday yet never mentioned his own, quietly carrying kindness like a lamp through the school year. （读后续写·人物·默默付出）
synonyms.usage: sort 与 type、kind 意义相近且口语化，'that sort of thing''sort of'为高频口语；表"某类人"时和 type 高度重合，但书面正式度低于 category

synonyms.example: As a genre, science fiction does not merely predict the future; it holds up a mirror in which we glimpse the hopes and fears of our own age. （议论文·文学类型）
synonyms.usage: genre 专指文学、影视、音乐等"艺术体裁"，是本单元 film type 语境的高级替换词；范围窄于 type，学术与影评中显专业

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. was the type who ... , the kind of person who ...
advancedExpressions.example: She was the type who noticed the boy eating alone in the corner, the kind of person who mended silences the way others mend torn sleeves. （定语从句叠加+比喻，含蓄勾勒人物善良，续写刻画配角）

advancedExpressions.expression: Could you kindly clarify what type of ... is expected, as ...
advancedExpressions.example: Could you kindly clarify what type of certificate is expected, as the announcement leaves this crucial detail unspecified? （委婉设问式咨询，礼貌又切中要点，书信高分句）

advancedExpressions.expression: There are broadly two types of ...: those who ... and those who ...
advancedExpressions.example: There are broadly two types of learners: those who wait to be pushed and those who set their own course — and it is invariably the latter who go the distance. （二分对照结构，逻辑清晰，快速搭建论证框架）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I like this type of film.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is this type of film — where an ordinary soul stumbles, falls and rises again — that speaks to me most, for in its flickering light I keep meeting a braver version of myself. （读后续写／记叙升华）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is ... that 强调句突出偏爱 + 破折号插入定义式定语 + 比喻(flickering light)+ meeting a braver version of myself 收束点题

sentenceUpgrade.original: There are many types of people in our club.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Our club embraces every type of dreamer, from the quiet writer scribbling in corners to the fearless debater who thrives on the stage, proving that difference, far from dividing us, is exactly what makes us whole. （应用文·社团介绍）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: embrace every type of 提升动词表现力 + from ... to ... 列举具象化 + proving 分词状语点明主旨 + far from ... 否定插入强调对比

original_sentence: Action / Horror / Cartoon / Musical / Comedy / Romance / Documentary / Science fiction / Fantasy / War
readingExamples: Action / Horror / Cartoon / Musical / Comedy / Romance / Documentary / Science fiction / Fantasy / War
definitionEn:
(1) n. a film, play or programme that is intended to be amusing and usually has a happy ending
(2) n. the branch of drama and entertainment concerned with making people laugh; humorous performance as a genre
(3) n. the amusing or funny quality of a situation; an event or aspect of life that seems ridiculous or laughable

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （生活中）滑稽可笑的事；令人啼笑皆非的局面
uncommonMeanings.example: What had begun as a solemn ceremony dissolved into pure comedy the moment the mayor's speech was drowned out by a stray goat wandering onto the stage. （读后续写·意外场面·喜剧转折）

posExamples.sentence: Half an hour into the comedy, Grandma was laughing so hard that tears rolled down her cheeks, and for one golden evening the worries of the whole difficult year seemed to melt away. （读后续写·家庭温情·笑声疗愈）
I would like to recommend a heart-warming comedy for our class film night, since a good laugh together is exactly what we all need after a month of intense revision. （应用文·推荐信）
Comedy is far more than cheap laughter; at its finest it holds up a gentle mirror to our follies, letting us recognise and forgive our own imperfections. （议论文·喜剧的价值）
The school comedy we staged was rough around the edges, yet when the final joke landed and the hall erupted in applause, every stumbled line suddenly felt worthwhile. （读后续写·校园演出·成就感）

wordForms.noun: comedy（喜剧）; comedian（喜剧演员）; comedienne（女喜剧演员）
wordForms.adjective: comic（喜剧的，滑稽的）; comical（好笑的，滑稽可笑的）
wordForms.other: comedy of errors（一连串误会引发的闹剧）

idioms.translation: 一连串阴差阳错引发的闹剧；令人啼笑皆非的混乱局面
idioms.example: Our attempt to surprise the teacher turned into a comedy of errors — the cake toppled, the lights failed, yet her delighted laughter told us the mess had been worth every misstep. （读后续写·惊喜策划·温馨收场）

collocations.example: On rainy Sundays my sister and I curl up with a romantic comedy, and no matter how predictable the ending, we cheer for the lovers as if seeing it all for the first time. （读后续写·姐妹时光·温馨）
The comedy show raised a wave of laughter across the audience, yet woven quietly beneath the jokes was a tender plea for kindness toward the lonely elderly. （议论文·喜剧的社会关怀）
Trembling behind the microphone, the shy boy delivered his first stand-up comedy, and the roar of laughter that followed rebuilt, joke by joke, the confidence he had lost. （读后续写·突破自我·舞台成长）
Life mingles comedy and tragedy so closely that the very moment we burst out laughing may be the one we later remember through tears. （议论文·人生思辨）
Our drama club is rehearsing a lively musical comedy, and we warmly invite every student to come and share an evening of song, dance and laughter. （应用文·活动邀请）
The clumsy new puppy brought endless comedy to our quiet household, chasing its own tail until even Grandfather set down his newspaper to laugh. （读后续写·家庭·温馨幽默）
The waiter slipping on the very banana skin he had just warned the guests about was the height of comedy, and the whole restaurant dissolved into helpless laughter. （读后续写·滑稽场面）

synonyms.example: Her gentle humour could thaw the tensest classroom, turning a nervous silence into ripples of easy laughter within a single sentence. （读后续写·人物魅力·化解尴尬）
synonyms.usage: humour 是抽象的"幽默感、诙谐特质"，可存在于人、语言或情境中；comedy 是具体的"喜剧作品／滑稽事件"，属可数名词，二者不能混用

synonyms.example: What should have been a dignified debate descended into farce as both speakers, red-faced and shouting, forgot every point they had come to make. （议论文·批评混乱局面）
synonyms.usage: farce 特指情节夸张、动作滑稽的"闹剧"，也常贬指"荒唐透顶的场面"，语气比 comedy 更强、常带批评色彩

synonyms.example: Every Friday the whole dormitory gathered around a laptop for the latest sitcom, and those shared bursts of laughter quietly stitched us into a family. （读后续写·校园生活·情谊）
synonyms.usage: sitcom（situation comedy 的缩略）专指"电视情景喜剧"这一具体形式，范围窄于泛指的 comedy，口语中更常用

advancedExpressions.expression: what had seemed a disaster suddenly turned into comedy when ...
advancedExpressions.example: What had seemed a disaster suddenly turned into comedy when the spilt flour crowned Dad's head white, and our anxious kitchen exploded into laughter. （情节反转句式，化紧张为温馨，续写高潮转折）

advancedExpressions.expression: I cannot recommend this comedy highly enough, for it ...
advancedExpressions.example: I cannot recommend this comedy highly enough, for it offers not only two hours of laughter but a warm reminder to cherish the people around us. （双重否定强推荐 + for 引出理由，推荐信亮点句）

advancedExpressions.expression: beneath its laughter, comedy often ...
advancedExpressions.example: Beneath its laughter, comedy often conceals the sharpest truths, allowing us to face our flaws with a smile rather than a frown. （地点状语前置+对比 smile/frown，揭示喜剧深层价值）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The comedy made everyone laugh.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The comedy sent wave after wave of laughter rolling through the hall, until even the sternest teacher, fighting a losing battle with a smile, finally surrendered and laughed along with us. （读后续写·集体欢乐·细节渲染）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: send ... rolling through 化抽象为动态画面 + wave after wave 反复强化 + fighting a losing battle with a smile 拟人细节 + finally surrendered 反差收束

sentenceUpgrade.original: I think comedy is good for us.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is my firm belief that comedy does us a quiet good, for shared laughter dissolves the walls of shyness and stress far more gently than any lecture ever could. （议论文·观点陈述）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is my firm belief that 正式主句立论 + for 引出因果 + dissolves the walls of ... 隐喻具象化 + far more ... than 比较结构强化说服力

translation: n. 纪录片，纪实节目 | adj. 文件的；纪录的
original_sentence: Action / Horror / Cartoon / Musical / Comedy / Romance / Documentary / Science fiction / Fantasy / War
readingExamples: Action / Horror / Cartoon / Musical / Comedy / Romance / Documentary / Science fiction / Fantasy / War
definitionEn:
(1) n. a film, television or radio programme that gives facts and information about a real subject, often examining it in depth
(2) adj. consisting of or based on official documents; using written records as evidence
(3) adj. presenting facts objectively about real events, people or situations, as opposed to fiction

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 文件的；由文件（书面记录）构成的
uncommonMeanings.example: The lawyer laid out page after page of documentary evidence — faded letters, signed receipts, a will yellowed with age — until the courtroom fell utterly silent. （读后续写·法庭·真相揭露）

posExamples.sentence: Halfway through the wildlife documentary, the screen filled with a mother polar bear guiding her cubs across the cracking ice, and the whole classroom held its breath, moved by a tenderness no textbook had ever captured. （读后续写·观影·情感触动）
I am writing to recommend an inspiring documentary about young volunteers in remote villages, for I believe it will encourage our classmates to look beyond themselves. （应用文·推荐信）
A well-made documentary can do what no lecture ever manages: it lets distant suffering look us in the eye, stirring not merely our knowledge but our conscience. （议论文·纪录片的力量）
The historian relied on documentary sources rather than hearsay, poring over decades-old newspapers until the forgotten heroine's story finally stepped back into the light. （议论文·治学严谨／叙事结合）

wordForms.noun: documentary（纪录片）; document（文件）; documentation（文件材料，证明文件）; documentarian / documentary-maker（纪录片制作人）
wordForms.adjective: documentary（文件的；纪实的）; documented（有记录的，有证据的）

collocations.example: It was a simple nature documentary that first lit the spark: watching whales sing beneath the waves, ten-year-old Amy quietly decided she would one day protect the sea. （读后续写·梦想萌芽·励志）
To make this documentary, the young director spent three winters filming in the mountains, his camera and his conviction never once freezing over. （读后续写·执着追梦）
The documentary on plastic pollution left the audience speechless, its final image — a seabird's stomach full of bottle caps — searing itself into every memory. （议论文·环保警示）
Our media club is producing a short documentary film about the unsung cleaners of our school, hoping to give their quiet dedication the recognition it has long deserved. （应用文·活动介绍）
Without a shred of documentary evidence, the wild accusation collapsed the moment it was calmly questioned. （议论文·理性求证）
As a documentary photographer, she believed the truest picture was never posed, so she waited, invisible and patient, for the unguarded moment to reveal itself. （读后续写·人物·艺术追求）
The award-winning documentary followed a village teacher for a decade, and by its closing scene not a single eye in the hall remained dry. （读后续写·感人叙事）

synonyms.example: Unlike a documentary bound to fact, a feature film is free to imagine, yet the best of them still whisper truths about who we really are. （议论文·纪实与虚构对比）
synonyms.usage: feature film 指"虚构的剧情长片"，与"纪实、以事实为本"的 documentary 恰成对照；作对比论证时常并举二者

synonyms.translation: 纪实性剧情片（真人真事改编但有戏剧化演绎）
synonyms.example: The docudrama recreated the rescue with actors and tension, blurring the line between what truly happened and what the camera chose to dramatise. （议论文·真实与演绎）
synonyms.usage: docudrama 介于 documentary 与虚构剧之间，取材真实但加入戏剧化表演；documentary 更强调客观记录，一般不安排演员搬演

synonyms.example: The old photographs served as a faithful record of a vanished street, each fading image guarding a corner of the city's memory. （读后续写·怀旧·历史感）
synonyms.usage: record 泛指任何形式的"记录"（文字、影像、声音）；documentary 特指"纪录片"这一影视体裁，或"文件的、纪实的"这一形容词义

advancedExpressions.expression: it was a documentary that first ... , and from that moment ...
advancedExpressions.example: It was a documentary that first opened my eyes to the melting glaciers, and from that moment I could no longer walk past a dripping tap in silence. （强调句+时间转折，写内心转变的起点，续写立志段）

advancedExpressions.expression: This documentary is well worth watching, not only because ... but also because ...
advancedExpressions.example: This documentary is well worth watching, not only because it is beautifully filmed, but also because it gently reshapes the way we see the world around us. （not only ... but also 递进推荐，推荐信提升说服力）

advancedExpressions.expression: compared with dry statistics, a documentary ...
advancedExpressions.example: Compared with dry statistics, a documentary gives distant tragedy a human face, turning numbers we forget into stories we cannot. （对比状语开篇+把抽象数字人格化，突出纪实影像的感染力）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The documentary was very moving.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The documentary did not simply inform us; it reached into the room and gripped our hearts, leaving a silence so heavy that no one dared to be the first to speak when the screen went dark. （读后续写·观影·集体震撼）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: not simply ... 否定递进 + reached into ... gripped 拟人化动作 + leaving 分词表结果 + no one dared to be the first to speak 以细节写震撼

sentenceUpgrade.original: Documentaries teach us about the real world.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Precisely because they refuse to look away, documentaries teach us about a real world that fiction is often too kind to show, forcing comfort to give way to conscience. （议论文·观点提升）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Precisely because 前置原因状语强化逻辑 + refuse to look away 拟人 + that fiction is often too kind to show 定语从句对比 + forcing ... to give way to 递进收束

original_sentence: Action / Horror / Cartoon / Musical / Comedy / Romance / Documentary / Science fiction / Fantasy / War
readingExamples: Action / Horror / Cartoon / Musical / Comedy / Romance / Documentary / Science fiction / Fantasy / War
definitionEn:
(1) n. a genre of imaginative fiction involving magic, mythical creatures or worlds that could not exist in reality
(2) n. a pleasant but unlikely situation that you imagine but that is not real; a daydream
(3) n. the activity of imagining things, or the power of the mind to invent images and ideas
(4) n. an idea or belief that has no basis in fact; a false or unrealistic notion

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 不切实际的空想；脱离现实的幻念
uncommonMeanings.example: For years he clung to the fantasy that his father would one day walk back through the door, until a single honest conversation with his mother finally set him free. （读后续写·成长·直面现实）

posExamples.sentence: As the last page turned, the world of the fantasy dissolved around Emma — the dragons, the floating castles, the singing rivers — and she looked up, half-surprised to find herself still curled in her own quiet bedroom. （读后续写·沉浸阅读·奇幻氛围）
I am writing to recommend a wonderful fantasy novel for our reading corner, as its magical world offers a much-needed escape after our exhausting weeks of study. （应用文·推荐信）
Far from being childish escapism, fantasy exercises the very muscle that all progress depends on — the human power to imagine a world different from the one we are handed. （议论文·想象力的价值）

Winning the lottery had always been Uncle Joe's private fantasy, yet the day it nearly came true, he discovered that what he had truly longed for was not money at all, but time with the family he had neglected. （读后续写·反转·人生领悟）

wordForms.noun: fantasy（幻想作品；空想）; fantasist（爱空想的人；奇幻作家）
wordForms.adjective: fantastic（极好的；奇异的，幻想的）; fantastical（离奇的，异想天开的）

idioms.translation: 生活在幻想世界里，脱离现实
idioms.example: His friends warned that he was living in a fantasy world, but it was precisely that stubborn dreaming that, years later, gave the world its most daring invention. （读后续写·梦想·力排众议）

idioms.translation: 一阵天马行空的想象；异想天开
idioms.example: In a sudden flight of fantasy, the lonely boy imagined the old lighthouse as a rocket, ready to carry him far beyond the grey little town. （读后续写·童心·想象场景）

collocations.example: The fantasy film swept us into a realm of floating islands and talking beasts, yet its truest magic was the courage it quietly kindled in every child watching. （议论文·奇幻的意义）
The line between fantasy and reality blurred as she stepped through the misty forest, no longer certain which world was dreaming the other. （读后续写·奇幻·梦境感）

collocations.phrase: live out / act out a fantasy
collocations.translation: 实现（一度只存于想象的）幻想
collocations.example: Standing at last on the concert stage, she was finally living out the fantasy that had comforted her through a thousand lonely practice nights. （读后续写·圆梦·舞台）
Whenever the arguments downstairs grew loud, the child would escape into fantasy, building in her mind a house where no one ever raised their voice. （读后续写·童年·心理避难所）
Great writers of fantasy do not flee reality; they build a world of fantasy in which the deepest truths of our own can finally be spoken. （议论文·文学创作）

collocations.translation: 纯属幻想，完全不切实际
collocations.example: The idea that success comes without struggle is sheer fantasy; behind every effortless-looking triumph lie years of unseen toil. （议论文·勤奋主题）
It is one thing to indulge in fantasy for a pleasant hour, and quite another to let it quietly steal the years meant for real living. （议论文·空想与行动）

synonyms.example: With nothing but a cardboard box and a boundless imagination, the twins turned a rainy afternoon into a voyage across seven seas. （读后续写·童趣·创造力）
synonyms.usage: imagination 是中性、褒义的"想象力"，强调创造与构想的能力；fantasy 更侧重"幻想的内容或作品"，有时带"不切实际"的贬义

synonyms.example: Lost in a daydream by the window, she barely heard the teacher call her name for the third time. （读后续写·走神·校园细节）
synonyms.usage: daydream 指清醒时短暂、愉快的"走神、遐想"，通常轻描淡写；fantasy 的想象更成体系、更宏大，也可指整个奇幻文类

synonyms.example: The mirage shimmered on the horizon like a lake, a cruel illusion that had lured many a thirsty traveller to their end. （读后续写·沙漠·危险氛围）
synonyms.usage: illusion 强调"与事实不符的错觉、假象"，常暗含被欺骗或误导；fantasy 是主动的、有意识的想象，未必虚假，也可指文学体裁

synonyms.example: It is a persistent myth that talent alone decides success, when in truth persistence outlasts talent nine times out of ten. （议论文·勤奋战胜天赋）
synonyms.usage: myth 指"广为流传却站不住脚的观念"或"神话传说"；fantasy 侧重个人或文学的想象，二者在"不实观念"义上部分重合，但 myth 更强调其"被普遍误信"

advancedExpressions.expression: what had once been mere fantasy was now within reach
advancedExpressions.example: As the finish line rose before her, what had once been mere fantasy was now within reach, close enough to touch, earned stride by aching stride. （today-vs-once 时间对照 + earned ... stride by stride 收束，写梦想成真的顿悟）

advancedExpressions.expression: if you long to escape the ordinary, this fantasy is exactly ...
advancedExpressions.example: If you long to escape the ordinary for an afternoon, this fantasy is exactly the doorway you have been looking for. （条件句召唤读者 + doorway 隐喻，推荐信生动开场）

advancedExpressions.expression: every great achievement begins as a fantasy in someone's mind
advancedExpressions.example: Every great achievement begins as a fantasy in someone's mind before it is ever written into the world; without the dreamers, there would be nothing for the doers to build. （溯源式立论 + dreamers/doers 对照，论证想象力的奠基作用）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She liked to imagine another world.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Whenever the real world pressed too hard, she slipped into a fantasy of her own making — a bright, boundless place where the shy girl at the back of the class became a hero at last. （读后续写·心理·内心世界）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Whenever 时间状语起笔 + slipped into 动词生动化 + 破折号插入具体描绘 + at last 收束情感 + shy girl / hero 反差点题

sentenceUpgrade.original: Fantasy is not useless.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Far from being an idle escape, fantasy is the seedbed of every invention we now take for granted, for nothing was ever built that had not first been imagined. （议论文·价值升华）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Far from being 否定前置纠正偏见 + seedbed 隐喻 + for 引出论据 + nothing ... that had not first been imagined 双重否定强化必然性

translation: 恐怖电影（或故事等）；震惊，恐惧
original_sentence: Action / Horror / Cartoon / Musical / Comedy / Romance / Documentary / Science fiction / Fantasy / War
readingExamples: Action / Horror / Cartoon / Musical / Comedy / Romance / Documentary / Science fiction / Fantasy / War
definitionEn:
(1) n. a strong feeling of shock, fear and disgust caused by something terrible or frightening
(2) n. a film, story or book that is intended to frighten people, dealing with the supernatural or violent events (also horror film / horror story)
(3) n. something that causes horror; a terrible or shocking thing, event or experience
(4) n. (informal) a person, especially a child, who behaves badly; a naughty or troublesome person

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （非正式，常带戏谑）淘气鬼，捣蛋鬼；讨厌的人
uncommonMeanings.example: 'Come back here, you little horror!' Grandma called after the giggling boy, though the smile tugging at her lips betrayed just how much she adored the mischief. （读后续写·祖孙·温馨戏谑）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （口语，the horrors）极度的恐惧或不安；令人毛骨悚然之物
uncommonMeanings.example: The abandoned hospital gave her the horrors — every creaking door and flickering bulb seemed to whisper that she was not, after all, alone. （读后续写·恐怖氛围·悬疑）

posExamples.sentence: Frozen at the top of the stairs, Lucy watched in horror as the shadow beneath the door stretched slowly, impossibly long, and a floorboard groaned somewhere far too close behind her. （读后续写·惊悚·画面感）
I am writing to express my horror at the careless dumping of chemical waste into our river, and to urge the community to act before this precious water is lost forever. （应用文·倡议信）
To look away from the horrors of war is easy and comforting; yet it is precisely by refusing to look away that a generation learns never to repeat them. （议论文·反战·历史反思）
My little brother insists on watching a horror before bed, then spends the whole night convinced that every shadow in the corridor is quietly moving toward his door. （读后续写·家庭·幽默恐惧）

wordForms.adjective: horrible（可怕的，糟糕的）; horrific（令人恐惧的，可怕的）; horrified（感到惊恐的）; horrifying（令人恐惧的）
wordForms.adverb: horribly（可怕地，极其）; horrifically（骇人地）
wordForms.other: horror film / horror story（恐怖片／恐怖故事）; horror-struck / horror-stricken（惊恐万状的）

idioms.example: To my horror, the moment I reached the summit, the rope slipped from my numb fingers and vanished silently over the edge into the white nothing below. （读后续写·登山遇险·惊恐时刻）
She shrank back in horror as the snake reared up on the path, yet in the next breath she remembered the trembling child behind her and stood her ground. （读后续写·恐惧与勇气·转折）
Ever since the flood, Grandpa had a horror of rising water, and the first grey clouds of the season would set his hands quietly shaking. （读后续写·心理创伤·人物刻画）

collocations.example: The whole crowd stepped back in horror as the burning beam crashed down, but one firefighter ran forward, straight into the very danger everyone else was fleeing. （读后续写·灾难·英雄凸显）
Our film club is screening a classic horror film this Friday, so bring a brave friend and a warm blanket for a night of delicious frights. （应用文·活动通知）
To her horror, she realised she had left the stove burning, and she raced home through the rain with her heart pounding louder than her footsteps. （读后续写·惊觉·紧张追赶）

collocations.phrase: the horrors of war / famine / poverty
collocations.example: The old photographs laid bare the horrors of famine, and no student in that hushed classroom would ever again waste a single grain of rice. （议论文·珍惜粮食·警醒）

collocations.phrase: a look / cry / gasp of horror
collocations.translation: 惊恐的表情／叫喊／倒抽气
collocations.example: A cry of horror tore through the theatre as the chandelier swayed, and for one endless heartbeat nobody knew whether it was part of the show. （读后续写·剧院·悬疑）

collocations.phrase: be filled with horror / be struck with horror
collocations.example: Filled with horror at the thought of losing her only photograph of her mother, she plunged back into the smoke-choked room without a second thought. （读后续写·亲情·奋不顾身）
Much to his horror, the words he had scribbled as a private joke had somehow been read aloud to the entire assembly. （读后续写·尴尬·意外）
The villagers could only watch in horror as the river swallowed the bridge inch by inch, carrying away a century of shared memories. （读后续写·洪灾·悲怆）

synonyms.example: Sheer terror rooted her to the spot; her legs, which had carried her through a hundred races, now refused to move a single step. （读后续写·极度恐惧·身体反应）
synonyms.usage: terror 指最强烈、最令人瘫痪的"极度恐惧"，程度重于 horror；horror 常兼有"震惊、厌恶"的成分，还可指"恐怖片"这一体裁，terror 无此义

synonyms.example: A quiet dread settled over her as the day of the results drew near, souring every meal and stealing every peaceful night. （读后续写·考前·心理）
synonyms.usage: dread 侧重对"即将发生之事"的持续畏惧、忧惧，多为预期性的；horror 多由眼前具体可怕之物瞬间引发，更即时、更强烈

synonyms.example: He mastered his fear the only way courage allows — not by feeling none, but by walking forward in spite of it. （议论文·勇气·哲理）
synonyms.usage: fear 是最普通、最广义的"害怕"，程度可轻可重；horror 特指伴随"震惊、厌恶"的强烈恐惧，语气比 fear 重得多

synonyms.example: She turned away in disgust at the sight of the litter smothering the once-clear stream, and there and then vowed to organise a clean-up. （议论文·环保·情感驱动）
synonyms.usage: disgust 强调"厌恶、反感"这一层，不含"害怕"；horror 是"恐惧+厌恶"的复合情绪，二者可叠加（in horror and disgust）

advancedExpressions.expression: a chill of horror ran down sb's spine as ...
advancedExpressions.example: A chill of horror ran down her spine as she realised the footprints in the snow, leading straight to the cabin door, were not her own. （生理反应写恐惧 + 悬念收尾，续写惊悚高潮）

advancedExpressions.expression: it fills me with horror to see ... ; I therefore call on ... to ...
advancedExpressions.example: It fills me with horror to see our beloved lake choked with rubbish; I therefore call on every resident to join this weekend's clean-up. （情感开场 + call on 呼吁，倡议信情理并重）

advancedExpressions.expression: only by remembering the horrors of ... can we hope to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Only by remembering the horrors of the past can we hope to build a future in which such suffering is never allowed to return. （Only by ... 倒装强调 + can we hope to 收束，反思类议论文高分句）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She was very afraid when she saw it.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The moment she saw it, a wave of horror washed over her — her breath caught, her fingers turned to ice, and the scream she wanted to give came out as nothing but silence. （读后续写·极度恐惧·细节堆叠）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: The moment 时间状语强化即时感 + a wave of horror washed over 隐喻 + 三重身体反应铺陈(breath, fingers, scream) + came out as silence 反差收束

sentenceUpgrade.original: War is terrible and we should stop it.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The horrors of war leave scars that no treaty can heal and no monument can measure; it is therefore the sacred duty of every generation to guard the fragile peace it inherits. （议论文·反战·升华）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: The horrors of war 抽象名词化主语 + no ... can ... 平行否定强化 + it is the sacred duty of ... to 责任句式 + fragile peace / inherits 收束呼应

original_sentence: Action / Horror / Cartoon / Musical / Comedy / Romance / Documentary / Science fiction / Fantasy / War
readingExamples: Action / Horror / Cartoon / Musical / Comedy / Romance / Documentary / Science fiction / Fantasy / War
definitionEn:
(1) n. a love affair or romantic relationship, especially one that is exciting and short-lived
(2) n. a film, novel or story dealing with love, often in an idealised or adventurous way; the genre of such stories
(3) n. a feeling of mystery, excitement, wonder and remoteness from everyday life
(4) n. the quality of being romantic; feelings and behaviour associated with love and courtship

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （对某地、某事的）传奇色彩，浪漫魅力；令人神往的氛围
uncommonMeanings.example: For young Tom, nothing could rival the romance of the open railway — the distant whistle, the swaying carriages, the promise that they were bound for somewhere his small town could never be. （读后续写·少年·远方向往）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （旧或书面）虚构，夸大其词；编造离奇故事
uncommonMeanings.example: The old sailor loved to romance about sea monsters and buried gold, and the wide-eyed children never once thought to doubt a single word. （读后续写·人物·讲故事的老者）

posExamples.sentence: Their romance began not with grand words but with a shared umbrella in a sudden downpour, two strangers walking slower than the rain required, neither willing to reach the corner where they would have to part. （读后续写·邂逅·细腻情感）
I am writing to recommend a touching romance for our class library, for beneath its love story lies a gentle lesson about patience, sacrifice and second chances. （应用文·推荐信）
True romance in literature does not lie in flawless heroes and effortless happy endings, but in the quiet courage of ordinary people who choose love again after being hurt by it. （议论文·文学与爱情）

There is a certain romance to travelling by night train — the darkened window, the rhythm of the rails, the strangers' murmured stories drifting through the dim carriage until sleep finally claims them all. （读后续写·旅途·氛围渲染）

wordForms.noun: romance（爱情故事；浪漫）; romantic（浪漫的人）; romanticism（浪漫主义）
wordForms.verb: romance（追求；虚构）; romanticize（使浪漫化，理想化）
wordForms.other: Romance languages（罗曼语族，如法语、西班牙语等）; hopeless romantic（不可救药的浪漫主义者）

idioms.translation: 旋风般的（迅猛而短暂的）恋情
idioms.example: After a whirlwind romance one unforgettable summer, they parted at the station promising to write, unaware that a single autumn would carry them into entirely different lives. （读后续写·夏日恋情·离别）

collocations.example: The romance film moved the whole cinema to tears, yet what lingered afterwards was not the kiss in the rain but the years of quiet devotion that had led up to it. （议论文·爱情作品的深度）
What began as a light-hearted summer romance slowly deepened into something neither of them had the words to name, long after the beach and the sunshine were gone. （读后续写·恋情·情感升温）
The romance of the old bookshop lay in its dust and disorder, in the thrill of never knowing which forgotten treasure the next shelf might hold. （读后续写·怀旧·氛围）
Even after forty years of marriage, Grandpa kept the romance alive, leaving a wildflower on Grandma's pillow every single morning without fail. （读后续写·恒久之爱·细节）
The whole class watched the budding romance between the two shy classmates with knowing smiles, careful never to say a word that might frighten it away. （读后续写·校园·青涩爱情）
She once had a brief romance with a travelling musician, and to this day a certain melody can still bring the whole distant summer flooding back. （读后续写·回忆·旧情）
A single handwritten letter, unearthed from a dusty drawer, was all it took to rekindle the romance the busy years had almost allowed to fade. （读后续写·破镜重圆）

synonyms.example: Their love needed no audience and no grand gestures; it lived quietly in shared silences and in the way each always saved the last bite for the other. （读后续写·平淡真情）
synonyms.usage: love 是最广、最深的"爱"，可指亲情、友情、爱情，情感持久而根本；romance 侧重爱情中"浪漫、激情、新鲜"的一面，常指具体恋情或爱情故事

synonyms.translation: 风流韵事；（尤指不正当的）恋情
synonyms.example: The scandalous affair set the whole village whispering, though few paused to wonder what loneliness had driven two lonely people together. （读后续写·小镇·流言）
synonyms.usage: affair 多指"（常为秘密或不正当的）短暂恋情"，可含贬义；romance 语气中性偏美好，强调浪漫感受，不必然指不正当关系

synonyms.example: Their old-fashioned courtship stretched over two patient years of letters and Sunday walks before he finally dared to ask for her hand. （读后续写·旧式恋爱·含蓄）
synonyms.usage: courtship 特指恋爱中"求爱、追求"的过程阶段，略显正式或旧派；romance 涵盖整段恋情乃至爱情文类，范围更广

synonyms.example: The passion that had once burned so fiercely between them gradually mellowed, over the years, into something steadier and far more precious. （议论文／记叙·爱情的成熟）
synonyms.usage: passion 强调"炽烈、汹涌的激情"，情绪浓度高但未必持久；romance 更偏"浪漫氛围与情调"，可炽烈也可温婉悠长

advancedExpressions.expression: there was a quiet romance in the way ...
advancedExpressions.example: There was a quiet romance in the way he always walked on the side nearest the traffic, a small daily kindness that spoke louder than any promise. （抽象名词+定语从句写细节 + spoke louder than 收束，续写含蓄写情）

advancedExpressions.expression: beyond its romance, the story offers ...
advancedExpressions.example: Beyond its romance, the story offers a quiet meditation on forgiveness, which is precisely why I believe every classmate should read it. （让步式提升 + which is precisely why 推荐理由，推荐信升格）

advancedExpressions.expression: romance may fade, but ... endures
advancedExpressions.example: The dizzy romance of first love may fade with time, but the loyalty and understanding it can grow into endure for a lifetime. （may ... but 对照句式 + fade/endure 反义收束，爱情类议论文点睛）

sentenceUpgrade.original: They fell in love.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Their romance crept up on them as gently as dusk over the harbour — no single moment they could name, only the slow, sweet realisation that the day now felt unfinished until they had spoken. （读后续写·爱情·细腻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: romance crept up on them 拟人化过程 + as gently as dusk over the harbour 明喻 + no ... only ... 否定对照 + the day felt unfinished until 以感受写深情

sentenceUpgrade.original: This romance novel is worth reading.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: This romance is well worth reading, not because it promises a perfect love, but because it dares to show how imperfect people, stumbling and forgiving, slowly learn to love at all. （应用文·推荐信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: well worth reading 提升表达 + not because ... but because 递进纠偏 + imperfect people, stumbling and forgiving 插入描绘 + learn to love at all 收束深化主题

original_sentence: Science fiction (informal sci‑fi; abbr: SF) 科幻电影（或小说等）
readingExamples: Science fiction (informal sci‑fi; abbr: SF) 科幻电影（或小说等）
definitionEn:
(1) n. a type of literature that describes imaginary people and events, especially novels and short stories
(2) n. novels and stories collectively, as a category (as opposed to non-fiction)
(3) n. something that is invented or untrue; a false account presented as fact
(4) n. a widely believed idea or belief that is not actually true

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 虚构的谎言；捏造的说法
uncommonMeanings.example: The account he gave the police was pure fiction, a web of half-truths spun so smoothly that even he seemed to believe it by the end. （读后续写·悬疑推理·谎言拆穿）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （人们普遍相信却站不住脚的）虚妄观念
uncommonMeanings.example: It is a comforting fiction that talent alone decides success; behind every 'overnight sensation' lie years of unglamorous, invisible toil. （议论文·努力与天赋·打破迷思）

posExamples.sentence: Curled up in the attic with a torch and a tattered paperback, the boy lost himself so completely in science fiction that he barely noticed the storm hammering against the roof. （读后续写·童年阅读·环境+沉浸）

I am writing to recommend that our school library expand its collection of English fiction, for well-chosen stories can nurture both language skills and imagination far more vividly than textbooks alone. （应用文·建议信）
Far from being a mere escape from reality, fiction quietly trains our empathy, allowing us to live a thousand lives and to feel, if only for a while, what it means to be someone else. （议论文·文学的价值）
As the detective laid the evidence on the table one piece at a time, the suspect's carefully rehearsed story began to unravel, exposed at last as nothing but fiction. （读后续写·真相揭露·反转）

wordForms.other: fiction writer（小说家）; nonfiction（非虚构类作品）

idioms.translation: 真事比小说还离奇（现实往往比虚构更不可思议）
idioms.example: When the long-lost brothers were reunited by a chance seat on the same flight, the old man shook his head and murmured, 'Truth really is stranger than fiction.' （读后续写·久别重逢·感慨）

idioms.idiom: fact and fiction / separate fact from fiction
idioms.example: In an age flooded with online rumours, the ability to separate fact from fiction has become one of the most vital skills a young person can possess. （议论文·信息素养）

collocations.example: The film blends heart-stopping science fiction with a tender human story, so that even viewers who dislike spaceships leave the cinema deeply moved. （应用文·影评/推荐）

collocations.translation: 一部虚构作品，一本小说
collocations.example: Although the novel is a work of fiction, every character seems so real that readers find themselves worrying about them long after the last page. （读后续写/议论文·文学感悟）
Ever since she was ten, Emma had dreamed of writing fiction that would make lonely children feel a little less alone. （读后续写·作家梦·人物动机）

collocations.translation: 历史 / 侦探 / 言情小说
collocations.example: Our reading club will devote next month to detective fiction, and members are warmly invited to share the twist that fooled them the most. （应用文·社团通知）
The so-called 'insider report' turned out to be pure fiction, and its author later admitted he had never set foot in the company. （议论文·媒体真实性）

collocations.phrase: fiction and reality / blur the line between fiction and reality
collocations.translation: 虚构与现实；模糊虚构与现实的界限
collocations.example: So immersive was the virtual game that some players began to blur the line between fiction and reality, forgetting where the screen ended and life began. （议论文·科技反思）

collocations.translation: 一篇虚构故事；（贬）一派胡言
collocations.example: His grand excuse for missing the deadline was such an obvious piece of fiction that the whole office struggled to keep a straight face. （读后续写·职场幽默）
Books opened a door for the shy village girl, and in the world of fiction she found courage that the real world had long denied her. （读后续写·成长治愈）

synonyms.example: She stayed up until dawn to finish the novel, tears blurring the final page as the two friends said their last goodbye. （读后续写·感人阅读）
synonyms.usage: novel 指具体的一部长篇小说，是可数名词；fiction 是不可数的总称，泛指'虚构文学'这一类别，如 a shelf of fiction 一书架小说

synonyms.example: Grandma's stories, half memory and half imagination, wove the long winter nights into something warm and unforgettable. （读后续写·亲情记忆）
synonyms.usage: story 既可指真实经历也可指虚构故事，范围最广、最口语；fiction 特指'虚构的、非真实的'文学或说法，强调其非事实属性

synonyms.example: It is a persistent myth that memorising word lists guarantees fluency; real language ability grows through use, not through hoarding. （议论文·学习方法）
synonyms.usage: myth 作'虚妄观念'时强调'广为流传却错误'；fiction 作此义时更中性，泛指'虚构、不真实的说法'，二者在'打破迷思'语境中可互补使用

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. was so lost in the world of fiction that ...
advancedExpressions.example: She was so lost in the world of fiction that the ringing bell, the emptying classroom, even the fading afternoon light all dissolved into nothing around her. （so...that 结果状语+三项排比虚化环境，渲染专注入迷）

advancedExpressions.expression: I would strongly recommend ... , a work of fiction that ...
advancedExpressions.example: I would strongly recommend Journey to the West, a work of fiction that not only entertains but also teaches the young reader courage, loyalty and perseverance. （recommend+同位语从句，推荐信点明作品价值）

advancedExpressions.expression: far from being mere fiction, ... in fact ...
advancedExpressions.example: Far from being mere fiction, great literature in fact holds up a mirror to society, reflecting truths that dry statistics can never capture. （far from 否定纠偏+in fact 反转，为文学正名的论证句式）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He liked reading science fiction.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Long after lights-out, a small torch would flicker beneath his blanket, for science fiction had become the secret universe into which he escaped each night, trading his cramped bedroom for boundless galaxies. （读后续写·童年阅读·环境+比喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: long after lights-out 时间状语营造画面 + flicker/beneath his blanket 细节动作 + 隐喻(secret universe/boundless galaxies) + trading...for 对比结构收尾显向往

sentenceUpgrade.original: Fiction is useful because it teaches us about life.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The true value of fiction lies not in the escape it offers but in the empathy it cultivates, for by walking a thousand imaginary miles in another's shoes, we return to our own lives a little wiser and a great deal kinder. （议论文·文学价值）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: not in...but in... 对比结构立论 + by doing 方式状语 + walk a thousand miles in another's shoes 化用习语 + a little/a great deal 程度递进收尾

translation: 科幻电影（或小说等）（非正式简称 sci-fi；缩写 SF）
original_sentence: Science fiction (informal sci‑fi; abbr: SF) 科幻电影（或小说等）
readingExamples: Science fiction (informal sci‑fi; abbr: SF) 科幻电影（或小说等）
definitionEn:
(1) n. a genre of imaginative literature or film based on real or imagined scientific and technological advances, often set in the future or in space
(2) n. works belonging to this genre collectively (novels, films, comics, etc.)
(3) n. (informal, abbreviated as sci-fi / SF) stories dealing with aliens, time travel, robots and other speculative ideas

posExamples.sentence: As the spaceship on screen tore through a shower of asteroids, ten-year-old Tom clutched his popcorn, utterly convinced that science fiction was not fantasy but a promise of the world he would one day help to build. （读后续写·科技梦想·观影瞬间）
Our film club will host a science fiction week next month, and we warmly welcome all students who are fascinated by robots, distant planets and the boundless what-ifs of tomorrow. （应用文·社团通知）

Good science fiction does more than entertain; by imagining tomorrow's technology, it quietly warns us of the choices we must make today, from artificial intelligence to the fragile balance of our planet. （议论文·科幻的现实意义）
What once existed only in science fiction — video calls, self-driving cars, pocket-sized computers — has, within a single generation, become the unremarkable furniture of our daily lives. （议论文·科技进步）

wordForms.other: sci-fi（非正式简称）; SF（缩写）; science-fiction writer（科幻作家）

collocations.phrase: a science fiction novel / film / writer
collocations.translation: 科幻小说 / 电影 / 作家
collocations.example: The science fiction film swept the audience off to a drowned city of the future, where a single child's courage rekindled hope for all humankind. （读后续写/影评·科幻震撼）

collocations.translation: 阅读 / 创作 / 观看科幻作品
collocations.example: Ever since he watched his first space adventure, Leo had dreamed of writing science fiction that would send other children reaching for the stars. （读后续写·梦想萌芽）
For newcomers to the genre, I would suggest starting with classic science fiction, whose bold ideas still feel astonishingly fresh decades later. （应用文·推荐信）

collocations.phrase: a fan of science fiction / a science fiction fan
collocations.example: As a lifelong fan of science fiction, I could hardly believe my luck when the famous author agreed to speak at our school festival. （应用文·活动预告）

collocations.phrase: the world / genre of science fiction
collocations.example: The genre of science fiction is a laboratory of the imagination, where writers test ideas that reality has not yet dared to try. （议论文·文学与科技）

collocations.phrase: sound like / belong to science fiction
collocations.translation: 听起来像科幻；属于科幻范畴
collocations.example: A hundred years ago, a machine that could translate a hundred languages in a heartbeat would have sounded like pure science fiction; today it sits in every schoolbag. （议论文·科技变迁）

synonyms.example: The young reader devoured every fantasy she could find, entranced by dragons, ancient spells and kingdoms that never were. （读后续写·阅读热爱）
synonyms.usage: fantasy 建立在魔法、神话等超自然设定上，不追求科学解释；science fiction 则以（真实或想象的）科学技术为根基，二者常被并提但分属不同类型

synonyms.example: Modern speculative fiction often asks the unsettling question: if we could do this, should we? （议论文·科技伦理）
synonyms.usage: speculative fiction 是更宽泛的上位概念，涵盖科幻、奇幻、反乌托邦等一切'设想非现实世界'的作品；science fiction 是其中以科技为核心的子类

synonyms.example: 'Another sci-fi movie?' his sister groaned, but twenty minutes in she was leaning forward, as spellbound as everyone else. （读后续写·家庭观影）
synonyms.usage: sci-fi 是 science fiction 的口语化简称，语气随意，多用于日常对话；正式写作、书评、书信中仍应使用完整的 science fiction

advancedExpressions.expression: what had once been only science fiction now ...
advancedExpressions.example: What had once been only science fiction to a boy with a torch and a comic book now stood before him, real and gleaming, as the rocket he had helped design rose slowly into the dawn sky. （what从句今昔对照+具象收尾，圆梦时刻升华）

advancedExpressions.expression: whether you are a devoted fan of science fiction or simply curious about ..., ...
advancedExpressions.example: Whether you are a devoted fan of science fiction or simply curious about the future, our film festival promises an evening you will not soon forget. （whether...or 让步涵盖两类受众，倡议/邀请开篇拉近距离）

advancedExpressions.expression: science fiction is not an escape from reality but a rehearsal for it
advancedExpressions.example: Science fiction is not an escape from reality but a rehearsal for it, for the dreams writers dare to imagine today often become the tools engineers dare to build tomorrow. （not...but 对比立论+today/tomorrow 时间呼应，为科幻正名）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He loved science fiction and wanted to be a scientist.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Every science fiction story he devoured was less an escape than a blueprint, and somewhere between the star maps and the daring inventions, the quiet resolve to become a scientist took root in his heart. （读后续写·梦想生根·比喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: less...than... 修正比较 + 隐喻(blueprint/take root) + between...and... 意象铺陈 + 抽象决心具象化(quiet resolve...took root)

sentenceUpgrade.original: Science fiction can make us think about the future.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: At its finest, science fiction is a telescope pointed not at the stars but at ourselves, urging us to weigh the consequences of our inventions before, rather than after, they reshape the world. （议论文·科幻的警示价值）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: at its finest 让步限定 + 隐喻(a telescope pointed at ourselves) + not...but... 转折深化 + before rather than after 时间对比强化论点

original_sentence: Actually, the film you see on the screen is the product of a huge amount of hard work, most of which takes place behind the scenes.
readingExamples: Actually, the film you see on the screen is the product of a huge amount of hard work, most of which takes place behind the scenes.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. happening or working in private, out of public view, especially in a way that influences a result
(2) phr. in the part of a theatre, film or television production that the audience does not see; backstage
(3) phr. (of people) doing important work quietly without receiving public recognition

posExamples.sentence: While the actors soaked up the thunderous applause, no one thought of the tired hands behind the scenes — the seamstress, the lighting boy, the prompter — whose quiet labour had made every dazzling moment possible. （读后续写·幕后英雄·对比烘托）
On behalf of the organising committee, I would like to thank everyone who worked tirelessly behind the scenes to make our school's charity concert such a resounding success. （应用文·感谢信/致辞）
Every polished performance we admire rests on countless hours of unseen effort behind the scenes; success, in truth, is merely the visible tip of a very deep iceberg. （议论文·努力与成功）
Curtains still drawn, the theatre buzzed behind the scenes: actors mouthing their lines, a director pacing, and a nervous stagehand triple-checking every rope and pulley. （读后续写·开演前·群像描写）

collocations.example: For thirty years the old caretaker had worked quietly behind the scenes, and the school he loved never once thought to ask his name. （读后续写·平凡坚守·感人）
Few of us ever pause to wonder what goes on behind the scenes to bring fresh vegetables from a distant farm to our breakfast table. （议论文·社会分工/感恩）
Actually, the film you see on the screen is the product of a huge amount of hard work, most of which takes place behind the scenes. （读后续写/说明文·课文原句）

collocations.translation: 对幕后的一瞥；幕后探秘
collocations.example: The documentary offers a fascinating behind-the-scenes look at how a single animated frame can swallow an entire day of an artist's life. （应用文·纪录片推荐）

collocations.phrase: the heroes / people behind the scenes
collocations.translation: 幕后英雄 / 幕后的人
collocations.example: When we celebrate the athletes on the podium, let us not forget the coaches, doctors and parents behind the scenes who carried them there. （议论文·团队与荣誉）

collocations.phrase: operate / pull the strings behind the scenes
collocations.example: Though he never once appeared on stage, everyone in the club knew it was he who pulled the strings behind the scenes, steering the whole production with a calm, invisible hand. （读后续写·低调掌舵者）
The behind-the-scenes footage revealed how many retakes and stumbles lay hidden beneath one flawless three-minute dance. （应用文·活动纪实）

synonyms.example: Backstage, her heart hammered against her ribs, but the instant she stepped into the light, a strange calm washed over her. （读后续写·登台前紧张）
synonyms.usage: backstage 侧重剧院/演出的具体'后台'空间；behind the scenes 更抽象，可泛指任何'公众看不到的幕后运作或工作'，适用范围更广

synonyms.example: The final decision, reached behind closed doors, took the whole school by surprise the next morning. （议论文/记叙·秘密决策）
synonyms.usage: behind closed doors 强调'不公开、保密'，常含隐秘甚至暗箱意味；behind the scenes 中性偏褒，多指默默付出的幕后工作，不必然带保密色彩

synonyms.example: She preferred to stay in the background, letting her teammates shine while she quietly held everything together. （读后续写·低调品格）
synonyms.usage: in the background 强调'不显眼、不引人注目的位置'；behind the scenes 更强调'公众视线之外的实际运作或付出'，二者语气相近但侧重不同

advancedExpressions.type: 读后续写·幕后英雄升华
advancedExpressions.expression: the applause belonged to ..., but the victory belonged to those behind the scenes
advancedExpressions.example: The applause belonged to the dancers, but the victory belonged to those behind the scenes — the ones who had swept the floor, mended the costumes and waited in the dark for a bow that would never be theirs. （对比句式+破折号列举，为无名者立传）

advancedExpressions.expression: our heartfelt thanks go to all who laboured behind the scenes
advancedExpressions.example: Our heartfelt thanks go to all who laboured behind the scenes, for without their quiet dedication, tonight's brilliance would simply not exist. （thanks go to 致谢句式+without 虚拟暗示，感谢信/致辞点睛）

advancedExpressions.expression: what we see is only the surface; the real work happens behind the scenes
advancedExpressions.example: What the world applauds is only the surface; the real work always happens behind the scenes, in the unglamorous hours of practice that no camera ever records. （surface/behind the scenes 表里对照+具象收尾，论证成功的隐性代价）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Many people worked behind the scenes to make the show successful.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: For every performer bathed in the spotlight, a dozen unseen hands had toiled behind the scenes — stitching, hammering, rehearsing in the dark — so that when the curtain finally rose, not a single detail was left to chance. （读后续写·幕后付出·排比+细节）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: for every...a dozen... 数量对比 + 破折号内三个-ing排比(stitching, hammering, rehearsing) + so that 结果从句 + not...to chance 收尾强调周全

sentenceUpgrade.original: Success needs a lot of hard work that people cannot see.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Behind every effortless triumph lies a mountain of invisible effort; what dazzles the crowd for a moment is built, quietly and painstakingly, behind the scenes over months and years. （议论文·成功的代价）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: behind...lies 倒装开篇 + a mountain of 夸张量化 + what从句主语 + quietly and painstakingly 副词强化 + over months and years 时间跨度收尾

original_sentence: Actually, the film you see on the screen is the product of a huge amount of hard work, most of which takes place behind the scenes.
readingExamples: Actually, the film you see on the screen is the product of a huge amount of hard work, most of which takes place behind the scenes.
definitionEn:
(1) adv. used to emphasize that something is true or real, especially when it is surprising or contrary to expectation; in fact
(2) adv. used to correct or contradict what someone has said, often politely
(3) adv. used when telling someone something they may not know, or to introduce a new point
(4) adv. used to refer to what really happened, as opposed to what was thought or claimed

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （表委婉纠正）其实，说实话（用于礼貌地反驳或纠正对方）
uncommonMeanings.example: 'You must be exhausted after the whole journey,' she said kindly. 'Actually, I feel more alive than I have in years,' the old man replied, his eyes shining. （读后续写·礼貌纠正·对话描写）

posExamples.sentence: Everyone had written him off as the clumsy new boy, but when the fire alarm shrieked, it was he who actually kept his head, guiding two frightened juniors calmly down the smoke-filled stairs. （读后续写·反转刻画·平凡英雄）
Actually, the film you see on the screen is the product of a huge amount of hard work, most of which takes place behind the scenes. （说明文/应用文·课文原句）
Many people assume that reading more books automatically makes one wiser; actually, it is reflection, not accumulation, that turns pages into wisdom. （议论文·观点纠偏）

I had always pictured my new roommate as cold and distant, but she actually turned out to be the warmest person I had ever met, sharing her snacks and her secrets from the very first night. （读后续写·印象反转·友情）

collocations.translation: 其实，……（句首委婉引出实情或转折）
collocations.example: 'I suppose you've given up on painting,' Dad said. 'Actually,' I answered, sliding my sketchbook across the table, 'I've never worked harder at anything.' （读后续写·亮出真相·对话）
Rumours swirled through the corridor all morning, yet only three people knew what had actually happened in the deserted lab the night before. （读后续写·悬疑铺垫）
Volunteering did not just fill my weekends; it actually reshaped the way I saw the world and my small place within it. （议论文·志愿服务感悟）

collocations.translation: 真正的意思是 / 确实认为
collocations.example: When she said she was 'fine', anyone who knew her could tell she actually meant the very opposite. （读后续写·言外之意·心理刻画）

collocations.phrase: if you think about it, actually ...
collocations.example: If you think about it, the classmate we envy for her effortless grades is actually the one who quietly studies longest after everyone has gone home. （议论文·努力被忽视）

collocations.phrase: actually, that's not quite right / true
collocations.translation: 其实那不太对（礼貌纠正）
collocations.example: 'So the pyramids were built by aliens?' the child asked. 'Actually, that's not quite right,' the guide smiled, kneeling to his level, 'they were built by thousands of very human hands.' （读后续写·师者耐心·对话）

synonyms.example: The task looked impossible at first; in fact, once we broke it into small steps, it proved surprisingly manageable. （议论文/记叙·实情揭示）
synonyms.usage: in fact 更书面正式，常用于议论文强调真实情况或递进补充；actually 口语色彩更浓，尤其擅长引出'出人意料'或'委婉纠正'的语气

synonyms.example: I never really understood the meaning of home until I stood, suitcase in hand, at a foreign airport far from everyone I loved. （读后续写·思乡顿悟）
synonyms.usage: really 侧重'真实、确实'的强调，可加强程度；actually 侧重'与预期相反的真实情况'，二者有时可换，但 actually 更含'纠正/意外'的意味

synonyms.translation: 事实上（引出新信息或强调）
synonyms.example: 'I hear you've never left this small town.' 'As a matter of fact, I once spent a whole summer in Paris,' she said, a mischievous smile tugging at her lips. （读后续写·意外揭底·对话）
synonyms.usage: as a matter of fact 较正式且带'其实还有你不知道的'意味，常引出新信息；actually 更简短随和，日常对话与书面皆宜

advancedExpressions.expression: what everyone had assumed ... was, actually, quite the opposite
advancedExpressions.example: What everyone had assumed to be arrogance was, actually, quite the opposite — a painful shyness the boy had spent years hiding behind a cold, unsmiling mask. （actually插入语制造反转+破折号补释，人物形象逆转）

advancedExpressions.expression: I should point out that, actually, ...
advancedExpressions.example: I should point out that, actually, the event has been rescheduled to Saturday afternoon, so I sincerely hope this note reaches everyone in good time. （礼貌澄清句式，通知/说明中纠正误解）

advancedExpressions.expression: contrary to popular belief, ... is actually ...
advancedExpressions.example: Contrary to popular belief, failure is actually not the opposite of success but a necessary chapter of it, for no lasting achievement was ever written without a few painful drafts. （contrary to+actually 双重纠偏+比喻收尾，颠覆常识的论证）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The film looks easy to make, but it is actually very hard.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: What looks, on screen, like two effortless hours of magic is actually the fruit of years of painstaking labour — a thousand invisible decisions distilled into a single seamless illusion. （议论文/说明文·揭示真相）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: what looks like...is actually 表里对比 + 破折号同位语补释 + a thousand...distilled into a single 数量对照升华 + seamless illusion 收尾呼应

sentenceUpgrade.original: I thought he was unfriendly, but actually he was kind.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The boy I had dismissed as cold and unfriendly turned out, actually, to be the gentlest soul in the class — the first to lend a pen, the last to laugh at another's stumble. （读后续写·印象反转·细节佐证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: dismissed as 前置贬评 + turned out actually to be 反转 + 破折号内对称细节(the first...the last...)具象化善良，避免空泛的 kind

translation: 简洁的，简单的；短时间的
original_sentence: Today, I'll give you a brief introduction to some aspects of film‑making you might not be familiar with.
readingExamples: Today, I'll give you a brief introduction to some aspects of film‑making you might not be familiar with.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. lasting only a short time; short in duration
(2) adj. using few words; concise
(3) adj. (of clothing) short and not covering much of the body
(4) n. a set of instructions or a summary of facts explaining a task, case or situation
(5) vt. to give someone detailed instructions or essential information in advance

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 任务简介；（律师的）案情摘要，诉讼要点
uncommonMeanings.example: The young lawyer stayed up all night poring over the brief, determined to find the single overlooked detail that might set an innocent man free. （读后续写·法庭·执着钻研）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 向……作简要介绍；面授机宜
uncommonMeanings.example: Before we set off into the mountains, the guide briefed us on every hidden danger, his voice calm but his eyes deadly serious. （读后续写·探险前·紧张铺垫）

posExamples.sentence: Their reunion was painfully brief — a hurried hug on a crowded platform — yet in those ten seconds a whole year of longing seemed to pour silently from one heart into another. （读后续写·离别重逢·情感浓缩）
Today, I'll give you a brief introduction to some aspects of film-making you might not be familiar with. （说明文/应用文·课文原句）
Since your time is precious, I will keep this proposal brief and focus only on the two changes that would most benefit our reading club. （应用文·建议信开篇）
However brief a kind word may be, its warmth can linger in a stranger's memory for a lifetime, proving that the smallest gestures often cast the longest shadows. （议论文·善意的力量）

idioms.example: In brief, the trip taught me that a map may show the way, but only courage can carry you along it. （读后续写/议论文·总结点题）
To be brief, I am writing to apply for the position of volunteer guide at the coming science exhibition. （应用文·申请信开门见山）

idioms.idiom: brevity is the soul of wit
idioms.translation: 言以简洁为贵（简洁是智慧的灵魂）
idioms.example: Remembering that brevity is the soul of wit, the champion debater made her point in a single unforgettable sentence and sat down to thunderous applause. （议论文·表达艺术·名言化用）

collocations.example: Allow me to begin with a brief introduction to our club before I invite the new members to share their own stories. （应用文·致辞开场）

collocations.translation: 短暂的一刻 / 停顿 / 沉默
collocations.example: There was a brief silence after her question, and in that fragile pause the whole classroom seemed to hold its breath. （读后续写·紧张氛围·细节）

collocations.phrase: keep it brief / make it brief
collocations.example: 'I'll keep it brief,' the coach said, though every player knew that his few blunt words would echo in their minds all through the final match. （读后续写·赛前动员）
During her brief stay in the village, the volunteer teacher planted a love of English in a dozen young hearts that would outlast a lifetime. （读后续写·支教·深远影响）
For a brief period after the storm, the whole valley fell utterly still, as if the world were catching its breath before beginning anew. （读后续写·雨后·环境描写）
Our exchange with the foreign students was brief but unforgettable, leaving each of us richer in friendship and wider in horizon. （应用文·活动感想）
To put it briefly, the secret of his success was neither talent nor luck, but a stubborn refusal to give up. （议论文·总结论点）

collocations.translation: 就某事向某人作简要介绍
collocations.example: The captain gathered the team and briefed them on the rescue plan, each word landing with the weight of a life at stake. （读后续写·救援部署）

synonyms.example: Her concise reply — just three well-chosen words — said more than a whole paragraph of empty praise ever could. （读后续写/议论文·言简意赅）
synonyms.usage: concise 特指'用词精练、无冗余'，评价的是表达方式；brief 兼指'时间短'与'篇幅短'，范围更广，可修饰访问、停顿等非语言事物

synonyms.example: It was only a short walk to school, yet along that familiar path she rehearsed a thousand versions of the apology she owed her friend. （读后续写·内心活动）
synonyms.usage: short 是最普通的'短'，可指长度、时间、身高等；brief 更正式，几乎只用于时间或言辞的'短暂/简短'，不用于形容物体或身高

synonyms.example: A momentary lapse of attention was all it took for the vase to slip from her fingers and shatter across the marble floor. （读后续写·意外瞬间）
synonyms.usage: momentary 强调'仅持续一瞬、转瞬即逝'，程度比 brief 更短；brief 指'短暂但仍有一段可感的时长'，如 a brief meeting 可持续数分钟

advancedExpressions.expression: brief as it was, the moment ... would ...
advancedExpressions.example: Brief as it was, that single glance of forgiveness would warm her through every cold and lonely night in the years that followed. （brief as it was 让步倒装+夸张时间跨度，把短暂瞬间的意义无限放大）

advancedExpressions.expression: I shall be brief, for ...
advancedExpressions.example: I shall be brief, for I know how busy your schedule is; my request concerns one small but meaningful change to the library rules. （I shall be brief 礼貌简洁承诺，正式书信开篇显体贴）

advancedExpressions.expression: in brief, ... — nothing more, nothing less
advancedExpressions.example: In brief, true education is the art of teaching a mind to think for itself — nothing more, nothing less. （in brief 收束+破折号 nothing more, nothing less 斩钉截铁定义，结尾有力）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Their meeting was very short.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Their meeting was heartbreakingly brief — a snatched embrace beneath the departure board — before the crowd swept them apart and the train swallowed him whole. （读后续写·车站离别·细节+比喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: heartbreakingly 副词渲染情感 + 破折号内动作特写(snatched embrace) + before 时间从句制造紧迫 + swallowed him whole 拟人收尾

sentenceUpgrade.original: I will give you a brief introduction to our plan.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Allow me to offer only a brief outline of our plan here, so that we may save our precious minutes for the questions and ideas that truly matter. （应用文·会议/演讲开场）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: allow me to 谦辞句式 + only a brief outline 限定谦逊 + so that 目的状语 + that truly matter 定语从句收尾显重点意识

original_sentence: Today, I'll give you a brief introduction to some aspects of film‑making you might not be familiar with.
readingExamples: Today, I'll give you a brief introduction to some aspects of film‑making you might not be familiar with.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. well known to you; easily recognized because you have seen or experienced it before
(2) adj. (familiar with sth) having a good knowledge of something; well acquainted with
(3) adj. friendly and informal, sometimes in a way that is too relaxed or over-friendly
(4) adj. commonly seen or encountered; ordinary and everyday

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （贬）过分随便的，套近乎的；放肆的
uncommonMeanings.example: His tone grew a little too familiar for a first meeting, and she took an instinctive step back, uneasy at how quickly he had dropped every formality. （读后续写·社交警觉·分寸感）

posExamples.sentence: The moment she pushed open the creaking gate, a familiar smell of jasmine and old wood rushed to meet her, and twenty years of memories came flooding back in a single, dizzying wave. （读后续写·故地重游·嗅觉记忆）
Today, I'll give you a brief introduction to some aspects of film-making you might not be familiar with. （说明文/应用文·课文原句）
To help our exchange guests feel at home, we have prepared a handbook of familiar Chinese customs, so that no gesture of kindness will be lost in translation. （应用文·活动方案）

idioms.translation: 亲近生狎侮；越熟悉越易轻慢

collocations.translation: 为某人所熟悉（主语是事物）
collocations.example: The old lullaby was so familiar to her that, though she had not heard it in decades, every note found its way home to her heart. （读后续写·记忆唤醒·主语区分）

collocations.translation: 熟悉的面孔 / 声音 / 景象
collocations.example: Lost and frightened in the vast foreign airport, she suddenly caught sight of a familiar face in the crowd, and relief broke over her like a warm tide. （读后续写·异乡遇故人）

collocations.translation: 看起来 / 听起来 / 似乎眼熟
collocations.example: The handwriting on the anonymous note looked oddly familiar, and a cold suspicion began to take shape in the back of his mind. （读后续写·悬疑推进）
Before the debate, we spent a week familiarizing ourselves with every argument the other side might possibly raise. （应用文/议论文·充分准备）
Within a single term the new teacher was on familiar terms with every student, greeting each by name and, more remarkably, by dream. （读后续写·亲和力·师生情）

As the volunteers grew familiar with the villagers' habits and hardships, mere sympathy slowly deepened into genuine, lasting friendship. （议论文/记叙·志愿服务）

synonyms.translation: 熟悉的，了解的（be acquainted with）

synonyms.usage: acquainted 较正式，几乎只用于 be acquainted with 结构，表'对某人/某事有所了解'；familiar 更常用、语气更自然，且可作 a familiar face 这类定语，acquainted 不能

synonyms.example: It is a well-known fact that regular exercise sharpens not only the body but also the focus of the mind. （议论文·健康主题）
synonyms.usage: well-known 强调'广为人知、有名气'，评价知名度；familiar 强调'因见过而熟悉、亲切'，主观色彩更强，如 a familiar face 熟脸不等于 a well-known face 名人脸

synonyms.example: Kindness may be common, yet it is precisely its quiet, everyday presence that keeps the fabric of society from tearing apart. （议论文·平凡的善）
synonyms.usage: common 侧重'普遍存在、不稀奇'，客观描述频率；familiar 侧重'因熟悉而亲切或易辨认'，带认知与情感色彩，二者有时可换但重心不同

advancedExpressions.type: 读后续写·环境唤醒记忆

advancedExpressions.expression: growth begins where the familiar ends
advancedExpressions.example: Growth begins precisely where the familiar ends, for it is only by stepping beyond the comfort of the known that we ever discover what we are truly capable of. （growth begins where...ends 警句式+it is only by 强调，走出舒适区的有力论证）

sentenceUpgrade.original: When she got home, everything looked familiar.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The moment she stepped through the door, every familiar corner reached out to greet her — the chipped teapot, the sun-faded curtains, the clock that had always run five minutes slow — and something long knotted in her chest quietly came undone. （读后续写·归家·细节+情感释放）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: the moment 时间从句 + 拟人(reached out to greet her) + 破折号内三项具体旧物排比 + something...came undone 内心具象化收尾

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should not always stay in a familiar environment.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Clinging forever to familiar surroundings may feel safe, but it is a costly kind of safety, for the mind, like a muscle, weakens in comfort and strengthens only against the resistance of the new. （议论文·舒适区反思·比喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: clinging to 动名词主语 + a costly kind of safety 矛盾修辞 + like a muscle 明喻 + weakens/strengthens 对比 + against the resistance of the new 收尾深化

original_sentence: To begin with, I'd like to draw your attention to an important factor of a film – sound effects.
readingExamples: To begin with, I'd like to draw your attention to an important factor of a film – sound effects.
definitionEn:
(1) n. one of several things that influence or cause a situation or result
(2) n. maths: a number that divides exactly into a larger number
(3) n. a level of protection provided by a substance (e.g. a factor 30 sunscreen)
(4) vt. (usu. factor sth in / into) to include a particular thing when making a calculation or decision

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （数学）因数，因子
uncommonMeanings.example: "The factors of twelve are one, two, three, four, six and twelve," the boy explained, his chalk squeaking across the board as the whole class fell silent in reluctant admiration. （读后续写·课堂·后进生逆袭）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （把某因素）计入，考虑进去
uncommonMeanings.example: When you factor in the hidden costs of travel and accommodation, the seemingly cheap tour turns out to be no bargain at all. （议论文·理性消费）

posExamples.sentence: Looking back, she realised that her grandmother's quiet encouragement had been the decisive factor that kept her going through those long, sleepless nights before the exam. （读后续写·亲情·回忆）
I am writing to suggest that we take the weather into account, since it is a factor that could easily ruin our outdoor charity sale if we fail to prepare a backup plan. （应用文·建议信）
Among the many factors that shape a person's success, perseverance arguably outweighs talent, for raw ability without sustained effort seldom bears fruit. （议论文·成功要素）
Before you dismiss volunteering as a waste of time, you must factor in the invaluable skills and lifelong friendships it quietly brings. （议论文·反驳）

collocations.example: Motivation, rather than intelligence, proved to be the crucial factor in her remarkable transformation from a shy dropout to a confident leader. （读后续写·成长）
Lack of sleep is a major contributing factor to the rising number of teenage traffic accidents. （应用文·倡议书）
For many families, cost remains the determining factor when choosing between public and private schools. （议论文·教育）
Peer pressure is a significant factor in shaping the choices young people make every day. （议论文·青少年）

collocations.phrase: take a factor into account / consideration
collocations.example: When planning the trip, we must take the safety factor into account and avoid the mountain roads after dark. （应用文·活动方案）
No matter how advanced the technology becomes, the human factor still determines whether a machine is used for good or ill. （议论文·科技与人）
The report attributes the decline of the small town to a combination of economic and social factors. （应用文·调查报告）
In the end, it was her sincere smile, not her polished résumé, that became the deciding factor in the interview. （读后续写·面试）

synonyms.example: Trust is the essential element without which no lasting friendship can be built. （议论文·人际关系）
synonyms.usage: 侧重构成整体的"组成部分"，中性；factor 更强调对结果的"影响/作用力"。

synonyms.example: Carelessness was the direct cause of the fire that swept through the old warehouse. （读后续写·事故）
synonyms.usage: 指直接引发某事的"原因"；factor 只是众多影响之一，未必是唯一直接起因。

synonyms.example: Passion is the secret ingredient that turns ordinary effort into extraordinary achievement. （议论文·励志）
synonyms.usage: 多为比喻用法，指"必不可少的要素"，偏形象；factor 更学术、中性。

advancedExpressions.expression: it was ... that proved to be the single most important factor
advancedExpressions.example: It was not her talent but her refusal to give up that proved to be the single most important factor in her ultimate triumph. （强调句 + 对比 not...but，突出真正的决胜因素）

advancedExpressions.expression: we should factor in ... before ...
advancedExpressions.example: We should factor in every possible risk before we finalise the schedule, so that the event runs smoothly from start to finish. （before 时间状语从句 + so that 目的状语，逻辑严密）

advancedExpressions.expression: a host of factors, chief among which is ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: Her family support was important to her success.

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Looking back 现在分词状语引出回忆 + the one factor that... 强调唯一决定因素 + tip the scales 隐喻 + long after 时间状语拉长情感

sentenceUpgrade.original: We must consider many factors when we make the plan.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: In drawing up the plan, we are obliged to weigh a multitude of factors, ranging from budget and safety to weather, so that nothing is left to chance. （应用文·正式建议）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: In drawing up... 介词+动名词状语 + be obliged to 正式表"必须" + ranging from...to 列举 + so that 目的状语

original_sentence: For example, in Jurassic Park, the sounds of different animals, including a baby elephant and a tiger, were mixed by a computer to make a dinosaur roar.

(2) n. (informal, disapproving) a person or thing that is old-fashioned and unwilling or unable to change with the times

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （贬）守旧过时的人／事物；老古董

I am writing to recommend the newly opened Natural History Museum, where lifelike dinosaur models and interactive screens bring the prehistoric world vividly back to life. （应用文·推荐信）

collocations.example: Kneeling beside the giant dinosaur fossil, the professor traced each bone as reverently as if it were a page from Earth's forgotten diary. （读后续写·科考）

For a brief, magical hour in the planetarium, the children were transported back to the age of the dinosaurs. （读后续写·想象）

The farmer had no idea that the strange stones in his field were in fact priceless dinosaur remains. （读后续写·意外发现）

synonyms.example: Unlike most modern reptiles, some dinosaurs may have been warm-blooded, recent studies suggest. （议论文·科普）

advancedExpressions.expression: as ... as if it had stepped straight out of ...

advancedExpressions.expression: the fate of the dinosaurs serves as a stark reminder that ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: The boy saw a big dinosaur model and was scared.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As the boy rounded the corner, a colossal dinosaur reared up before him, jaws gaping and eyes aglow; his heart lurched into his throat and, for one frozen instant, he forgot how to breathe. （读后续写·惊吓+动作）

original_sentence: For example, in Jurassic Park, the sounds of different animals, including a baby elephant and a tiger, were mixed by a computer to make a dinosaur roar.

definitionEn:

(2) vi. (roar with laughter) to laugh very loudly

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （车辆等）呼啸疾驰而过

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 放声大笑（roar with laughter）

posExamples.sentence: The wounded lion roared in agony, its cry echoing across the empty savannah until even the bravest hunters felt a chill crawl down their spines. （读后续写·非洲·惊险）

collocations.phrase: the roar of the engine / traffic

synonyms.example: The dog gave a low growl, warning the stranger not to come any closer. （读后续写·紧张）

synonyms.example: "Get out of the water at once!" the coach bellowed from the shore. （读后续写·呵斥）

synonyms.usage: thunder 强调声音如雷、极具威慑力，常带命令语气；roar 更侧重持续而洪亮的声响。
