(1) vt. to make it possible for someone to do something, or for something to happen
(2) vt. to make something possible or easier by providing the means or opportunity
(3) vt. (of technology) to make a device or system able to work or function

posExamples.sentence: A single word of encouragement from his teacher enabled the timid boy to raise his trembling hand at last, and in that instant something inside him quietly shifted forever. （读后续写·鼓励的力量·转变）
The scholarship will enable dozens of gifted but underprivileged students to pursue the university dreams that once seemed hopelessly out of reach. （应用文·倡议书）
Far from replacing human effort, technology at its best simply enables us to do more with the time and talent we already possess. （议论文·科技与人）
The rope, worn but faithful, enabled the exhausted climbers to inch their way up the icy cliff, hand over trembling hand, towards the light above. （读后续写·登山·脱险）

collocations.example: Years of quiet practice enabled her to play the entire sonata without a single glance at the score. （读后续写·苦练）

collocations.phrase: enable sth. to happen / be done
collocations.example: This new bridge will enable goods to be transported across the valley in half the time. （应用文·说明）
Modern technology enables students in remote villages to attend lessons taught by the finest teachers in the country. （议论文·教育公平）
The free library card enables access to thousands of books that would otherwise stay locked behind a price tag. （应用文·倡议）
A supportive environment enables genuine growth, allowing young talents to blossom without fear of failure. （议论文·成长环境）
A few shared words of a common language enabled communication between the two lost travellers. （读后续写·陌生人）
The generous donation financially enabled the school to rebuild its crumbling laboratory. （应用文·报道）

synonyms.example: The extra hour allowed her to finish the painting she had almost given up on. （读后续写·完成）
synonyms.usage: 既可指‘准许’也可指‘使有条件’，语气较弱；enable 更强调‘赋予能力/提供手段’，正式且积极

synonyms.translation: 赋予（能力/权力），增强信心
synonyms.example: Learning to code empowered the shy girl to build the app she had only dared to dream about. （读后续写·自我实现）
synonyms.usage: 强调赋予力量、增强自主性与信心，情感色彩更强；enable 更中性，侧重‘提供条件’

synonyms.example: Clear signposts facilitated the flow of visitors through the crowded exhibition. （应用文·活动组织）
synonyms.usage: 书面正式，强调‘使过程更顺畅/更容易’，常搭配抽象过程；enable 强调‘从不可能变为可能’

advancedExpressions.expression: it was ... that enabled sb. to ...
advancedExpressions.example: It was not talent but sheer perseverance that enabled him to stand, at last, upon the winner's podium. （强调句 + 对比(not...but) 突出真正的关键，续写点题）

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., which will enable us to ...
advancedExpressions.example: I propose setting up a book-sharing corner, which will enable every student to read widely at no cost at all. （非限定定语从句说明方案意义）

advancedExpressions.expression: rather than ..., ... enables us to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Rather than diminishing our abilities, well-used technology enables us to reach heights our ancestors could scarcely imagine.

sentenceUpgrade.original: His teacher's help made him able to succeed.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It was his teacher's unwavering faith, more than any lesson taught, that enabled him to rise from a stammering outsider into the confident young man now addressing the whole school. （读后续写·师恩·蜕变）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 强调句(It was...that) + 插入语(more than any lesson taught) + rise from...into 蜕变句式 + 现在分词收尾

sentenceUpgrade.original: The plan lets students read more books.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Once put into practice, this plan would enable every student, regardless of family background, to hold a world of books within arm's reach. （应用文·倡议书）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Once put into practice 过去分词状语 + regardless of... 插入强调普惠 + within arm's reach 形象化收尾

original_sentence: However, the aid of computers isn't always preferred.
readingExamples: However, the aid of computers isn't always preferred.
definitionEn:
(1) n. help or support given to someone who needs it
(2) n. money, food, or equipment given to a country or people in need (e.g. foreign aid, humanitarian aid)
(3) n. a person or thing that helps or is useful (e.g. a teaching aid, a hearing aid)
(4) vt. & vi. to help someone or something, especially to make a process easier or faster

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 辅助器具/工具（a hearing aid 助听器、a visual aid 视觉教具等）
uncommonMeanings.example: The old man fumbled with his hearing aid, and when the music suddenly rushed in, clear and warm, his eyes filled with the wonder of a child hearing the world for the very first time. （读后续写·重获·感动）

posExamples.sentence: With the aid of a flickering torch and a stranger's steady hand, the frightened girl found her way out of the collapsed tunnel and back into the trembling embrace of her mother. （读后续写·救援·团圆）
On behalf of our club, I am writing to appeal for your generous aid in supporting the children of the flood-stricken mountain village. （应用文·倡议信）
Regular reading not only enriches the mind but also aids clear thinking, for words are the very tools with which we shape our thoughts. （议论文·阅读的价值）
The villagers, armed with nothing but ropes and courage, rushed to aid the drowning boy against the roaring current. （读后续写·见义勇为）

wordForms.other: aide（助手，尤指政要/将领的副官）

idioms.translation: 前来帮助某人，出手相助
idioms.example: Just as she was about to give up, a group of passing hikers came to her aid, hauling her frozen body up the last stretch of the trail. （读后续写·危难相助）

idioms.translation: 为了帮助/支援（尤指慈善）
idioms.example: The whole school threw itself into a charity concert in aid of the earthquake victims. （应用文·活动报道）

collocations.example: With the aid of a magnifying glass, the boy uncovered a whole hidden universe in a single drop of pond water. （读后续写·好奇心）
Thanks to the first aid she had learned at school, she kept the injured cyclist calm until the ambulance arrived. （读后续写·急救·冷静）
Total strangers came to his aid without a moment's hesitation. （读后续写·人间温情）

collocations.translation: 经济援助/人道主义援助
collocations.example: The organisation delivered humanitarian aid to families who had lost everything in the storm. （应用文·报道）
A simple visual aid — a hand-drawn map — turned an abstract history lesson into a living adventure. （应用文·教学）
Their timely aid and support gave the struggling family the courage to start again. （读后续写·温情）
The mayor appealed for aid on national television as the floodwaters kept rising. （应用文·新闻）
We are holding a book sale in aid of the local children's hospital. （应用文·倡议）

synonyms.example: A kind nurse assisted the elderly patient down the long, echoing corridor. （读后续写·关怀）
synonyms.usage: 较正式的动词，强调‘从旁协助’完成某事；aid 作动词更强调使过程更快更易，也可作名词

synonyms.example: Should you require any assistance during the trip, our guides will be glad to help. （应用文·通知）
synonyms.usage: aid 的正式名词近义词；assistance 更书面，常用于服务/正式场合；aid 更常指救济、援助物资

synonyms.example: Her unwavering support carried him through the darkest days of self-doubt. （读后续写·陪伴）
synonyms.usage: 范围最广，可指物质、精神、道义上的支持；aid 更侧重实际的、及时的帮助

advancedExpressions.expression: just as ..., sb. came to one's aid
advancedExpressions.example: Just as hope was slipping through her fingers, a warm hand reached down through the smoke and came to her aid. （just as 引导关键时刻 + 感官细节，续写高潮反转）

advancedExpressions.expression: I sincerely appeal for your aid in ...
advancedExpressions.example: I sincerely appeal for your aid in giving these forgotten children the warm winter they so richly deserve. （倡议信结尾情感呼吁）
Human ingenuity, aided by relentless curiosity, has time and again turned the impossible into the everyday.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Some people helped her, so she got out.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Just as her strength was failing, a chain of unfamiliar hands came to her aid, passing her upward through the wreckage until, at last, she broke into the blinding, blessed daylight. （读后续写·脱险·群像温情）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: just as 关键时刻 + a chain of hands 群像意象 + 动作递进(passing...until) + broke into the daylight 象征希望

sentenceUpgrade.original: Please help us support the poor children.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: On behalf of every child still waiting in the cold, I earnestly appeal for your aid, for a single act of kindness from you may rewrite the whole course of a young life. （应用文·倡议信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: On behalf of... 代言弱势群体 + earnestly 情感副词 + for 引导原因 + rewrite the course of a life 升华收尾

original_sentence: However, the aid of computers isn't always preferred.
readingExamples: However, the aid of computers isn't always preferred.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to like one thing or person better than another; to choose one thing rather than another because you like it more
(2) vt. to want or wish that something should happen (prefer to do / prefer doing / prefer that ...)
(3) vt. (formal, law) to bring or make a formal accusation against someone (prefer a charge against sb.)

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （法律，正式）提出（控告）：prefer a charge against sb.
uncommonMeanings.example: After weeks of silent suffering, she finally found the courage to prefer a charge against the man who had wronged her, her voice steady for the first time in months. （读后续写·勇气·正义）

posExamples.sentence: While the other children clamoured for the newest toys, little Tom quietly preferred the battered old bicycle his grandfather had left him, for to him it carried a love that no shiny gadget ever could. （读后续写·亲情·懂事）
If it is convenient for you, I would prefer to hold the meeting on Friday afternoon, when most of our members are free from lessons. （应用文·电子邮件）
Many would prefer a life of comfort to one of struggle, yet it is often struggle, not comfort, that carves character out of raw human clay. （议论文·安逸与奋斗）
Exhausted as she was, she preferred to walk the last three miles home under the stars rather than accept a ride from the noisy, careless crowd. （读后续写·独立·选择）

collocations.translation: 喜欢 A 胜过 B
collocations.example: She had always preferred the quiet company of books to the noise of crowded parties. （读后续写·性格）
I would prefer to solve the problem myself before turning to anyone for help. （议论文·独立）

collocations.translation: 更喜欢做某事（泛指习惯）
collocations.example: He prefers writing his diary by hand, feeling that ink somehow captures emotion better than a screen. （读后续写·习惯）

collocations.phrase: prefer to do A rather than do B
collocations.translation: 宁愿做 A 而不愿做 B
collocations.example: She preferred to fail honestly rather than succeed by cheating. （议论文·诚信）

collocations.translation: 更希望某人（做）……（虚拟语气）
collocations.example: I would prefer that the ceremony be held outdoors, weather permitting. （应用文·安排）
Cycling to school soon became the preferred option for students who cared about the planet. （议论文·环保）
You may join either the morning or the evening session, as you prefer. （应用文·通知）

synonyms.example: The judges clearly favoured the bold, unconventional design over the safe one. （读后续写·比赛）
synonyms.usage: 强调对某方的偏袒或倾向，可用于观点、方案；prefer 更常表个人喜好上的取舍

synonyms.example: I would rather stand alone for what is right than sit comfortably with the crowd. （议论文·立场）
synonyms.usage: 口语化的‘宁愿’，后接动词原形，句式灵活；prefer 更正式，可接名词、to do、doing

synonyms.example: Faced with two safe paths, she opted for the uncertain one that made her heart race. （读后续写·抉择）
synonyms.usage: 强调在选项中做出主动选择的动作；prefer 强调基于喜好而更倾向于某一方

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. would always prefer ... to ...
advancedExpressions.example: He would always prefer the honest sting of truth to the sweet poison of a comforting lie. （prefer A to B + 对比意象(sting of truth / poison of a lie) 刻画人物风骨）

advancedExpressions.expression: if it is all the same to you, I would prefer to ...
advancedExpressions.example: If it is all the same to you, I would prefer to volunteer at the library, where I feel I can be of the greatest use. （委婉客气地表达偏好，书信礼貌用语）

advancedExpressions.expression: we should prefer ... over ..., for ...
advancedExpressions.example: We should prefer lasting growth over instant comfort, for the challenges we shy away from today are often the very ones that shape us tomorrow.

sentenceUpgrade.original: She liked staying home more than going out.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Given the choice, she would always prefer the gentle hush of home — a cup of tea, a well-worn book, the rain tapping at the glass — to the glittering emptiness of another crowded party. （读后续写·内向·诗意）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Given the choice 状语 + prefer A to B + 破折号三重意象铺陈 + glittering emptiness 反差修饰

sentenceUpgrade.original: I want to have the trip on Saturday.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: If it would not cause too much inconvenience, I would greatly prefer to schedule our trip for Saturday, when the weather promises to be far kinder. （应用文·礼貌协商）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 条件状语从句委婉铺垫 + would greatly prefer 礼貌情态 + when 引导定语从句补充理由 + promises to be 拟人化

translation: 创造性的，创作的；有创造力的
original_sentence: Peter Jackson, director of The Lord of the Rings films, took a creative approach – he used clever camera angles to make characters seem bigger or smaller than they really were.
readingExamples: Peter Jackson, director of The Lord of the Rings films, took a creative approach – he used clever camera angles to make characters seem bigger or smaller than they really were.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. producing or using original and unusual ideas; showing imagination
(2) adj. involving the making of things through skill, especially in art, writing, music, or design
(3) adj. able to invent and develop original ideas, especially in an artistic way

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 创意工作者（广告/设计行业口语，可数）
uncommonMeanings.example: Fresh out of art school, she was hired as a creative at a small agency, where her wild sketches soon set the whole office buzzing. （读后续写·职场起步·崭露头角）

posExamples.sentence: With a single stroke of chalk, the street artist turned a grey, cracked wall into a leaping tiger — a creative spark that stopped every hurrying passer-by in their tracks. （读后续写·街头艺术·惊艳瞬间）
We warmly invite all students to join our Creative Writing Club, where you can unleash your imagination, exchange original stories, and discover a voice that is uniquely your own. （应用文·社团招募）
A truly creative mind does not merely memorise the answers handed down by others; it dares to question, to reimagine, and to forge fresh paths where none existed before. （议论文·创新精神）
Rather than scolding her son for the crayon marks on the wall, my aunt took a creative approach, framing them and hanging them proudly in the hallway as his 'first exhibition'. （读后续写·亲情·包容）

collocations.translation: 有创意的方法／解决方案
collocations.example: Faced with a shortage of funds, the volunteers came up with a creative solution — turning recycled bottles into glowing lanterns for the night market. （读后续写·公益·巧思）
Schools that reward creative thinking, rather than rote memorisation, tend to nurture students who can adapt to a fast-changing world. （议论文·教育）
The open-ended project finally unlocked the creativity that years of standardised testing had kept firmly locked away. （议论文·教育反思）
When the props ran out backstage, we had to get creative, fashioning a crown out of gold paper and a coat hanger. （读后续写·校园戏剧·临场应变）
Her passion for creative writing was first kindled by a teacher who scribbled 'Never stop dreaming on paper' at the bottom of her essay. （读后续写·师恩·启蒙）
In recent years, the creative industries have flourished, offering young people countless opportunities to turn imagination into a livelihood. （应用文·调查报告）
In a sudden burst of creativity, he sketched the entire storyboard in one feverish night, hardly noticing the sunrise creeping through the curtains. （读后续写·艺术家·灵感涌现）
A relaxed classroom atmosphere, where mistakes are treated as stepping stones, does far more to foster creativity than constant criticism. （议论文·教育方法）

synonyms.example: Her imaginative retelling of the old legend gave the tired story a startlingly fresh and vivid life. （读后续写·叙事）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'想象力丰富'，强调头脑中构想画面的能力；creative 更侧重把想象付诸实际、产出新事物

synonyms.example: The company's innovative design won it worldwide acclaim almost overnight. （议论文·科技创新）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'引入新方法、打破旧模式'，常用于科技、商业、产品；creative 更宽泛，也用于艺术与日常巧思

synonyms.example: What impressed the judges most was not his technique but the utterly original concept behind the painting. （读后续写·比赛）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'非模仿、独一无二'，强调作品来源的新；creative 强调创作过程与才能

synonyms.example: The inventive child rigged up a pulley system to hoist snacks straight to his treehouse. （读后续写·童年·巧思）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'巧妙发明、解决实际问题'，带机巧色彩；creative 更侧重艺术与观念层面的原创

advancedExpressions.expression: in a flash of creative inspiration, sb. did ...

advancedExpressions.expression: let us dare to be creative and ...
advancedExpressions.example: Let us dare to be creative and reimagine our campus not as it is, but as it could be — greener, kinder and more alive with ideas. （倡议信呼吁，祈使句+对比升华）

advancedExpressions.expression: creativity is not a gift reserved for a chosen few, but ...
advancedExpressions.example: Creativity is not a gift reserved for a chosen few, but a muscle that grows stronger with every bold attempt and every celebrated failure. （否定前提+比喻定义，破除误区式论证）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He had a creative idea.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: An idea, wild and glittering, took shape in his mind — the kind of creative leap that could only come to someone reckless enough to ignore the rules everyone else obeyed. （读后续写·人物·灵感）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 后置形容词(wild and glittering)营造画面 + 破折号补充定义 + the kind of...that 定语从句刻画性格

sentenceUpgrade.original: Creative people are important for society.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is those daring enough to think creatively — to see a bridge where others see only a chasm — who ultimately push society forward, transforming the impossible of yesterday into the ordinary of tomorrow. （议论文·创新价值）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 强调句 It is...who + 插入语破折号形象说明(bridge/chasm) + 对比结构(impossible of yesterday/ordinary of tomorrow)

translation: n. 方法；接近，靠近 | vt. 接近，靠近；处理
original_sentence: Peter Jackson, director of The Lord of the Rings films, took a creative approach – he used clever camera angles to make characters seem bigger or smaller than they really were.
readingExamples: Peter Jackson, director of The Lord of the Rings films, took a creative approach – he used clever camera angles to make characters seem bigger or smaller than they really were.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a particular way of thinking about or dealing with something; a method
(2) n. the act of coming or getting nearer in distance or time
(3) vt. to come near or nearer to someone or something in space or time
(4) vt. to begin to deal with a problem, task, or situation in a particular way

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 接洽，主动接触（某人以提出请求/建议）
uncommonMeanings.example: Summoning up all her courage, she approached the famous director after the show, a rolled-up script trembling in her hands. （读后续写·追梦·鼓起勇气）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （接近某地的）通道，入口
uncommonMeanings.example: Snow had blocked every approach to the mountain village, cutting it off from the world for a full week. （读后续写·自然·被困）

posExamples.sentence: Instead of forcing the frightened stray to obey, the old vet took a gentle approach, kneeling in the mud and letting the dog come to him in its own time. （读后续写·动物·耐心）
In this letter I would like to suggest a fresh approach to reducing waste on campus: setting up clearly labelled recycling stations in every dormitory building. （应用文·建议信）
As the deadline approached, a quiet panic spread through the newsroom, yet the young intern kept typing, refusing to let fear steal her focus. （读后续写·职场·压力下的坚持）
When we approach failure not as a verdict but as feedback, every setback quietly becomes a lesson that sharpens us for the challenges ahead. （议论文·成长心态）

collocations.example: Peter Jackson took a creative approach, using clever camera angles to make his characters seem larger than life. （议论文·电影艺术）
Realising that scolding only made things worse, the teacher adopted a new approach, praising each small step the boy managed to take. （读后续写·教育·转变）
Her calm, methodical approach to solving problems reassured the whole team even when the deadline loomed. （应用文·推荐信）

collocations.translation: 亲身实践的／务实的方法
collocations.example: The workshop favours a hands-on approach, letting students learn to code by building their own small games. （应用文·课程介绍）
At the approach of winter, the villagers stacked firewood high against the walls, bracing for the long cold months. （读后续写·乡村·季节）
Several publishers approached the young writer about turning her viral blog into a book. （读后续写·成名）
The charity made a formal approach to the local school, hoping to recruit volunteers for the weekend clean-up. （应用文·公益）
In dealing with online rumours, a cautious approach — checking the facts before sharing — protects both ourselves and others. （议论文·网络素养）

synonyms.example: The traditional method of learning vocabulary by endless copying bored most of the class to tears. （议论文·学习）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'具体、成体系的步骤或程序'；approach 更侧重'处理问题的总体思路和角度'，更抽象灵活

synonyms.example: Music became her chief means of expressing feelings she could never put into words. （读后续写·情感）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'达到目的所用的工具或途径'，单复数同形；approach 强调思路而非工具

synonyms.example: As the stranger came near, the child instinctively hid behind her mother's coat. （读后续写·陌生人）
synonyms.usage: 口语化的动词短语，仅表'物理靠近'；approach 作动词还可表'着手处理''接洽'，用法更广、更正式

synonyms.example: Determined to tackle the problem head-on, the team stayed up all night rewriting the faulty code. （议论文·解决问题）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'积极、正面地对付难题'，动作性强；approach 侧重'以某种方式开始处理'，中性且可搭配态度形容词

advancedExpressions.expression: as ... approached, sth. crept over sb.

advancedExpressions.expression: may I suggest a more ... approach, namely ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: The exam was coming, so she was nervous.

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should deal with problems in a good way.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The wiser course, I would argue, is to approach every problem with a cool head and an open mind, treating it less as a threat to be feared than as a puzzle to be solved. （议论文·处世态度）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 插入语 I would argue 强化立场 + approach...with 固定搭配 + less...than 对比结构重塑认知

original_sentence: Peter Jackson, director of The Lord of the Rings films, took a creative approach – he used clever camera angles to make characters seem bigger or smaller than they really were.
readingExamples: Peter Jackson, director of The Lord of the Rings films, took a creative approach – he used clever camera angles to make characters seem bigger or smaller than they really were.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the space between two lines or surfaces that meet, measured in degrees
(2) n. the position from which you look at something; a point of view or direction
(3) n. a particular way of thinking about or presenting a situation, especially in the media
(4) vt. to move or point something so that it is not straight or level; to slant

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （报道、故事的）切入点，侧重点
uncommonMeanings.example: Every reporter on the scene chased the same tragedy, but the young journalist found a fresh angle — the quiet heroism of the rescue dog no one else had noticed. （读后续写·新闻·独特视角）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 钓鱼；（角度上）转向
uncommonMeanings.example: Old Tom would angle by the river for hours, less interested in the fish than in the silver stillness of the dawn. （读后续写·乡村·垂钓）

posExamples.sentence: The director crouched low and tilted the camera upward, and from that unusual angle the frail old man on the screen suddenly loomed like a towering giant. （读后续写·电影拍摄·镜头语言）
To make our school magazine more appealing, I suggest we cover the sports meet from a personal angle, telling the stories behind each athlete rather than merely listing the scores. （应用文·建议信）
When we examine a controversial issue from every angle — economic, moral and practical — we are far less likely to fall prey to one-sided, hasty conclusions. （议论文·辩证思考）
She angled the mirror toward the window so that a single blade of morning light slid across the sleeping baby's face. （读后续写·清晨·温情）

idioms.idiom: look at sth from a different / new angle
idioms.translation: 从不同的／新的角度看待某事
idioms.example: Only when he forced himself to look at the quarrel from his mother's angle did the boy finally understand the tears she had hidden. （读后续写·亲情·换位思考）
The old lighthouse leaned at a slight angle, as though bowing wearily to the sea it had guarded for a hundred years. （读后续写·景物·拟人）

collocations.example: By choosing clever camera angles, Peter Jackson made ordinary actors appear either towering or tiny on screen. （议论文·电影技巧）
Viewed from a purely economic angle, the plan seemed foolish; viewed from a human angle, it was priceless. （议论文·多角度）
The two paths met at a perfect right angle in the centre of the quiet garden. （读后续写·景物描写）
Travelling abroad taught her to see her own hometown from a completely different angle. （读后续写·成长·视野）
Before making the final decision, the committee carefully explored every angle of the proposal. （应用文·会议纪要）
Her essay offered a fresh angle on friendship, arguing that silence, not chatter, is its truest test. （议论文·独到见解）

collocations.phrase: the angle of the sun / light
collocations.example: As the angle of the setting sun lowered, the whole valley turned the colour of molten gold. （读后续写·黄昏·景色）

synonyms.example: Losing the match, painful as it was, gave him a new perspective on what truly deserved his tears. （读后续写·成长感悟）
synonyms.usage: 更抽象、更宏观，强调整体的观察立场与思维方式；angle 更具体，常指某一个特定的切入点或方位

synonyms.example: From an environmental viewpoint, single-use plastics are simply indefensible. （议论文·环保）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'个人所持的意见或立场'；angle 偏中性，指分析或呈现事物时选取的方向，未必带明确主张

synonyms.example: From a moral standpoint, turning a blind eye to the cheating was itself a kind of dishonesty. （议论文·道德）
synonyms.usage: 较正式、书面，多用于议论文表明立足点；angle 更灵活，也可用于视觉、镜头等具体含义

advancedExpressions.expression: seen from another angle, sth. was no longer ...
advancedExpressions.example: Seen from another angle, the wall that had trapped her for years was no longer a prison but a canvas, waiting for the first brave stroke of paint. （过去分词状语+隐喻重构，续写升华段）

advancedExpressions.expression: approaching the matter from the angle of ..., I propose ...
advancedExpressions.example: Approaching the matter from the angle of long-term sustainability, I propose that we plant native trees rather than import exotic ones. （现在分词状语框定视角+propose 提议，正式而有条理）

advancedExpressions.expression: examined from every angle, the truth is that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Examined from every angle — historical, cultural and personal — the truth is that no single label can ever capture the full richness of a human life. （分词状语+插入并列成分，全面立论）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He looked at the problem in a new way.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: For the first time, he tilted his head and looked at the stubborn problem from a wholly new angle — and just like that, the tangle that had defeated him for hours quietly unravelled. （读后续写·解题·顿悟）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 动作细节(tilted his head) + from a new angle 搭配 + 破折号制造顿悟节奏 + 拟物(tangle unravelled)

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should look at the issue from many sides.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Only by weighing an issue from every conceivable angle — moral, practical and emotional alike — can we hope to reach a judgement that is both fair and wise. （议论文·辩证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Only by...倒装强调 + from every conceivable angle 搭配 + 破折号列举三维度 + both...and 收束观点

original_sentence: Props also contribute to a film's success.
readingExamples: Props also contribute to a film's success.
definitionEn:
(1) n. an object used by actors or in a film or play, other than costumes and scenery
(2) n. a stick or other object placed under or against something to support it and stop it from falling
(3) vt. to support something or keep it in position, especially by leaning it against something
(4) n. a person or thing that gives support, help, or strength to someone

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （精神上的）支柱，依靠
uncommonMeanings.example: After his father died, the boy became the sole prop of the family, shouldering burdens far too heavy for his slender years. （读后续写·亲情·担当）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 支撑，支起（prop up: 撑起，扶持）
uncommonMeanings.example: She propped her chin on her hands and stared out at the rain, wondering whether the letter would ever come. （读后续写·等待·心理）

posExamples.sentence: Moments before the curtain rose, a stagehand rushed on to place the final prop — a battered leather suitcase that would, by the last act, break the whole audience's heart. （读后续写·校园戏剧·舞台）
For our history play, we still need a few simple props, so I would be grateful if any classmate could lend us an old lantern, a wooden sword, or a worn-out map. （应用文·借物请求）
He propped the broken door shut with a heavy chair, then pressed his back against it, listening to the storm howl through the ruined house. （读后续写·惊险·避险）
In any film, well-chosen props are far more than decoration; they quietly carry the story's mood and root fantasy firmly in believable detail. （议论文·电影艺术）

wordForms.other: prop up (phr. v. 撑起，支撑)

collocations.example: The volunteers spent all weekend painting stage props for the charity performance. （应用文·活动筹备）
Realistic props contribute enormously to a film's success, drawing audiences deeper into a world that feels entirely true. （议论文·电影）
Exhausted, the old farmer propped his rake against the fence and wiped the sweat from his brow. （读后续写·农忙·疲惫）
Too weak to stand, she propped herself up on one elbow just to catch a last glimpse of the departing train. （读后续写·离别·不舍）
For decades, that tiny shop had been the economic prop of the whole street. （读后续写·社区）
The nervous speaker used the podium as a prop, gripping its edges until his knuckles whitened. （读后续写·演讲·紧张）
Before the rehearsal began, the crew hurried to gather the props scattered across the dusty backstage. （读后续写·后台）

synonyms.example: The ancient roof was held up by twelve wooden supports, each carved with a coiling dragon. （读后续写·古建筑）
synonyms.usage: 最通用的'支撑'，可实可虚，正式中性；prop 更口语、更具体，常指临时或简易的支撑物，或戏剧道具

synonyms.example: For thirty years, Grandmother had been the pillar of our family, calm and unbreakable through every storm. （读后续写·家庭·精神支柱）
synonyms.usage: 既指建筑柱子，也常作比喻'中坚、栋梁'，庄重有力；prop 作比喻时更强调'扶持、依靠'，语气较轻

synonyms.example: Engineers added steel braces to the old bridge before the winter floods arrived. （议论文·工程）
synonyms.usage: 多指有加固、抵抗压力作用的支撑构件，专业性强；prop 更日常、更随意

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. propped ... and did ...
advancedExpressions.example: She propped the little umbrella over the shivering kitten, then tucked her own coat around it, forgetting entirely that she herself was soaked to the skin. （连贯动作+对比忘我，续写温情细节）

advancedExpressions.expression: we would be most grateful if you could lend us ... as props
advancedExpressions.example: We would be most grateful if you could lend us a few traditional lanterns as props, which would lend our performance an authentic festive glow. （借物委婉句式+which 非限定说明用途）

advancedExpressions.expression: seemingly trivial ..., like a well-chosen prop, can ...
advancedExpressions.example: Seemingly trivial details, like a well-chosen prop on a bare stage, can transform a flat, forgettable story into one that lingers in the mind for years. （明喻类比+抽象化，以小见大论证）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He was tired and leaned on the wall.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Bone-weary, he propped himself against the cold stone wall, his chest heaving, his legs trembling like reeds after the long, desperate climb. （读后续写·跋涉·疲惫）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 形容词前置(Bone-weary)作状语 + prop against 搭配 + 独立主格(his chest heaving) + 明喻(like reeds)刻画疲态

sentenceUpgrade.original: Props are important in films.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Far from being mere background clutter, carefully chosen props serve as the silent storytellers of a film, anchoring wild fantasy in details so real that we forget we are watching at all. （议论文·电影艺术）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Far from being...否定前置纠偏 + 比喻(silent storytellers) + so...that 结果状语强化说服力

original_sentence: Director James Cameron spent six months looking at and revising plans of the Titanic in order to build a full‑sized model for his 1997 film.
readingExamples: Director James Cameron spent six months looking at and revising plans of the Titanic in order to build a full‑sized model for his 1997 film.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to change, improve, or make additions to a piece of writing, plan, or set of ideas
(2) vt. to change your opinion, decision, or expectations because of new information
(3) vt. & vi. (British English) to study again lessons you have already learned, in preparation for an exam

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 修正（观点、看法、估计）
uncommonMeanings.example: The more he came to know the quiet new boy, the more he was forced to revise his first, unkind impression. （读后续写·友情·改观）

posExamples.sentence: Long past midnight, she was still hunched over her desk, revising the final paragraph again and again until every word finally rang true. （读后续写·写作·执着）
In light of the heavy rain forecast, we have decided to revise our original plan and move the charity fair from the playground to the school hall. （应用文·通知）
A wise person is never too proud to revise a firmly held belief once the evidence points, however uncomfortably, in a different direction. （议论文·理性与谦逊）
During the last week of term, the library was packed with students quietly revising for their final examinations. （应用文·校园生活）

collocations.example: James Cameron spent six months revising the plans of the Titanic before a single plank of his full-sized model was cut. （议论文·精益求精）
After witnessing the shy girl's courage on stage, the whole class was quick to revise its opinion of her. （读后续写·刮目相看）
Every evening after supper, the twins sat side by side, revising for the exam that would decide their futures. （读后续写·备考）
Given the falling costs, the committee revised its budget estimate downwards by nearly a third. （应用文·报告）
The manuscript came back thoroughly revised, its margins crowded with the editor's tiny, patient notes. （读后续写·写作·打磨）
The revised edition of the guidebook corrected dozens of errors that had misled travellers for years. （应用文·出版说明）
We should keep revising and refining the proposal until it truly reflects everyone's voice. （应用文·建议信）

synonyms.translation: 修正，修订（正式，尤指条文）
synonyms.example: The school council voted to amend the outdated rule that banned students from using the library at weekends. （应用文·规章）
synonyms.usage: 较正式，多指对法律、规则、条款作出正式改动；revise 更通用，可用于文稿、计划、观点乃至复习功课

synonyms.example: The engineer modified the design slightly so that the wheelchair ramp met the new safety standard. （议论文·细节）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'作局部、有限度的调整'，改动幅度通常不大；revise 可指大幅重写或整体修正

synonyms.example: Dissatisfied with the flat ending, she tore up the last page and rewrote it from scratch. （读后续写·创作）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'推倒重来、整段重写'，改动最彻底；revise 侧重在原有基础上修改润色，不一定重写

synonyms.example: Before the debate, the team reviewed every argument the opponents might raise. （应用文·准备）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'回顾、审视'以检查或巩固；作'复习'时与英式 revise 相近，但 review 通用于英美，且更强调审查评估

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. was forced to revise ..., realising that ...
advancedExpressions.example: He was forced to revise everything he had once believed about the old man, realising that behind that stern face lay a heart brimming with quiet kindness. （被动+realising 分词状语，续写认知反转）

advancedExpressions.expression: in view of ..., we have decided to revise ...
advancedExpressions.example: In view of the many suggestions received, we have decided to revise the schedule so that every club is given a fair share of the stage. （in view of 引出原因+revise 表调整，通知体规范）

advancedExpressions.expression: the courage to revise one's own views is ...
advancedExpressions.example: The courage to revise one's own views in the face of new evidence is not a sign of weakness, but the very hallmark of a mature and reasoning mind. （抽象名词作主语+not...but 递进定义，赞理性）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He changed his essay many times.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Draft after draft, he revised the essay with almost painful devotion, crossing out, rewriting, and crossing out again, until at last the words on the page matched the ones burning in his heart. （读后续写·写作·执着）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Draft after draft 名词重复推进 + revise 搭配 + 三动词排比(crossing out, rewriting, crossing out) + until 从句收束升华

sentenceUpgrade.original: People should change their ideas when they are wrong.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: To cling stubbornly to a proven error is mere vanity; to revise one's beliefs in the light of truth, however humbling, is the quiet mark of genuine wisdom. （议论文·理性）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 对偶结构(cling to error / revise beliefs) + 分号平衡两分句 + however humbling 让步插入语 + 抽象升华(mark of wisdom)

original_sentence: He talked to historians to ensure that the details were correct and even went down to the bottom of the Atlantic Ocean to see what was left of the ship for himself.
readingExamples: He talked to historians to ensure that the details were correct and even went down to the bottom of the Atlantic Ocean to see what was left of the ship for himself.
definitionEn:
(1) n. someone who studies or writes about history, especially as a subject at a university
(2) n. an expert in history, or a person who is a specialist in a particular period or aspect of the past

posExamples.sentence: The old historian ran a trembling finger along the faded map, and suddenly the dusty room seemed to fill with the clash of swords and the roar of battles fought a thousand years ago. （读后续写·历史·沉浸）
To make our history week truly memorable, I sincerely suggest that we invite a local historian to share the forgotten stories hidden in our own town's streets. （应用文·建议信）
As many historians have wisely observed, a nation that forgets its past is doomed, sooner or later, to stumble blindly into the very same mistakes. （议论文·以史为鉴）
Determined to get every detail right, James Cameron consulted historians and even dived to the ocean floor to see the wreck of the Titanic with his own eyes. （读后续写·匠心·求真）

wordForms.adjective: historic (有历史意义的) / historical (历史的)

collocations.example: Before writing the screenplay, the director consulted several historians to make sure not a single costume was out of place. （议论文·严谨创作）
According to historians, the tiny fishing village had once been a bustling port visited by merchants from across the sea. （读后续写·历史背景）

collocations.translation: 著名的／权威的历史学家
collocations.example: The lecture was delivered by a leading historian whose books have reshaped how we understand the ancient trade routes. （应用文·讲座通知）

collocations.translation: 历史学家一致认为／主张
collocations.example: Most historians agree that the invention of printing changed the course of civilisation more than any single ruler ever did. （议论文·文明进程）
As a social historian, she was less interested in kings and battles than in how ordinary people once lived and loved. （读后续写·治学视角）
Future historians may well remember our age not for its wars, but for the quiet moment humanity chose to save its dying planet. （议论文·时代反思）

synonyms.example: The visiting scholar had spent forty years piecing together the story of a single ruined temple. （读后续写·治学）
synonyms.usage: 泛指各学科的研究者、饱学之士，范围最广；historian 特指研究历史的学者，是 scholar 的一个具体类别

synonyms.example: As the village's unofficial chronicler, old Mr Lee filled notebook after notebook with the births, deaths and floods of a hundred years. （读后续写·记录者）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'按时间顺序记录事件的人'，偏叙述与保存；historian 更强调对史料的研究、分析与解释

synonyms.example: The archaeologists brushed away the sand grain by grain, until a golden mask stared up at them across three thousand years. （读后续写·考古·发现）
synonyms.usage: 通过发掘实物遗迹研究过去，重在'挖掘与实物'；historian 主要依据文献记载研究历史，二者常合作但方法不同

advancedExpressions.expression: as the old historian spoke, the past seemed to ...
advancedExpressions.example: As the old historian spoke, the past seemed to rise from the yellowed pages and walk quietly among us, as real and near as our own beating hearts. （as 状语+拟人复活历史，续写沉浸段）

advancedExpressions.expression: I would strongly recommend inviting a historian to ...
advancedExpressions.example: I would strongly recommend inviting a local historian to our reading festival, for nothing brings the past to life quite like a story told by someone who truly loves it. （recommend 提议+for 引出理由，建议信规范）

advancedExpressions.expression: as historians never tire of reminding us, ...
advancedExpressions.example: As historians never tire of reminding us, those who refuse to learn from the past are condemned, in one form or another, to relive it. （引用式立论 as...remind us+经典论点，权威可信）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The historian told us about the past.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: With every word the historian uttered, the dead centuries stirred awake, and we found ourselves no longer sitting in a classroom but standing amid the smoke and glory of a vanished age. （读后续写·历史·沉浸）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: With every word...状语引导 + 拟人(dead centuries stirred awake) + no longer...but 空间转换营造画面

sentenceUpgrade.original: Historians say we should learn from history.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Time and again, historians have warned us that history, when ignored, does not simply fade away — it waits patiently in the shadows, ready to repeat its harshest lessons upon those too proud to listen. （议论文·以史为鉴）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Time and again 频率状语强化 + 拟人(history waits in the shadows) + 破折号补充+定语从句(too proud to listen)深化警示

original_sentence: He talked to historians to ensure that the details were correct and even went down to the bottom of the Atlantic Ocean to see what was left of the ship for himself.
readingExamples: He talked to historians to ensure that the details were correct and even went down to the bottom of the Atlantic Ocean to see what was left of the ship for himself.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to make certain that something will happen or be the case
(2) vt. to make sure that someone or something is protected or safe from harm
(3) vt. to guarantee that a particular result or outcome is achieved

posExamples.sentence: Kneeling in the flickering candlelight, the old fisherman checked each knot twice, determined to ensure that not a single line would snap when the storm finally struck at dawn. （读后续写·细节动作）
To ensure the safety of every participant, we kindly ask that all volunteers arrive half an hour early and strictly follow the instructions given by the organisers on the day of the event. （应用文·通知）
No matter how advanced technology becomes, only a genuine sense of responsibility can ensure that scientific progress truly serves the well-being of humanity rather than threatening it. （议论文·科技与责任）
She rehearsed her lines over and over on the bus, refusing to let nerves ensure her failure on a stage she had dreamed of for years. （读后续写·心理准备）

collocations.example: The committee took every precaution to ensure that the charity concert ran smoothly from start to finish. （应用文·活动报告）
Lifeguards patrolled the shore constantly to ensure the safety of the swimmers as the tide grew rougher. （读后续写·海边救援）

collocations.phrase: ensure sb sth / ensure sth for sb
collocations.example: A balanced timetable ensures students enough rest as well as adequate time for independent study. （应用文·建议信）
Talent alone rarely ensures success; it is relentless practice that turns promise into achievement. （议论文·成功之道）
Recycling every scrap of paper helps ensure that our campus stays green and clean throughout the year. （应用文·倡议书）
The new online library ensures every rural student equal access to high-quality reading resources. （议论文·教育公平）
The strict quarantine measures were designed to ensure that the outbreak would not spread beyond the small village. （应用文·说明文）
Only by treasuring every learning opportunity today can we ensure a bright future for ourselves tomorrow. （议论文·励志）

synonyms.example: The workshop guarantees that beginners will finish their first painting within a single afternoon. （应用文·招募）
synonyms.usage: 语气比 ensure 更强，常含'承诺、担保'之意，也可作名词(a money-back guarantee)；ensure 侧重'采取行动使某事必定发生'

synonyms.example: Hard work does not always guarantee immediate rewards, but it never fails to shape a stronger character. （议论文·奋斗）
synonyms.usage: 见上，二者常可互换，但 guarantee 更强调对结果作出承诺

synonyms.example: After months of effort, she finally secured a place on the national debate team. （读后续写·奋斗成果）
synonyms.usage: secure 侧重'努力争取到'或'使稳固安全'，宾语多为具体成果(a job, a seat)；ensure 强调'使某事确定发生'

synonyms.example: Please make sure the windows are locked before you leave the classroom. （应用文·提醒）
synonyms.usage: 口语化，日常提醒常用；ensure 更书面正式，写作中更显水平

advancedExpressions.expression: determined to ensure that ..., sb did ...
advancedExpressions.example: Determined to ensure that his little sister never went hungry again, the boy took on every odd job the village had to offer. （分词短语作状语点明动机，续写塑造人物担当）

advancedExpressions.expression: only by ... can we ensure ...
advancedExpressions.example: Only by acting together, hand in hand, can we ensure a cleaner and greener community for generations to come. （Only 引导部分倒装，倡议结尾增强号召力）

advancedExpressions.expression: what truly ensures ... is not ..., but ...
advancedExpressions.example: What truly ensures lasting success is not fleeting luck, but the quiet perseverance that carries one through countless setbacks. （what 主语从句 + not...but 对比，论点鲜明有力）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He checked everything to make sure the plan would work.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: He went over every single step twice, leaving nothing to chance, determined to ensure that the rescue plan would unfold exactly as he had imagined it in the sleepless hours before dawn. （读后续写·心理+动作）

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should make sure every student gets a chance.

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is our shared responsibility to... 正式主句 + every single 强调 + regardless of background 插入语体现公平立场

original_sentence: He talked to historians to ensure that the details were correct and even went down to the bottom of the Atlantic Ocean to see what was left of the ship for himself.
readingExamples: He talked to historians to ensure that the details were correct and even went down to the bottom of the Atlantic Ocean to see what was left of the ship for himself.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. of or relating to the Atlantic Ocean or the regions that border it
(2) n. (the Atlantic) the Atlantic Ocean, the second largest ocean, lying between the Americas to the west and Europe and Africa to the east

posExamples.sentence: As the small boat rose and fell on the towering Atlantic waves, the young sailor gripped the mast and whispered a silent prayer to the grey, unforgiving sky. （读后续写·海上历险）
Our school is organising a documentary evening about the Atlantic voyages of early explorers, and we warmly invite every history lover to join us this Friday. （应用文·通知）
The bond between the two continents on either side of the Atlantic coast reminds us that no ocean is wide enough to separate people who share a common dream. （议论文·合作与联系）

wordForms.other: the Atlantic (Ocean) 大西洋（名词，专有名词，首字母大写）

collocations.example: It took the explorers weeks to cross the vast Atlantic Ocean in their fragile wooden ship. （读后续写·航海）

collocations.translation: 横渡大西洋；在大西洋彼岸
collocations.example: News of the discovery travelled across the Atlantic and stirred excitement in every European port. （议论文/记叙·历史）
We spent our summer holiday exploring the rugged villages along the Atlantic coast. （应用文·游记）
The first pilots to cross the Atlantic non-stop became overnight heroes celebrated on both continents. （读后续写·壮举）
Storms in the North Atlantic can turn a calm crossing into a fight for survival within hours. （读后续写·海难）

original_sentence: He talked to historians to ensure that the details were correct and even went down to the bottom of the Atlantic Ocean to see what was left of the ship for himself.
readingExamples: He talked to historians to ensure that the details were correct and even went down to the bottom of the Atlantic Ocean to see what was left of the ship for himself.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the very large area of salt water that covers most of the earth's surface
(2) n. one of the five main areas of sea, e.g. the Pacific Ocean
(3) n. (an ocean of / oceans of) a very large amount or number of something

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 大量，无数(oceans of / an ocean of)
uncommonMeanings.example: Standing before oceans of cheering faces, the once-shy boy suddenly understood that every lonely hour of practice had finally been worth it. （读后续写·舞台高光·数量夸张）

posExamples.sentence: The sun sank slowly into the ocean, spilling molten gold across the water until the whole horizon seemed to catch fire before her tearful eyes. （读后续写·环境描写）
To protect our blue ocean, we sincerely call on every student to refuse single-use plastics and to join our beach-cleaning campaign next weekend. （应用文·倡议书）
The ocean, which covers more than seventy percent of our planet, is not an endless dumping ground but a fragile home we are all duty-bound to protect. （议论文·环境保护）
As a child, I would sit for hours listening to the ocean roar against the rocks, dreaming of the distant lands hidden beyond that endless line of blue. （读后续写·童年回忆）

idioms.translation: 沧海一粟，微不足道的一点
idioms.example: The coins he donated were a drop in the ocean compared with the vast sum needed, yet his outstretched hand moved everyone in the square to tears. （读后续写·善举·以小见大）

collocations.example: Divers descended to the bottom of the ocean to photograph the wreck resting silently in the dark. （读后续写·探险）
Long before aeroplanes existed, brave sailors dared to cross the ocean guided only by the stars. （议论文·勇气）
Every plastic bottle we recycle is a small step towards protecting the ocean we all depend on. （应用文·倡议书）
Warm ocean currents carry heat around the globe and shape the climate of distant continents. （议论文/说明·科普）
An ocean of doubts flooded her mind, yet she forced herself to take that first trembling step onto the stage. （读后续写·心理）
Scientists mapped the ocean floor and discovered mountain ranges taller than any on land. （议论文/说明·科学发现）
They sailed across the ocean for forty days before a thin green line of coast finally appeared on the horizon. （读后续写·抵达）

synonyms.example: The calm sea glittered under the moon like a sheet of silver silk. （读后续写·夜景）
synonyms.usage: sea 泛指海，范围可大可小，常指近陆的海域(the Mediterranean Sea)；ocean 指五大洋，面积更大、更宏大，也可比喻'大量'

advancedExpressions.expression: the ocean stretched out before sb, ...
advancedExpressions.example: The ocean stretched out before them, vast and silver under the rising moon, as if the whole world were holding its breath. （as if 虚拟从句 + 视觉画面，续写开篇造境）

advancedExpressions.expression: let us join hands to protect the ocean ...
advancedExpressions.example: Let us join hands to protect the ocean, for its health is inseparable from the future of us all. （祈使句 + for 引导原因，倡议增强感染力）

advancedExpressions.expression: just as the ocean is made up of countless drops, ...
advancedExpressions.example: Just as the ocean is made up of countless drops, a nation's strength is built upon the small efforts of ordinary individuals. （just as 类比 + is made up of 结构，论证以小成大）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She looked at the ocean and felt calm.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As she gazed at the boundless ocean shimmering in the golden dusk, the anxiety that had gnawed at her heart for weeks slowly dissolved into the gentle rhythm of the waves. （读后续写·心理+环境交融）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: As 时间状语从句 + boundless/shimmering 修饰渲染 + dissolved into the rhythm of the waves 情景交融的隐喻收束

sentenceUpgrade.original: We must protect the ocean because it is important.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The ocean is not merely a body of water but the very cradle of life on this planet; safeguarding it, therefore, is nothing less than safeguarding our own future. （议论文·正式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: not merely...but... 递进强调 + cradle of life 比喻 + nothing less than 加强语气收尾

original_sentence: It took 500 workers 100 days to build the fine model, not to mention the thousands of props inside.
readingExamples: It took 500 workers 100 days to build the fine model, not to mention the thousands of props inside.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. used to introduce an additional and often more striking fact, meaning 'and also' or 'in addition to what has already been said'
(2) phr. used to emphasise something extra so obvious or so great that it hardly needs to be stated ('let alone', 'to say nothing of')

posExamples.sentence: The old house had a leaking roof and creaking stairs, not to mention the cold wind that whistled through every crack on winter nights. （读后续写·环境描写）
Joining the volunteer club will sharpen your communication skills and broaden your horizons, not to mention the lifelong friendships you are sure to make. （应用文·招募/建议信）
Overusing our smartphones wastes precious study time and weakens our eyesight, not to mention the way it quietly erodes our ability to focus. （议论文·手机之害）

collocations.example: She had already mastered three languages, not to mention her remarkable talent for music. （议论文/记叙·人物）

collocations.translation: 更不用说做某事(接动名词)
collocations.example: Climbing the mountain in the dark was exhausting, not to mention finding the narrow path hidden among the rocks. （读后续写·登山）

collocations.phrase: not to mention the cost / time / effort
collocations.translation: 更不用说花费 / 时间 / 精力
collocations.example: Renovating the whole library would take months, not to mention the enormous cost involved. （应用文·说明）

collocations.phrase: not to mention the fact that ...
collocations.example: The plan is risky, not to mention the fact that we have very little time left to prepare. （议论文·反驳）

synonyms.example: The exhausted climber could barely stand, let alone take another step towards the distant summit. （读后续写·极限）
synonyms.usage: let alone 多用于否定句后，强调'连前者都做不到，后者更不可能'，语气递进向下；not to mention 多用于肯定句，追加一个更突出的正面或负面事实

synonyms.example: The trip offered stunning scenery and delicious food, to say nothing of the warm hospitality of the locals. （应用文·游记）
synonyms.usage: to say nothing of 与 not to mention 用法几乎相同，更为书面正式，可互换

synonyms.example: The programme develops leadership as well as teamwork. （应用文·介绍）
synonyms.usage: as well as 只是平列添加，无'强调更突出一层'的语气；not to mention 带有'这还没算上'的强调意味

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., not to mention ... —— 追加压垮性细节
advancedExpressions.example: His shoes were soaked and his hands numb, not to mention the hunger that clawed at his empty stomach. （连续列举困境后用 not to mention 补上最沉重的一笔，强化处境之艰）

advancedExpressions.expression: you will gain ..., not to mention ...
advancedExpressions.example: By joining our reading club, you will gain knowledge and confidence, not to mention the joy of discovering a whole new world between the pages. （罗列收获后用 not to mention 点出最动人的一条，增强吸引力）

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., not to mention the deeper harm that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Cheating in exams damages one's reputation, not to mention the deeper harm it does to the integrity a young person should treasure most. （先列表层危害，再用 not to mention 引出更深层危害，论证层层递进）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The room was small and it was also very dirty.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The room was cramped and stuffy, not to mention the layer of dust that had clearly settled undisturbed for years. （读后续写·环境）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: cramped and stuffy 形容词升级 + not to mention 追加更刺眼的细节 + that 定语从句(settled undisturbed for years)增强画面

sentenceUpgrade.original: Reading is good for your knowledge and your mind.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Reading broadens our knowledge and sharpens our thinking, not to mention the quiet comfort it brings on a lonely evening. （议论文/应用文）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: broadens...and sharpens... 平行动词 + not to mention 引出情感层面的额外益处，使论述由理性升向感性

translation: n. 讲座，演讲；教训，训斥 | vi. 开讲座，讲课 | vt. 指责，训斥
original_sentence: My lecture today may not be able to do justice to all the work people have done behind the scenes.
readingExamples: My lecture today may not be able to do justice to all the work people have done behind the scenes.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a talk given to a group of people to teach them about a particular subject, especially at a university
(2) n. a long, serious warning given to someone about their behaviour; a scolding
(3) vi. to give a lecture or a series of lectures
(4) vt. to criticise or warn someone angrily or seriously about their behaviour

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 教训，训斥，说教
uncommonMeanings.example: She braced herself for another long lecture about coming home late, but her father only sighed, sat down beside her, and quietly asked what was really troubling her. （读后续写·亲情反转·意外温柔）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 教训，训斥，责备
uncommonMeanings.example: Instead of lecturing the trembling boy about the broken vase, the old teacher knelt down and gently asked whether he had hurt his hand. （读后续写·师者仁心）

posExamples.sentence: Halfway through the professor's lecture, a hush fell over the hall as she projected a photograph that would change the way everyone in the room saw the world. （读后续写·课堂震撼）
We are honoured to invite Professor Li to give a lecture on Chinese poetry, and all students interested in traditional culture are warmly welcome to attend. （应用文·通知）
Great teachers do not merely lecture at their students from a distance; they light a fire of curiosity that keeps burning long after the class is over. （议论文·教育）
The more parents lecture their children about mistakes, the more likely those children are to hide their next one. （议论文·教育方式）

collocations.example: The scientist gave a fascinating lecture on space travel that left the young audience wide-eyed with wonder. （读后续写/应用文·讲座）
Hundreds of eager students attended the lecture, filling every seat and even the stairs of the crowded hall. （应用文·报道）
Her lecture on environmental protection inspired the whole class to start a recycling programme the very next day. （议论文/记叙·影响）
The lecture hall fell silent the moment the famous author stepped up to the microphone. （读后续写·场景）

collocations.translation: 训斥某人，给某人上一课
collocations.example: Rather than giving me a lecture, my grandmother simply told a story that taught me more than any scolding ever could. （读后续写·亲情/成长）

collocations.translation: 巡回演讲 / 系列讲座
collocations.example: The professor went on a nationwide lecture tour to spread awareness of endangered species. （应用文·报道）
This week's guest lecture by a Nobel laureate is an opportunity too precious for any curious mind to miss. （应用文·通知）

synonyms.example: His graduation speech was so moving that many students were still quoting it years later. （应用文/记叙·毕业）
synonyms.usage: speech 泛指在正式场合的讲话，主题不限、时间较短(a wedding speech)；lecture 特指教学或学术性质的讲座，目的在于传授知识

synonyms.example: The author gave an informal talk about how she found ideas for her stories. （应用文·活动）
synonyms.usage: talk 比 lecture 随意、亲切、篇幅更短，学术性弱；lecture 更正式、系统、常与大学课堂相关

synonyms.example: His mother scolded him for staying out so late, her voice sharp with worry rather than anger. （读后续写·亲情）
synonyms.usage: 作'训斥'讲时，lecture 强调'长篇大论地说教'，语气冗长；scold 强调'厉声责骂'，更短促直接

advancedExpressions.expression: brace oneself for a lecture, only to find ...
advancedExpressions.example: He braced himself for a lecture, only to find his coach pulling him into a warm, wordless embrace. （braced oneself for + only to find 制造预期落差，续写常用的温情反转）

advancedExpressions.expression: we are honoured to invite ... to give a lecture on ...
advancedExpressions.example: We are honoured to invite Dr. Wang to give a lecture on artificial intelligence this Friday afternoon in the school hall. （正式邀请套语，通知/邀请信首段）

advancedExpressions.expression: true education is not about lecturing but about ...
advancedExpressions.example: True education is not about lecturing students into silence, but about inspiring them to ask questions no textbook has yet answered. （not about...but about... 对比 + 隐喻，教育类论点鲜明）

sentenceUpgrade.original: His father told him off for being lazy.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: He expected the usual lecture about his laziness, yet his father merely handed him a worn notebook and said softly, 'Read this when you are ready to try again.' （读后续写·亲情反转）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: expected...yet 制造预期反差 + 熟词僻义 lecture(训斥) + 直接引语 + worn 细节，冲突化为温情

sentenceUpgrade.original: The teacher gave a lecture and the students learned a lot.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: So vividly did the professor deliver her lecture that, long after the final bell, the students lingered in the corridor, still arguing passionately about the ideas she had planted in their minds. （议论文/记叙·感染力）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: So + 副词 + did 部分倒装强调 + long after 时间对比 + planted in their minds 隐喻，突出讲座的深远影响

original_sentence: My lecture today may not be able to do justice to all the work people have done behind the scenes.
readingExamples: My lecture today may not be able to do justice to all the work people have done behind the scenes.
definitionEn:
(1) n. fairness in the way people are treated; the quality of being just or fair
(2) n. the system of laws and courts by which people are judged and punished
(3) n. the fact of being right or reasonable; rightfulness of a claim
(4) n. (Justice) a judge in a law court, especially of a supreme court (title)

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 法官(尤指高等法院法官，作头衔时大写 Justice)
uncommonMeanings.example: The old Justice removed his glasses, looked down at the trembling defendant, and for a long moment said nothing at all, as if weighing not the crime but the whole of a broken life. （读后续写·法庭·人性时刻）

posExamples.sentence: When the real thief finally confessed, tears of relief streamed down the wronged man's face — after ten long years, justice had come at last. （读后续写·沉冤得雪）
As students, we should firmly stand up for justice, refusing to stay silent when a classmate is unfairly treated before our very eyes. （应用文·倡议书）
A society without justice is like a house built on sand: no matter how splendid it looks, it cannot stand the test of time. （议论文·社会公正）
The photograph did not do justice to the breathtaking beauty of the valley at sunrise, where mist and gold seemed to melt into one. （读后续写·景物·do justice to）

wordForms.adjective: just（公正的，正义的）/ justifiable（正当的，有理由的）
wordForms.other: justify vt. 证明……正当；unjust adj. 不公正的

idioms.translation: 公正地对待；充分展现，与……相称
idioms.example: No words could ever do justice to the courage of the firefighters who ran into the flames while everyone else was running out. （读后续写·英雄·赞颂）
Crippled by nerves, she failed to do herself justice in the first round, yet she walked back on stage with her chin held high. （读后续写·比赛·心理）
The detective vowed that, however long it took, he would bring the criminal to justice. （读后续写·侦探）
The documentary exposed a shocking miscarriage of justice that had ruined an innocent man's life. （议论文/记叙·社会）

collocations.example: Fighting for social justice means giving a voice to those who have long been ignored. （议论文·社会）

collocations.translation: 为正义而战 / 主持正义
collocations.example: Throughout history, countless ordinary people have dared to stand for justice against overwhelming odds. （议论文·勇气）
Her strong sense of justice would not let her walk past the crying child without stopping to help. （读后续写·善良）
The grieving family sought justice not out of hatred, but out of love for the truth. （读后续写·亲情/法庭）
He could, with justice, claim that his hard work rather than luck had brought him success. （议论文·公正评价）
A fair justice system is the cornerstone of any civilised society. （议论文·社会）
The essay argues that equality and justice must go hand in hand if a nation is to prosper. （议论文·主题）

collocations.translation: 善有善报、恶有恶报的因果报应
collocations.example: In a moment of perfect poetic justice, the bully who had mocked the weak was rescued by the very boy he once despised. （读后续写·因果反转）

synonyms.example: The teacher treated every student with such fairness that no one ever doubted her judgement. （议论文/记叙·公正）
synonyms.usage: fairness 侧重具体待遇上的'不偏不倚、一视同仁'，较日常；justice 更宏大、庄严，常与法律、道德、社会秩序相关

synonyms.translation: 公平，公正(尤指制度上的)
synonyms.example: Educational equity ensures that a child's future is not decided by the place where he happens to be born. （议论文·教育公平）
synonyms.usage: equity 强调'因人制宜的实质公平'，多用于制度、资源分配语境；justice 更强调'是非曲直得到伸张'

synonyms.example: He acted out of pure righteousness, never once considering what he might gain or lose. （议论文·品德）
synonyms.usage: righteousness 偏道德、宗教色彩，指个人的'正直、义举'；justice 偏社会与法律层面的'公正得以实现'

advancedExpressions.expression: at last, justice had been done / had prevailed
advancedExpressions.example: At last, justice had been done, and the truth that darkness had buried for so long finally rose into the light. （at last + 抽象名词作主语 + 光暗隐喻，续写沉冤得雪的高潮收束）

advancedExpressions.expression: let us stand up for justice and ...
advancedExpressions.example: Let us stand up for justice and lend a hand to every classmate who is treated unfairly, for silence is itself a kind of injustice. （祈使呼吁 + for 引导原因，倡议信有力结尾）

advancedExpressions.expression: justice delayed is justice denied
advancedExpressions.example: As the old saying goes, justice delayed is justice denied; a right that comes too late may be no better than a right that never comes at all. （引用格言 + 平行同构，论证公正的时效性）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Finally the bad man was punished and it was fair.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: When the courtroom doors finally swung open and the verdict was read aloud, a wave of relief washed over the crowd — after so many years of waiting, justice had at last prevailed. （读后续写·法庭高潮）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: When 时间状语铺陈场景 + a wave of relief washed over 比喻 + justice had at last prevailed 抽象名词作主语升华主题

sentenceUpgrade.original: We need a fair society for everyone.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: A truly civilised society is not measured by the height of its skyscrapers, but by the justice it guarantees to its humblest citizen. （议论文·正式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: not...but... 对比结构 + 具象(skyscrapers)与抽象(justice)对照 + the humblest citizen 以小见大凸显立意

translation: 恰当处理（某人或某事）；公平对待（某人或某事），给予公正的评价
original_sentence: My lecture today may not be able to do justice to all the work people have done behind the scenes.
readingExamples: My lecture today may not be able to do justice to all the work people have done behind the scenes.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. to treat, represent or judge someone or something fairly, in a way that shows their true worth or full value
(2) phr. to deal with or perform something well enough to show how good it really is
(3) phr. (of a photograph, description, etc.) to represent someone or something as favourably as they deserve

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (常用于餐桌)充分享用、大快朵颐，把食物吃得干干净净以示赞赏
uncommonMeanings.example: After three days lost in the mountains, the rescued boy finally sat down to a warm meal and did full justice to every dish his grandmother had prepared, as tears of relief slid down her cheeks. （读后续写·团圆·饱含深情的一餐）

posExamples.sentence: As the curtain fell, she stood frozen backstage, tears in her eyes, convinced that no words could ever do justice to the roar of applause still echoing through the theatre. （读后续写·舞台谢幕·情感高潮）
I am writing to recommend Li Hua for the exchange programme, for a mere paragraph can hardly do justice to the dedication and kindness she has shown our whole community. （应用文·推荐信）
A single test score can never do justice to a student's true abilities, since creativity, resilience and character all lie far beyond what any examination can measure. （议论文·教育评价）
The photograph on the postcard simply did not do justice to the breathtaking sunrise we witnessed from the summit, its molten gold spilling across an endless sea of clouds. （读后续写·登顶·景物描写）

idioms.translation: 充分发挥自己的水平；不辜负自己的能力
idioms.example: Crippled by nerves in the first round, the young violinist finally did herself justice in the finale, her bow gliding across the strings as if guided by some invisible hand. （读后续写·比赛逆袭）

idioms.idiom: to do sb. justice / in fairness to sb.
idioms.example: To do him justice, the new coach had never promised miracles; he had only asked us to trust the process and never give up. （读后续写·公正评价）

collocations.translation: 充分体现/尽情享用某物
collocations.example: No summary could do full justice to the sheer scale of the volunteers' effort behind this charity concert. （应用文·感谢信）

collocations.phrase: cannot / can hardly do justice to
collocations.translation: 无法充分展现/难以公正评价
collocations.example: Photographs can hardly do justice to the majesty of the Great Wall winding endlessly over the mountains. （读后续写·景物）

collocations.phrase: do justice to one's talent / ability
collocations.translation: 使某人的才华得到应有的展现
collocations.example: The dull, repetitive script failed to do justice to the actor's remarkable talent. （议论文·影视评论）

collocations.translation: 与场合相称；不负这一时刻

synonyms.example: No lens could truly capture the wonder in the child's eyes as the fireworks bloomed overhead. （读后续写·节日）
synonyms.usage: 侧重'完整生动地再现'某个瞬间或本质，常用于描写/艺术语境；do justice to 更强调'与其应得的价值相称'

advancedExpressions.expression: no words / nothing could ever do justice to ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: The photo was not as beautiful as the real scene.

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: do no justice to 否定强调 + 破折号铺陈感官细节(触觉/视觉) + 现在分词短语(blooming in my chest)状写心理 + 意象升华(free)

sentenceUpgrade.original: One exam cannot show a student's real ability.

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is my firm conviction that... 正式主句 + however引导让步 + do justice to 主干 + for引导原因 + 三个c头韵词(character, curiosity, courage)增强气势

original_sentence: Just as the poor passengers on the real Titanic saw the tip of the iceberg, what we see on the cinema screen is just the tip of the huge iceberg of filming.
readingExamples: Just as the poor passengers on the real Titanic saw the tip of the iceberg, what we see on the cinema screen is just the tip of the huge iceberg of filming.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a very large mass of ice floating in the sea, most of which is hidden beneath the surface of the water
(2) n. (figurative) the small, visible part of a much larger hidden problem, situation or body of information
(3) n. (informal) a person who is cold, unemotional or emotionally distant

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (比喻)冷漠无情、不动声色的人

posExamples.sentence: Out of the freezing mist loomed an iceberg the size of a cathedral, its jagged blue walls glittering coldly as the tiny fishing boat drifted helplessly towards them. （读后续写·海上险境·环境描写）
We are writing to remind all residents that the litter visible on our beach is merely the tip of the iceberg, for tonnes of plastic lie hidden beneath the sand and the waves. （应用文·环保倡议书）

What we admire in a champion — the medal, the podium, the roar of the crowd — is only the tip of the iceberg, concealing years of solitary training in the dark before dawn. （议论文·成功与努力）

idioms.example: The complaints reaching the headmaster's desk were only the tip of the iceberg; beneath them simmered a discontent that had been building for years. （读后续写·校园矛盾）

The moment the ship struck the iceberg, a terrible shudder ran through the hull and the lights flickered out. （读后续写·海难）
A melting iceberg, dripping under the relentless sun, has become the haunting image of a warming planet. （议论文·气候变化）
What the audience applauds on screen is just the visible edge of an enormous iceberg of unseen labour. （应用文·观后感）
Beneath the iceberg of his cheerful smile lay a loneliness he had never dared to confess. （读后续写·心理描写）

synonyms.example: The ancient glacier crept down the valley at a pace no human eye could detect. （读后续写·自然）
synonyms.usage: 指陆地上缓慢移动的巨大冰体，不漂浮在海上；iceberg 是断裂入海、随水漂流的冰块

advancedExpressions.expression: out of the mist / darkness loomed an iceberg ...

advancedExpressions.expression: ... is merely the tip of the iceberg; beneath it lies ...

original_sentence: To the frequently asked question, 'What's your favourite film?', my answer is Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon.
readingExamples: To the frequently asked question, 'What's your favourite film?', my answer is Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a large imaginary creature that can breathe out fire, usually represented as a fierce, winged, fire-breathing beast in Western stories
(2) n. (in Chinese culture) a mythical creature symbolising power, good fortune, nobility and the emperor
(3) n. (informal, disapproving) a fierce, strict or bad-tempered woman who frightens people

posExamples.sentence: In the Spring Festival parade, a golden dragon over thirty metres long twisted and soared above the roaring crowd, its scales flashing like a thousand tiny suns. （读后续写·传统节日·场面描写）

collocations.example: In his nightmare a fire-breathing dragon circled the village, its shadow blotting out the moon. （读后续写·梦境）

synonyms.example: A great serpent slid silently through the temple ruins, its eyes gleaming like emeralds. （读后续写·神话）

synonyms.example: The knight had slain many a beast, but nothing had prepared him for what waited in the cave. （读后续写·冒险）
synonyms.usage: 泛指凶猛的动物或怪物，范围最广；dragon 特指传说中的龙，文化内涵丰富

advancedExpressions.expression: a dragon ..., its scales flashing / shadow blotting out ...

advancedExpressions.expression: come alive in ... hands / bring the dragon to life

advancedExpressions.expression: far from ..., the dragon stands for ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: A dragon appeared in the sky during the festival.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As the drums thundered, a colossal dragon burst into the sky above the square, its scales blazing crimson and gold, weaving and plunging through clouds of firework smoke while the crowd below erupted into a single, deafening cheer. （读后续写·节日高潮）

sentenceUpgrade.original: In China the dragon is a good symbol, but in the West it is bad.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Whereas the Western dragon lurks in caves as a hoard-guarding monster to be slain, its Eastern counterpart soars through the clouds as a benevolent bringer of rain and fortune — a vivid reminder that a single image may wear opposite faces in different cultures. （议论文·文化对比）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Whereas引导对比状语从句 + counterpart 避免重复 + 破折号引出结论(a vivid reminder that...) + 拟人化对照(lurks vs. soars)

translation: n. 奖，奖品，奖金 | vt. 授予，给予
original_sentence: It has won many awards, including an Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.
readingExamples: It has won many awards, including an Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a prize, certificate or amount of money given to someone as an official recognition of their achievement, skill or quality

(3) vt. (law) to decide officially that someone should receive something such as compensation or damages

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (法律)判给，裁定给予(赔偿、金额等)

collocations.phrase: award sb. sth. / award sth. to sb.

The foundation awards ten scholarships each year to students from disadvantaged families. （议论文·教育公平）

synonyms.example: She clutched the first prize to her chest as though afraid it might vanish. （读后续写·比赛）

synonyms.usage: 指为特定目的(研究、学习等)提供的资金，不含'表彰'意味；award 侧重对功绩的褒奖

synonyms.example: It was the highest honour the academy could bestow. （应用文·表彰）

advancedExpressions.expression: when sb.'s name was called for the award, ...

posExamples.sentence: The moment the lights dimmed, a hush swept over the audience, and a thousand held breaths seemed to rise together as the first note trembled through the silent hall. （读后续写·演出开场·氛围渲染）
