It is a mistake to judge an entire generation by a few typical complaints heard online; behind the noise stand millions of young people quietly working towards a better tomorrow. （议论文·反对以偏概全）
With her patched coat and endless questions, she was not a typical new student, and within a week she had turned our sleepy classroom completely upside down. （读后续写·人物出场·反差）

collocations.example: His quiet act of returning the lost wallet was a typical example of the honesty our teacher had spent three years trying to plant in us. （读后续写·品格·以事显德）

collocations.translation: 是某人/某物的典型特征；很符合……的一贯风格
collocations.example: It was typical of Grandma to give away her own umbrella and walk home soaked through, smiling as if nothing had happened. （读后续写·祖母·无私）
A typical morning at the shelter began before dawn, with the soft padding of paws and the eager eyes of dogs waiting to be fed. （读后续写·志愿服务）

collocations.phrase: far from typical / anything but typical
collocations.translation: 远非寻常，一点也不典型
collocations.example: What happened next was far from typical: instead of laughing, the whole class rose to its feet and applauded the trembling boy. （读后续写·意外反转·感动）
The little museum, typical of its kind in old mining towns, held rusty tools and faded photographs that whispered of a vanished way of life. （读后续写·怀旧·环境）
On the surface it seemed a fairly typical village, yet beneath its calm ran stories of courage no history book had ever recorded. （读后续写·表里对比）
In my presentation, I outlined the typical features of Chinese tea culture — patience, harmony and quiet respect for guests. （应用文·文化介绍）

synonyms.example: The survey chose a representative group of students from every grade, so that no single voice could drown out the rest. （议论文/应用文·调查报告）
synonyms.usage: representative 强调'能代表整体、可作样本'，常用于调查、抽样语境；typical 更强调'具备该类事物的常见特征'。

synonyms.example: With characteristic calm, the old captain gave his orders, and the panic aboard slowly gave way to order. （读后续写·人物·沉稳）
synonyms.usage: characteristic 强调'某人/某物独有、区别于他者的特征'；typical 强调'与同类相符、有代表性'，前者重个性，后者重共性。

synonyms.example: The standard procedure required every visitor to sign in, yet on that snowy night the guard quietly waved the shivering stranger inside. （读后续写·规则与温情）
synonyms.usage: standard 侧重'符合规定/常规标准'；typical 侧重'具代表性、常见'，standard 更中性、程序化。

advancedExpressions.expression: it was a typical ..., with ..., ..., and ...
advancedExpressions.example: It was a typical autumn afternoon, with golden leaves drifting down, sunlight pooling on the old stone steps, and the distant laughter of children floating on the breeze. （典型场景 + with 独立主格三细节，快速铺开画面）

advancedExpressions.expression: to give you a clearer picture, let me describe a typical ...
advancedExpressions.example: To give you a clearer picture of our campus life, let me describe a typical school day, from the cheerful morning run to the quiet reading hour before dusk. （介绍信过渡句，用 typical 引出具体描写）

advancedExpressions.expression: it is unfair / misleading to take a few typical cases as representative of the whole
advancedExpressions.example: It is both unfair and misleading to take a few typical cases of failure as representative of an entire group, for every generalization is a shadow that hides countless bright exceptions. （反对以偏概全，typical/representative 精准对比）

sentenceUpgrade.original: It was a normal winter morning.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It was a typical winter morning, and yet, as the first snow of the year settled softly over the sleeping town, even the most ordinary rooftops seemed touched with a quiet, unexpected magic. （读后续写·平凡中见诗意·环境）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: typical...and yet 制造'平凡→不凡'转折 + 拟人 town sleeping / rooftops touched with magic + 副词 softly, quietly 控制节奏

sentenceUpgrade.original: Don't judge everyone by a few bad examples.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: We should never allow a handful of typical failures to colour our view of an entire generation, for behind every loud complaint stand countless silent souls working, hoping and quietly changing the world. （议论文·反对以偏概全·排比）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: never allow...to colour our view 提升语气 + for 引出理由 + 三动词排比 working, hoping and changing + 对比 loud vs silent，论证更有力

translation: adj. 复杂的；花哨的；昂贵的 | vt. 想要，想做；倾慕
original_sentence: The film looks like a fairly typical historical film without fancy special effects, and it is made enjoyable by the performances of the main actors.
readingExamples: The film looks like a fairly typical historical film without fancy special effects, and it is made enjoyable by the performances of the main actors.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. elaborate, decorative, or complicated in design, rather than plain or simple
(2) adj. expensive and fashionable, often unnecessarily so
(3) vt. (BrE, informal) to want something or want to do something
(4) vt. (BrE, informal) to feel sexually or romantically attracted to someone
(5) vt. to think or believe something, especially without being certain
(6) n. a feeling of wanting or liking something, which is not based on reason

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （英式口语）喜欢，倾慕，看上（某人）
uncommonMeanings.example: Everyone in class had guessed that he fancied the new girl long before he dared even to say hello. （读后续写·校园·青涩情愫）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （较正式/文学）以为，认为，想象（尤指没把握地设想）
uncommonMeanings.example: For one wild moment she fancied she heard her late grandmother humming in the kitchen, and her heart clenched with a longing too deep for words. （读后续写·思念·恍惚幻觉）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 一时兴起的喜好，突发的念头；想象力
uncommonMeanings.example: Building a boat from old crates was just a summer fancy of theirs, yet that reckless dream taught the boys more than any classroom ever had. （读后续写·童年·奇思异想）

posExamples.sentence: The little café needed no fancy decorations; its worn wooden tables and the smell of roasting coffee were enough to make every traveller feel instantly at home. （读后续写·温馨小店·朴实之美）
For our charity sale, please do not bring fancy or expensive gifts; a simple handmade card will carry far more warmth to the children in the mountains. （应用文·倡议/通知）
"Fancy a walk before dinner?" Grandpa asked, holding out his weathered hand, and in that small invitation lay all the love he could never quite put into words. （读后续写·祖孙·含蓄温情）
A film need not rely on fancy special effects to move us; more often, it is an honest story and a single true performance that stay with us long after the lights come up. （议论文·艺术的本质）

idioms.idiom: take a fancy to sb / sth
idioms.example: The lonely old widow took such a fancy to the stray cat that within a week it was sleeping on the softest cushion in the house. （读后续写·孤独与陪伴）
Of all the paintings in the gallery, it was a child's clumsy sketch of a sunrise that caught her fancy and would not let go. （读后续写·艺术·童真打动人心）

idioms.translation: 投合某人兴趣，逗某人开心
idioms.example: If none of the usual clubs tickle your fancy, why not gather a few friends and start one of your very own? （应用文·社团招募·亲切鼓励）

idioms.translation: 真没想到！竟有这种事！（表惊讶）
idioms.example: "The shy boy who never spoke in class has won the national writing prize — fancy that!" the old teacher murmured, wiping a tear of pride. （读后续写·意外·惊喜）

collocations.translation: 华丽的衣服/正装/高档餐厅
collocations.example: She did not own a single fancy dress, yet when she stepped into the hall in her plain white blouse, every head turned all the same. （读后续写·质朴之美·反差）
The meal was nothing fancy — just rice, eggs and pickled greens — but shared around that small table, it tasted like the finest feast in the world. （读后续写·家的味道·温情）
Stripped of fancy special effects, the documentary let the vast, silent desert speak for itself, and the audience sat spellbound. （议论文/读后续写·艺术评论）
"Fancy joining us for the mountain clean-up this Saturday?" she asked, and to her surprise the quiet boy nodded at once. （应用文/读后续写·邀请）
The moment the children took a fancy to the abandoned puppy, there was no chance any of them would leave the shelter without it. （读后续写·收养·温情）
He fancied himself a fearless explorer, until the first clap of thunder sent him scrambling back to the safety of the tent. （读后续写·自负受挫·幽默）
At first her parents dismissed the violin as a passing fancy, but ten years of dawn practice proved just how wrong they had been. （读后续写·坚持·证明自己）

collocations.translation: 花哨的脚法/华丽的辞藻
collocations.example: Real leadership is not about fancy words but about quiet deeds; people follow those who act, not those who merely talk. （议论文·言与行）

synonyms.translation: 精心制作的，复杂华丽的
synonyms.example: The palace ceiling was covered with elaborate carvings, each tiny figure telling a story older than the kingdom itself. （读后续写·古迹·环境）
synonyms.usage: elaborate 强调'工艺繁复、精雕细琢'，中性偏褒；fancy 有时暗含'华而不实、过分讲究'的意味，可褒可贬。

synonyms.example: After weeks in the wild, even a plain warm bed felt as luxurious as a king's chamber to the weary travellers. （读后续写·历尽艰辛·对比）
synonyms.usage: luxurious 侧重'昂贵、舒适、令人享受'；fancy 侧重'装饰花哨、显眼时髦'，未必真正舒适。

synonyms.example: All she desired that lonely evening was a familiar voice on the other end of the line. （读后续写·孤独·渴望）
synonyms.usage: desire 正式、语气强，表'强烈渴望'；fancy 作动词是英式口语，语气轻，多指'临时想要、有点想'。

advancedExpressions.expression: there was nothing fancy about ..., yet ...
advancedExpressions.example: There was nothing fancy about the tiny cottage, yet the warmth glowing from its windows on that snowy night felt richer than any mansion could ever offer. （nothing fancy...yet 对比，以简陋衬温情，续写常用）

advancedExpressions.expression: there is no need for anything fancy; what truly matters is ...
advancedExpressions.example: There is no need for anything fancy at our farewell party; what truly matters is that we gather, laugh, and treasure these last days together. （倡议/通知，反对铺张、强调心意）

advancedExpressions.expression: ... does not lie in fancy ..., but in ...
advancedExpressions.example: The value of a good film does not lie in fancy special effects, but in its power to make us feel, remember, and quietly become better people. （not in...but in...对比句，凸显本质超越形式）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The restaurant was not fancy but the food was good.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The little roadside restaurant was nothing fancy — no soft lights, no white tablecloths — yet the steaming bowl the old cook set before us carried a homely richness that no five-star kitchen could ever match. （读后续写·市井温情·对比）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: nothing fancy + 破折号列举缺失细节 no lights, no tablecloths + 对比 no five-star kitchen could match + 通感 steaming...homely richness

sentenceUpgrade.original: A good film doesn't need special effects.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: A truly great film need not dazzle us with fancy special effects; it wins our hearts instead through honest storytelling and performances so real that we forget, for two short hours, that we are only watching. （议论文·艺术本质·对比升华）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: need not dazzle...with fancy... + 分号转折 wins our hearts instead + so real that 结果状语 + 细节 forget that we are only watching，虚实结合论证

translation: adj. 狭窄的；勉强的；狭隘的 | vt. & vi. (使) 窄小，缩小
original_sentence: In the meantime, Hooper skilfully creates uncertainty and tension with narrow indoor sets and dark lighting.
readingExamples: In the meantime, Hooper skilfully creates uncertainty and tension with narrow indoor sets and dark lighting.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. measuring a small distance from one side to the other, especially in relation to length
(2) adj. limited in range, scope or variety; not broad-minded
(3) adj. only just achieved or avoided by a small margin
(4) v. to become or make sth less wide; to reduce or limit sth

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 勉强的，险胜的；仅以微弱差距的
uncommonMeanings.example: It was a narrow escape: had the branch snapped a second earlier, the falling climber would have plunged into the ravine below. （读后续写·历险脱困·后怕）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （眼睛）眯起，（差距）缩小
uncommonMeanings.example: Her eyes narrowed as she studied the stranger's face, and a flicker of recognition crept across her features. （读后续写·人物心理·警觉）

posExamples.sentence: As we edged along the narrow mountain path, the mist thickened around us, and every loose stone sent my heart hammering against my ribs. （读后续写·徒步历险·紧张氛围）
I would strongly advise against such a narrow selection of activities, for a festival confined to a single theme can hardly cater to the varied tastes of our student body. （应用文·建议信）
Those who cling to a narrow definition of success — money and fame alone — often overlook the quiet fulfilment that comes from serving others. （议论文·成功的意义）
By reading widely and travelling far, we can narrow the gap between what we imagine the world to be and what it truly is. （议论文·视野与成长）

idioms.idiom: a narrow escape / a close shave
idioms.example: The driver swerved just in time — it was such a narrow escape that his hands would not stop trembling for a full ten minutes. （读后续写·车祸险情·后怕）

idioms.idiom: keep to the straight and narrow
idioms.example: After years of trouble, he finally vowed to keep to the straight and narrow and rebuild the trust of those who had never given up on him. （读后续写·浪子回头·救赎）

collocations.example: We wandered through the narrow cobbled lanes of the old town, where washing hung like flags between the leaning houses. （读后续写·古镇漫游·画面感）
Looking back on that narrow escape, I realized how a single moment of caution had spared us from disaster. （读后续写·脱险反思）

collocations.phrase: a narrow margin / by a narrow margin
collocations.translation: 微弱的差距／以微弱优势
collocations.example: Our team won the debate by a narrow margin, a victory made all the sweeter by the weeks of relentless preparation behind it. （应用文·比赛报道）
The old fisherman narrowed his eyes against the glare of the setting sun, searching the horizon for the boat that had not yet returned. （读后续写·环境+心理·担忧）
Free evening classes were introduced to narrow the gap between urban and rural students' access to quality education. （议论文·教育公平）
After weeks of research, the committee narrowed down the candidates to just three finalists. （应用文·评选通知）

collocations.translation: 狭隘的心胸；心胸狭窄的
collocations.example: A narrow mind, forever suspicious of the unfamiliar, is the surest barrier to genuine friendship between cultures. （议论文·包容与偏见）
Confining ourselves to a narrow view of our own hometown blinds us to the astonishing diversity of the wider world. （议论文·开阔视野）

collocations.translation: 勉强避开／险些错过／侥幸逃脱
collocations.example: The goalkeeper dived full length and narrowly stopped the ball from crossing the line, sparing his team a crushing defeat. （读后续写·比赛·关键时刻）

synonyms.example: In such a restricted space, the two rescue workers could barely turn around, let alone lift the collapsed beam. （读后续写·救援·困境）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:restricted 强调受外部条件限制而受限，narrow 更直接描述物理宽度小或思想不开阔

synonyms.example: With only limited resources at his disposal, the young teacher still managed to bring the whole village a library. （议论文·条件与作为）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:limited 泛指数量/范围有限，narrow 在抽象义上更强调思想或选择的狭隘、不宽广

synonyms.example: A slender ray of light slipped through the crack in the curtains, tracing a golden line across the dusty floor. （读后续写·环境描写·清晨）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:slender 多形容优雅细长的形状（身材、光线），narrow 中性地强调宽度小，不带审美色彩

advancedExpressions.expression: it was a narrow escape; had ... , sb. would have ...
advancedExpressions.example: It was a narrow escape indeed; had the rope frayed a moment sooner, he would have been swept away by the churning current. （虚拟条件倒装+后怕心理，续写脱险段升华）

advancedExpressions.expression: I would caution against so narrow a ... , for ...
advancedExpressions.example: I would caution against so narrow a focus on academic scores, for a truly enriching campus life must also nourish the heart and body. （委婉劝诫+because从句，建议信论证）

advancedExpressions.expression: to narrow the gap between ... and ... , we must ...
advancedExpressions.example: To narrow the gap between ambition and achievement, we must translate lofty ideals into disciplined daily action.

sentenceUpgrade.original: We walked along a narrow path.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Single file, we picked our way along a narrow ledge that clung to the cliff face, the valley yawning dizzyingly beneath our trembling feet. （读后续写·环境+动作·惊险）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 定语从句(that clung to)拟人化 + 独立成分(Single file)开头 + 环境细节(yawning dizzyingly)营造惊险氛围

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should not have narrow minds.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: If we are ever to flourish as global citizens, we must cast off the narrow-mindedness that breeds prejudice and instead embrace the rich tapestry of human difference. （议论文·包容主题）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 条件状语从句前置 + 定语从句(that breeds prejudice) + 比喻(rich tapestry) + 对比结构(cast off...embrace)

original_sentence: All in all, I highly recommend this film.
readingExamples: All in all, I highly recommend this film.
definitionEn:
(1) v. to advise sb that a particular person, product or course of action would be good or suitable
(2) v. to praise sth or say it is good; to speak favourably of
(3) v. to suggest that sth should be done or accepted
(4) v. (of a quality) to make sb or sth attractive or acceptable

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 使显得吸引人；使被接受（常用 have much to recommend it）
uncommonMeanings.example: The little seaside inn had much to recommend it: home-cooked meals, a crackling fire, and a hostess whose kindness made every guest feel like family. （读后续写·旅途温情·环境）

posExamples.sentence: 'You simply must try the almond cake,' the old baker recommended with a wink, sliding an extra slice onto my plate before I could refuse. （读后续写·人物对话·温情）
I am writing to recommend Li Hua for the position of student ambassador, as her warmth and fluent English make her an ideal candidate for the role. （应用文·推荐信）
Experts strongly recommend that teenagers limit their screen time, arguing that unbroken hours before a glowing display do lasting harm to both sleep and concentration. （议论文·健康与科技）
The committee recommended replacing the outdated computers, a proposal that was warmly welcomed by teachers and students alike. （应用文·会议纪要）

collocations.example: It was my grandmother who first recommended this dusty little bookshop to me, and I have loved its quiet corners ever since. （读后续写·回忆·温情）
Our head teacher recommended me for the exchange programme, a vote of confidence that filled me with both pride and nervous excitement. （读后续写·成长机遇）
I would recommend arriving at least half an hour early, so that everyone has time to settle in before the ceremony begins. （应用文·通知）

collocations.translation: 建议某人做某事（虚拟语气）
collocations.example: The doctor recommended that he take a complete rest for a fortnight and avoid any strenuous exercise. （应用文·建议）
All in all, I highly recommend this novel to anyone who has ever felt lost and longed to find their way home. （应用文·书评）
The professor kindly agreed to write me a letter of recommendation, praising the very qualities I had feared no one had noticed. （读后续写·师生·感激）

collocations.translation: 经某人推荐；根据某人的建议
collocations.example: On my teacher's recommendation, I joined the debate club, a decision that would quietly reshape the course of my life. （读后续写·转折·成长）

collocations.phrase: have much / little to recommend it
collocations.translation: 有很多／没什么可取之处
collocations.example: The plan, hastily drawn up overnight, had little to recommend it beyond its low cost. （议论文·方案评价）

synonyms.example: May I suggest that we hold the charity sale in the school hall rather than outdoors, in case the weather turns against us? （应用文·活动建议）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:suggest 语气较委婉、平等，只提出想法；recommend 带有背书、担保的分量，暗示说话者认为这确实是好选择

synonyms.example: I would advise you to think twice before making so hasty a decision, for haste seldom leads to a wise outcome. （议论文/应用文·劝诫）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:advise 强调基于经验给出忠告，带指导意味；recommend 更侧重积极地推举、赞许某物值得选择

synonyms.example: The famous athlete publicly endorsed the campaign, and overnight thousands of young people signed up. （议论文·名人效应）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:endorse 多指公开、正式地表示支持（常见于产品代言、政策），比 recommend 更正式、更有权威色彩

advancedExpressions.expression: it was sb. who recommended ... , and for that I shall be forever grateful
advancedExpressions.example: It was Mr. Li who recommended me for the contest, and for that act of quiet faith I shall be forever grateful. （强调句+情感升华，续写感恩段）

advancedExpressions.expression: it is with the greatest confidence that I recommend ... , for ...
advancedExpressions.example: It is with the greatest confidence that I recommend Wang Ming for this scholarship, for seldom have I taught a student of such diligence and integrity. （正式主句+倒装强调，推荐信开篇）

advancedExpressions.expression: experts recommend that ... , a view that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Experts recommend that schools cultivate curiosity rather than mere obedience — a view that gains fresh urgency in an age of relentless change.

sentenceUpgrade.original: My teacher recommended this book to me.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It was my teacher who, noticing how I lingered by the shelves, gently pressed this worn little book into my hands and recommended I read it slowly, as one savours a fine meal. （读后续写·师生·细腻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 强调句(It was...who) + 现在分词状语(noticing) + 明喻(as one savours a fine meal)增添画面与温度

sentenceUpgrade.original: I recommend this film because it is inspiring.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: All in all, I would wholeheartedly recommend this film, not merely for its stunning visuals but for the quiet courage it awakens in every heart that dares to watch it. （应用文·影评）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 递进关联词(not merely...but) + 副词强化(wholeheartedly) + 定语从句(that dares to watch)升华情感

original_sentence: It tells the story of Forrest Gump, a simple man with a warm personality.
readingExamples: It tells the story of Forrest Gump, a simple man with a warm personality.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the various aspects of a person's character that combine to make them different from others
(2) n. qualities that make sb interesting, attractive or full of life
(3) n. a famous person, especially in entertainment or sport; a celebrity
(4) n. the quality of being a lively, distinctive individual

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 名人，公众人物
uncommonMeanings.example: The charity gala drew a host of television personalities, yet it was a shy little boy's speech that brought the entire hall to tears. （读后续写·慈善晚会·反差）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （场所、物件的）独特气质，鲜明特色
uncommonMeanings.example: The old café had a personality all its own — mismatched chairs, jazz humming from a corner, and walls papered with the dreams of a hundred regulars. （读后续写·环境·怀旧）

posExamples.sentence: Beneath his gruff exterior lay a warm and generous personality, one that revealed itself only to those patient enough to look beyond first impressions. （读后续写·人物刻画·反差）
In choosing our class monitor, we should value a sincere and responsible personality far more highly than a merely impressive academic record. （应用文·选举倡议）
It is often adversity, rather than comfort, that forges a resilient personality capable of weathering life's fiercest storms. （议论文·逆境与成长）
Her bubbly personality lit up the classroom the moment she walked in, and within a week not a single stranger remained. （读后续写·转学生·活泼）

wordForms.other: personalized (adj. 个性化的); persona (n. 人格面具)

idioms.example: What began as a mere clash of personalities gradually softened into mutual respect, as each learned to see the world through the other's eyes. （读后续写·和解·成长）

idioms.idiom: the life and soul of the party
idioms.translation: 聚会的灵魂人物，最活跃的人
idioms.example: With her boundless energy, Grace was always the life and soul of the party, drawing even the shyest guests into laughter. （读后续写·人物·活力）

collocations.example: It tells the story of a simple man with a warm personality whose kindness quietly changes everyone he meets. （应用文·电影简介）
Her strong personality, once mistaken for stubbornness, proved to be exactly the courage the team needed in its darkest hour. （读后续写·人物·反转）
His outgoing personality made him the natural bridge between the shy newcomers and the tight-knit old class. （读后续写·融入集体）
On stage she was fearless and radiant, but off it a quiet shyness took over — a dual personality that few of her fans ever guessed at. （读后续写·反差）
The way a person treats a waiter, they say, reveals more about their true personality than any interview ever could. （议论文·品格）
Patience and perseverance are the two personality traits that most reliably distinguish those who succeed from those who give up. （议论文·成功要素）
The young coach had such a magnetic personality that players would run through walls for him without a second thought. （读后续写·领袖魅力）
The years spent volunteering abroad did more to shape his personality than a decade of comfortable schooling ever had. （议论文·经历塑造人）

synonyms.example: It is in moments of hardship, not of ease, that a person's true character stands revealed. （议论文·品格）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:character 偏重道德品质与内在原则（诚实、勇敢），personality 侧重外在表现出的性格特点与魅力（活泼、外向）

synonyms.example: Blessed with a calm temperament, she remained composed even as chaos erupted all around her. （读后续写·危机·沉稳）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:temperament 指与生俱来、较稳定的情绪倾向和脾性；personality 范围更广，涵盖后天形成的整体性格面貌

synonyms.example: His cheerful disposition was infectious, turning even the dreariest of rainy afternoons into an occasion for laughter. （读后续写·氛围·感染力）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:disposition 较正式，指一个人惯常的、内在的情绪倾向；personality 更常用、更全面地描述整个人的性格特质

advancedExpressions.expression: beneath sb.'s ... exterior lay a ... personality
advancedExpressions.example: Beneath his cold, unsmiling exterior lay a tender personality, bruised by years of loneliness yet aching to be understood. （倒装+反差刻画，续写人物深度）

advancedExpressions.expression: what truly sets sb. apart is not ... but his / her ... personality

advancedExpressions.expression: it is ... that shapes personality, far more than ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: He has a warm personality.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: There was a warmth to his personality that needed no words to express — a smile that reached the eyes, a hand always first to reach out, a presence that made strangers feel, somehow, at home. （读后续写·人物·细节）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 破折号引出并列名词短语铺陈(a smile...a hand...a presence) + 排比 + 具体动作细节替代抽象形容

sentenceUpgrade.original: Personality is more important than looks.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: While a pleasing appearance may open a door, it is a genuine and generous personality that keeps it open — for beauty fades, but character endures. （议论文·内在与外在）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 让步状语从句(While...) + 强调句(it is...that) + 隐喻(open a door) + 对偶收束(beauty fades, but character endures)

original_sentence: Despite an IQ of 75, he lives a truly amazing life.
readingExamples: Despite an IQ of 75, he lives a truly amazing life.
definitionEn:
(1) prep. without being affected by; in spite of
(2) prep. used to show that sth happens or is true although sth else might have prevented it
(3) n. (formal / literary) contempt; the state of being scorned (chiefly in the phrase 'in despite of')

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （文学／古语）轻蔑，蔑视（多见于 in despite of）
uncommonMeanings.example: In despite of every warning the villagers had given him, the stubborn old sailor set out to sea, his weathered jaw set hard against the coming storm. （读后续写·倔强性格·文学化）

posExamples.sentence: Despite the biting wind that clawed at his coat, the boy pressed on toward the distant light, determined to bring the medicine home before dawn. （读后续写·雪夜·意志）
Despite the tight budget, I firmly believe our class outing can still be both meaningful and memorable if we plan it with care. （应用文·活动策划）
Despite an IQ of just 75, Forrest Gump lives a truly amazing life, proving that a good heart may carry a person further than a brilliant mind ever could. （议论文·善良的力量）
Despite repeated failures, the young inventor refused to abandon her dream, and it was precisely this stubborn hope that finally lit the world. （议论文·坚持与成功）

wordForms.other: in spite of (同义介词短语); despite the fact that (引导让步状语从句)

idioms.translation: 不由自主地，情不自禁地
idioms.example: Despite herself, a tear slid down her cheek as the old melody drifted from the piano, unlocking memories she had long tried to bury. （读后续写·情感·触动）
In despite of the danger, he plunged into the icy river without a moment's hesitation to save the drowning child. （读后续写·英勇·文学化）

collocations.example: Despite the fact that he had never held a brush before, his first painting stunned everyone who saw it. （读后续写·天赋·惊叹）
Despite everything she had suffered, she never allowed bitterness to harden her generous heart. （读后续写·苦难·坚韧）
Despite our best efforts, the rescue came too late — yet the whole village would forever remember how hard they had fought. （读后续写·悲情·尊严）
Despite the countless obstacles in their path, the volunteers built a school where once there had been only ruins. （应用文·公益报道）
Despite being the youngest competitor, she carried herself with a calm that put even the veterans to shame. （读后续写·比赛·沉稳）
That so many students persisted despite the exhausting schedule speaks volumes about their dedication. （议论文·毅力）

synonyms.example: In spite of the pouring rain, the fans stood their ground and cheered until the final whistle blew. （读后续写·球迷·热忱）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:in spite of 与 despite 意义完全相同，但 in spite of 由三个词组成、稍口语；despite 更简洁正式，写作中显得凝练

synonyms.example: Notwithstanding the committee's objections, the headmaster pushed the reform through, convinced that history would prove him right. （议论文·改革·魄力）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:notwithstanding 极为正式、书面，多用于公文、议论文；despite 通用性更强，日常与正式写作皆宜

synonyms.example: Regardless of the risks, the firefighters charged into the blaze, thinking only of the family trapped inside. （读后续写·英勇·舍己）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:regardless of 强调'不顾、不理会'某因素而行动，主动色彩强；despite 侧重客观上'尽管有某阻碍事情仍发生'

advancedExpressions.expression: despite ... , sb. pressed / soldiered on, determined to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Despite the numbing cold and his aching legs, he soldiered on through the snow, determined to reach the summit before the light failed. （介词短语前置+分词状语，续写坚持段）

advancedExpressions.expression: despite the ... , I am confident that, together, we can ...
advancedExpressions.example: Despite the limited funds at our disposal, I am confident that, together, we can turn this modest classroom into a warm and welcoming library. （让步开篇+呼吁团结，倡议信）

advancedExpressions.expression: despite ... , the truth remains that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Despite the dazzling convenience of modern technology, the truth remains that no screen can replace the warmth of a human hand.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Although it was raining, he kept running.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Despite the rain lashing at his face and the mud dragging at his shoes, he kept running, driven by a single thought: he would not let his team down. （读后续写·比赛·意志）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: despite 替代 although 使句子更凝练 + 现在分词并列(lashing...dragging) + 冒号引出内心独白强化动机

sentenceUpgrade.original: He was not clever, but he succeeded.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Despite an intellect far from remarkable, he carved out a life of quiet triumph — proof, if any were needed, that character often outweighs cleverness. （议论文·品格胜过才智）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: despite + 抽象名词短语 + 破折号插入评论(proof, if any were needed) + 对比(character...cleverness)提炼主旨

original_sentence: He sees, and sometimes influences, some of the major events of the United States in the second half of the 20th century.
readingExamples: He sees, and sometimes influences, some of the major events of the United States in the second half of the 20th century.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. very large or important, especially when compared with other things or people of a similar kind
(2) adj. very serious or dangerous
(3) n. a student's main subject or field of study (esp. AmE); v. to specialize in a subject at university
(4) n. an officer of middle rank in the army or air force

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （大学的）主修专业；（v.）主修
uncommonMeanings.example: Standing at the crossroads of her future, she finally chose to major in medicine — not for the salary, but for the frail grandmother who had once needed a doctor and found none. （读后续写·选择·动机）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （军队）少校
uncommonMeanings.example: The old major, his chest heavy with medals, saluted the young recruits one last time, his eyes betraying a pride no words could hold. （读后续写·军旅·传承）

posExamples.sentence: The discovery of the hidden letter marked a major turning point in the story, unravelling secrets the family had guarded for three long generations. （读后续写·情节·转折）
I am writing to propose a major change to our recycling scheme, one that I believe could transform our school into a model of green living. （应用文·建议信）
One major reason so many students lose interest in reading is that they are forced to chase grades rather than encouraged to chase wonder. （议论文·阅读教育）
After months of hesitation, he decided to change his major from law to marine biology, drawn irresistibly by the silent mysteries of the deep. （读后续写·抉择·热爱）

wordForms.other: majority (n. 多数); majorly (adv. 非正式:非常)

idioms.example: The major part of his childhood was spent by that quiet river, where he first learned to dream beyond the narrow horizon of his village. （读后续写·回忆·成长）

collocations.example: He witnesses, and sometimes influences, some of the major events that shaped his nation in the second half of the century. （应用文·人物简介）
Encouragement from a single teacher can play a major role in awakening a talent the child never knew he possessed. （议论文·教育的力量）
Water shortage remains a major challenge for the region, one that demands the combined wisdom of scientists and citizens alike. （议论文·环境）

That rainy afternoon, when a stranger returned her lost wallet, became a major turning point that restored her faith in humanity. （读后续写·转折·温情）
She dreams of majoring in astronomy, of one day naming a star after the mother she lost too soon. （读后续写·梦想·深情）
The young scientist's persistence led to a major breakthrough that would save countless lives in the decades to come. （议论文·科研·坚持）
Learning to listen is a skill of major importance, yet one that our schools too often neglect. （议论文·沟通能力）

synonyms.example: That small act of kindness, seemingly trivial, would have a significant impact on the course of her entire life. （读后续写·细节·深远影响）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:significant 强调'意义重大、值得注意'，常搭配影响、变化；major 更侧重'规模大、地位重要'，二者常可互换但 major 更口语化

synonyms.example: The principal cause of the misunderstanding was not malice but a simple failure to communicate. （议论文·分析）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:principal 指'首要的、排第一位的'，强调在众多中居首；major 强调'重要且规模大'，不一定是唯一最重要的

synonyms.example: In that crucial moment, when everyone else froze, it was the quietest boy who stepped forward. （读后续写·关键时刻·反转）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:crucial 强调'成败攸关、决定性'，语气最强；major 只表'重要、大'，未必到生死攸关的程度

advancedExpressions.expression: little did sb. know that ... would become a major turning point

advancedExpressions.expression: I am convinced that a major improvement lies in ...

advancedExpressions.expression: ... plays a major role in ... ; without it, ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: This event was very important to him.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: That single event, so easily overlooked at the time, proved to be a major landmark in his life — the invisible hinge on which his entire future would silently turn. （读后续写·回望·顿悟）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Reading is a major part of learning.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Reading, far from being a mere pastime, plays a major part in the shaping of the mind, for every book we open is a new window flung wide upon the world. （议论文·阅读的价值）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 插入让步结构(far from being a mere pastime) + because从句说理 + 隐喻(window flung wide)形象论证

original_sentence: He sees, and sometimes influences, some of the major events of the United States in the second half of the 20th century.
readingExamples: He sees, and sometimes influences, some of the major events of the United States in the second half of the 20th century.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a thing that happens, especially something important, interesting or unusual
(2) n. a planned public or social occasion, such as a party, competition or celebration
(3) n. any of the races or competitions in a sports programme
(4) n. (in the phrase 'in the event of / in any event') a possible or actual situation or outcome

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （体育）比赛项目
uncommonMeanings.example: The 800-metre was the one event she had trained for all year, and as she crouched at the starting line, the roar of the crowd faded into a single, steady heartbeat. （读后续写·赛场·专注）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （in the event / in any event）无论如何；结果
uncommonMeanings.example: We had feared the storm would ruin the ceremony, but in the event the skies cleared just as the first guest arrived. （读后续写·转折·天意）

posExamples.sentence: That summer's flood was an event none of the villagers would ever forget, for out of its muddy ruin grew a bond stronger than any they had known before. （读后续写·灾难·团结）

History teaches us that great events are rarely the work of a single hero, but the quiet accumulation of countless ordinary acts of courage. （议论文·历史与个人）
He witnesses, and sometimes influences, some of the major events of the United States in the second half of the twentieth century. （读后续写·人物·时代）

idioms.idiom: in any event / at all events

collocations.example: The school's centenary was such a big event that alumni flew in from every corner of the globe to celebrate. （应用文·活动报道）

collocations.phrase: attend / take part in an event

The annual charity event has become a cherished tradition, weaving generosity into the very fabric of our school life. （应用文·活动介绍）
A single careless remark set off a chain of events that no one could have foreseen or undone. （读后续写·连锁反应·悬念）
Keeping abreast of current events broadens the mind and sharpens one's judgement of the wider world. （议论文·关注时事）

collocations.translation: 事态的发展，事件的进程
collocations.example: One brave decision that morning altered the entire course of events, sparing the town a tragedy it never learned it had escaped. （读后续写·关键抉择）

collocations.translation: 事态的转变，形势的变化
collocations.example: By a strange turn of events, the very rival she had feared became, in the end, her closest friend. （读后续写·反转·温情）

synonyms.example: The graduation was a joyous occasion, one that mingled the sweetness of triumph with the quiet ache of farewell. （读后续写·毕业·复杂情感）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:occasion 强调'特定的、往往正式或有纪念意义的场合'；event 更泛，可指任何发生的事或有组织的活动

synonyms.translation: （尤指不寻常或不愉快的）事件

synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:incident 多指较小的、常带负面或意外色彩的事件；event 中性，且常指重大或有计划的活动

synonyms.translation: 发生的事情，事件（较正式）
synonyms.example: Power cuts were a common occurrence in the mountain village, yet the children learned to find magic in the candlelit dark. （读后续写·乡村·诗意）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:occurrence 较正式书面，强调'发生的事情'这一事实本身；event 更常用，且带'重要／有组织'的意味

advancedExpressions.expression: a strange turn of events found sb. ...
advancedExpressions.example: A strange turn of events found her, only a year later, standing on the very stage she had once fled in tears. （无灵主语+对比命运，续写转折升华）

advancedExpressions.expression: on behalf of ... , I cordially invite you to this year's ... event, where ...

advancedExpressions.expression: history shows that great events spring not from ... but from ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: The sports day was a big event for us.

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 定语从句(we had counted down to)蓄势 + 环境细节(cracked the morning air) + 抽象名词具象化(sweat and hope surged)

sentenceUpgrade.original: Many events happened that changed history.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The events that reshaped history were seldom trumpeted in advance; more often they crept in quietly, disguised as ordinary days, recognised for what they were only long after they had passed. （议论文·历史的偶然）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 定语从句(that reshaped history) + 分号连接对比 + 拟人(crept in quietly) + 时间状语延宕(only long after)引发思辨

original_sentence: The bus pulls up as Mrs Gump prepares Forrest for his first day of school.
readingExamples: The bus pulls up as Mrs Gump prepares Forrest for his first day of school.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. v. (of a vehicle or its driver) to stop, especially for a short time
(2) phr. v. to move your body upwards, especially by pulling with your arms
(3) phr. v. to bring or drag something into an upright or higher position
(4) phr. v. to tell someone that they have done something wrong; to check or correct sb.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 责备，纠正（某人）
uncommonMeanings.example: The stern coach pulled the boy up sharply for slacking, and the sudden reproof stung more than any physical fall on the track ever had. （读后续写·师生冲突·被批评的挫败）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 拽近，拉起（把身体或物体往上/往近拉）
uncommonMeanings.example: She pulled up a chair beside the hospital bed, took her grandmother's frail hand, and settled in for the long, quiet vigil of the night. （读后续写·亲情陪伴·病榻守候）

posExamples.sentence: Just as I was about to give up hope, a battered old pickup pulled up beside me, its window rolled down to reveal the kind, weathered face of the farmer who would change my journey. （读后续写·陌生人的善意·雨夜求助）

idioms.idiom: pull yourself up by your (own) bootstraps

collocations.phrase: pull sb up for / on sth

collocations.phrase: pull up at the kerb / roadside

collocations.translation: 并排停靠；追上并停在旁边

synonyms.example: The driver stopped the coach at the foot of the mountain so that the exhausted travellers could stretch their legs. （读后续写·旅途·停歇）

synonyms.usage: 偏正式、书面，常用于命令、军队、进程被强行中止的语境；pull up 更口语、更常指车辆

synonyms.example: A carriage drew up at the manor gates, and the butler hurried out to greet the long-awaited guest. （读后续写·古典场景·迎宾）

advancedExpressions.expression: just as ..., a car / figure pulled up ...

advancedExpressions.expression: drivers are kindly reminded to pull up ... so that ...

advancedExpressions.expression: it is high time we pulled up and reconsidered ...
advancedExpressions.example: It is high time we pulled up and reconsidered whether relentless pursuit of speed has quietly cost us the very things worth slowing down for. （it is high time + 虚拟过去式 + 反问，呼吁反思）

sentenceUpgrade.original: A car stopped and a man got out.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: A weather-beaten car pulled up at the roadside, and out stepped a stranger whose gentle eyes seemed to say that everything, somehow, was going to be all right. （读后续写·陌生人善意·倒装+外貌暗示）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: pull up 替换 stop 增画面感 + out stepped 倒装 + whose 定语从句刻画人物 + 用外貌暗示情感走向

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should slow down in life.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Perhaps the wisest thing we can do amid the ceaseless rush of modern life is to pull up now and then, breathe deeply, and remember why we ever set out on the journey at all. （议论文·哲理·文体升级）

translation: vi. & vt. 挥手，招手；挥舞 | n. 海浪；大量涌现
original_sentence: Mrs Gump waves to Forrest as the bus drives away.
readingExamples: Mrs Gump waves to Forrest as the bus drives away.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a raised line of water that moves across the surface of the sea, especially when the wind blows
(2) n. a sudden increase in a particular type of behaviour, feeling, or activity; a large number of people or things arriving at the same time
(3) v. to raise your hand and move it from side to side as a greeting, farewell, or signal
(4) v. to move something held in your hand from side to side, or to move gently to and fro in the air

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （情绪、活动、事物的）浪潮，热潮，一阵
uncommonMeanings.example: A wave of unexpected tenderness washed over her as she watched her son, now a grown man, sleep as peacefully as he had done as a child. （读后续写·亲情·情感涌动）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （无线电、声、光等的）波
uncommonMeanings.example: The rescuers sent radio waves crackling across the frozen valley, praying that somewhere in the white silence someone was still listening. （读后续写·救援·科技细节）

posExamples.sentence: As the train pulled away, my grandmother stood on the platform and waved until her small figure was swallowed by the crowd, yet I could still feel her love reaching after me. （读后续写·离别·目送）
On behalf of the whole school, I sincerely invite you to wave our banners high at the sports meeting and cheer our athletes on with unfailing enthusiasm. （应用文·邀请信·运动会）
A wave of environmental awareness is sweeping across our campus, inspiring students to abandon disposable cups and embrace a greener way of living. （议论文·环保·社会趋势）
Towering waves crashed against the rocks as the tiny fishing boat fought its way home, and I clung to the rail, both terrified and strangely exhilarated. （读后续写·海上历险·环境描写）

wordForms.other: waver (vi. 摇曳；动摇); waveform (n. 波形)

idioms.translation: 兴风作浪；制造麻烦；引起轰动
idioms.example: The young journalist was warned not to make waves, but she knew that some truths were worth every ounce of the trouble they caused. （议论文/读后续写·勇气·坚持真相）
When the factory closed, hundreds of workers had to wave goodbye to the only livelihood they had ever known. （议论文·社会·失业）

collocations.example: The little boy waved frantically at the departing ship until his mother, tears in her eyes, gently lowered his tired arm. （读后续写·离别·童真）

collocations.phrase: wave sb goodbye / wave goodbye to sb
collocations.example: We waved the volunteers goodbye at dawn, knowing that the memories of that summer would bind us together for years to come. （读后续写·分别·友情）

collocations.phrase: a wave of + 情绪/事物
collocations.example: A wave of relief swept through the classroom the instant the invigilator announced that the exam had been postponed. （读后续写·校园·情绪）
Her debut novel made waves in literary circles, forcing even seasoned critics to reconsider what youth was capable of. （议论文·成就·影响力）
He waved his arms wildly above the swaying grass, desperate to catch the attention of the search helicopter overhead. （读后续写·求救·动作）
By riding the wave of renewed interest in traditional crafts, the old artisan finally found the recognition he had long deserved. （议论文·文化·机遇）

collocations.translation: 把（意见、担忧等）置之不理；挥手示意走开
collocations.example: The captain waved aside our fears with a confident smile, assuring us that he had weathered far worse storms than this. （读后续写·危机·领袖气度）

collocations.phrase: the wind blows the waves / waves crash / roll
collocations.example: As waves crashed and rolled beneath a bruised evening sky, she made a silent promise never to give up on her dream. （读后续写·海边立志·环境烘托）

collocations.translation: 挥手示意某人继续前进/通过
collocations.example: The traffic officer waved us on with a reassuring nod, and the tension that had gripped the car finally began to ease. （读后续写·旅途·细节）

synonyms.example: A surge of pride rose in his chest as he watched the national flag climb slowly up the pole. （读后续写·荣誉·情感）
synonyms.usage: 作"一阵情绪/激增"时比 wave 更强烈、更有冲击力，强调突然而猛烈的涌动；wave 更中性、更常见

synonyms.translation: v. 拍打，挥动（翅膀、旗帜等）
synonyms.example: The flag flapped violently in the gale, a splash of defiant colour against the grey and threatening sky. （读后续写·环境·象征）
synonyms.usage: 指旗帜、翅膀等来回快速拍打，强调拍击声与动作；wave 更柔和，侧重打招呼或缓慢摆动

synonyms.example: She gestured towards the empty seat, silently inviting the weary traveller to rest. （读后续写·善意·无声交流）
synonyms.usage: 泛指用手/头示意的动作，比 wave 更宽泛，可含各种手势；wave 特指挥手这一动作

advancedExpressions.expression: a wave of ... washed / swept over sb
advancedExpressions.example: A wave of gratitude washed over me, so warm and so sudden that I had to blink back the tears threatening to fall. （"a wave of + 情绪" + wash over 拟人 + 副词强化，续写情感高潮）

advancedExpressions.expression: let us wave ... high and ...
advancedExpressions.example: Let us wave the banner of volunteering high and inspire the whole community to lend a helping hand. （祈使句号召 + 象征意象，倡议信收尾）

advancedExpressions.expression: a growing wave of ... is sweeping across ...
advancedExpressions.example: A growing wave of digital minimalism is sweeping across young people today, a quiet rebellion against the tyranny of endless notifications. （"wave of + 现象" + sweep across 描绘趋势 + 同位语点评，议论文引入）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She waved to me and I felt happy.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: She waved at me across the crowded platform, and a wave of warmth surged through my heart, dissolving in an instant all the loneliness of the long months apart. （读后续写·重逢·双关+情感）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: wave(挥手)与 a wave of warmth(一阵暖意)双关呼应 + surge through 拟人 + dissolving 现在分词状语 + 具体化情感来源(months apart)

sentenceUpgrade.original: Many people care about the environment now.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: A powerful wave of environmental consciousness is now sweeping across our society, urging ordinary citizens to rethink the true cost of their everyday choices. （议论文·环保·文体升级）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 抽象名词 wave of ... consciousness 使论点更有气势 + sweep across 动态描绘 + urge...to rethink 引出行动 + "true cost"深化论证

original_sentence: You know, it's funny what a young man recollects.
readingExamples: You know, it's funny what a young man recollects.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. & vi. to remember something, especially by making an effort to do so
(2) vt. to bring an image, event, or fact back into your mind after a period of forgetting
(3) vi. to call past experiences to mind, often in a reflective or nostalgic way

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 使镇定，使（自己）恢复镇静（recollect oneself）
uncommonMeanings.example: For a moment she stood frozen with shock; then, recollecting herself, she straightened her shoulders and walked calmly towards the waiting examiners. （读后续写·临场·恢复镇定）

posExamples.sentence: Sitting by the fading firelight, the old sailor recollected the storms he had survived, and his weathered face softened with a strange, wistful pride. （读后续写·回忆·人物刻画）
As I write this letter, I recollect with deep gratitude the countless evenings you spent patiently helping me with my English, and I owe my success to your kindness. （应用文·感谢信·回忆恩师）
When we pause to recollect, we often discover that the moments which shaped us most were not the grand triumphs but the small, quiet acts of love we once overlooked. （议论文·成长·人生反思）
Try as he might, the boy could not recollect where he had last seen his grandfather's watch, and a cold dread began to creep up his spine. （读后续写·遗失·心理）

collocations.phrase: as far as I can recollect
collocations.example: As far as I can recollect, it was on that very bench that we first shared our dreams of travelling the world together. （读后续写·回忆·友情）
I distinctly recollect promising my dying mother that I would care for my little sister, and that promise has guided every choice I have made since. （读后续写·承诺·情感）
He took a deep breath, recollected himself, and stepped onto the stage with a composure that surprised even his closest friends. （读后续写·上台·镇定）
Even now, I can vividly recollect the smell of my grandmother's kitchen and the warmth of her flour-dusted hands. （读后续写·回忆·感官细节）
Only later did she recollect that the kind stranger had never once asked for her name in return. （读后续写·善意·后知后觉）
If I recollect rightly, the annual charity fair was your idea in the first place, and it has since helped hundreds of children. （应用文·信件·委婉肯定）

synonyms.example: I still recall the exact moment my name was called out as the winner of the speech contest. （读后续写·荣誉·回忆）
synonyms.usage: 与 recollect 近义，但 recall 更常用、更中性，回忆常是直接浮现；recollect 更书面、更强调"努力去想"和怀旧色彩

synonyms.example: The old friends sat late into the night, reminiscing about the reckless adventures of their youth. （读后续写·老友·怀旧）
synonyms.usage: 特指愉快地、絮絮地"追忆往昔"，多用于口头畅谈美好回忆；recollect 侧重把某事想起来这一动作

synonyms.example: I will always remember the day you believed in me when no one else would. （读后续写·感恩·回忆）
synonyms.usage: 最普通、最口语的"记得"，可指自然记起或牢记不忘；recollect 更正式、更强调主动追忆的过程

advancedExpressions.expression: as sb recollected ..., the years seemed to melt away
advancedExpressions.example: As she recollected the summers of her childhood, the long grey years seemed to melt away, and once more she was a barefoot girl running through the golden wheat. （回忆过渡 + 时间拟人"melt away" + 具象闪回，续写倒叙）

advancedExpressions.expression: I recollect with gratitude ...
advancedExpressions.example: I recollect with heartfelt gratitude the many teachers who shaped who I am today. （"recollect with + 情感名词"，感谢信/毕业致辞正式开头）

advancedExpressions.expression: when we recollect ..., we come to realise that ...
advancedExpressions.example: When we recollect the sacrifices of previous generations, we come to realise that the comforts we take for granted were paid for in courage and toil. （"when we recollect...we realise"引出反思结论，议论文说理）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He remembered his happy childhood.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As he sat alone in the darkening room, he recollected the sunlit afternoons of his childhood — the laughter, the scraped knees, the endless summers that had once seemed as though they would never end. （读后续写·怀旧·细节堆叠）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: recollect 替换 remember 增文学感 + 破折号引出细节列举 + 三重意象(laughter, scraped knees, summers) + 用"never end"反衬时光流逝

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should think about the past.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is only when we pause to recollect the road we have travelled that we can truly appreciate how far we have come and how much we owe to those who walked beside us. （议论文·感恩·文体升级）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: it is only when...that 强调句 + recollect the road we have travelled 隐喻人生 + 两个 how 引导的宾语从句递进 + 收尾点出"感恩他人"主题

original_sentence: I don't recall what I got for my first Christmas and I don't know when I went on my first outdoor picnic.
readingExamples: I don't recall what I got for my first Christmas and I don't know when I went on my first outdoor picnic.
definitionEn:

(2) vt. to order someone to return, or to order a product to be returned (e.g. because of a fault)
(3) vt. to make you think of something because of a similarity; to be reminiscent of
(4) n. the ability to remember things; an act of officially ordering someone or something back

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 召回（有缺陷的产品）；召回（人员，如大使、议员）
uncommonMeanings.example: The company was forced to recall thousands of faulty heaters, and its once-spotless reputation crumbled overnight. （议论文·企业·诚信危机）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 记忆力，回想的能力；召回
uncommonMeanings.example: Her powers of recall were so extraordinary that she could recite, word for word, letters she had read a decade ago. （读后续写·天赋·人物特写）

posExamples.sentence: Even after all these years, I can still recall the trembling of my voice and the pounding of my heart the first time I stood before a crowd. （读后续写·第一次·紧张回忆）
I am writing to recall the wonderful days our exchange group spent in your city, and to express, on behalf of us all, our deepest thanks for your warm hospitality. （应用文·感谢信·回顾行程）
History teaches us a lesson we would do well to recall: that arrogance, however dazzling, has always been the prelude to a fall. （议论文·历史·警示）
As the familiar melody drifted from the old radio, it recalled to her a face she had spent twenty years trying, and failing, to forget. （读后续写·睹物思人·情感）

idioms.example: By the time he understood how deeply he had wounded her, the friendship was already beyond recall, lost like a letter thrown into the sea. （读后续写·遗憾·无法挽回）

collocations.example: I clearly recall telling him to be careful, yet the reckless boy paid me no heed. （读后续写·后悔·回忆）

collocations.phrase: as I recall / if I recall correctly

collocations.example: As I recall, it was a stormy night in October when the stranger first knocked upon our door. （读后续写·开篇·设置背景）
The scent of jasmine instantly recalled to mind the little courtyard where I had grown up. （读后续写·嗅觉·闪回）
I faintly recall a lullaby my mother used to hum, though the words have long since slipped away. （读后续写·童年·朦胧记忆）
Public safety must always come first, which is why responsible firms recall a product the moment a defect is discovered. （议论文·企业责任·论证）
Years of training had sharpened her powers of recall to a razor's edge. （读后续写·天赋·人物）

collocations.translation: 把某人召回；使某人回想起
collocations.example: The sharp cry recalled him to the present, and he snapped out of his daydream at once. （读后续写·回神·细节）
Some opportunities, once let slip, are gone beyond recall. （议论文·珍惜·警句）

synonyms.example: Sitting by the window, she recollected the summers she had once spent by the sea. （读后续写·怀旧·回忆）
synonyms.usage: 与 recall 近义，但 recollect 更正式、更文学，强调"努力去想、带怀旧色彩"；recall 更常用、更中性

synonyms.example: I will always remember the kindness you showed me on that cold winter's night. （读后续写·感恩·回忆）
synonyms.usage: 最普通的"记得"，既可自然记起也可牢记；recall 更强调"回想、检索出"这一过程，常需一点努力

synonyms.translation: 唤起，使人想起（情感、记忆）
synonyms.example: The faded photograph evoked a flood of memories she thought she had buried forever. （读后续写·睹物·情感）
synonyms.usage: 指某物"唤起"记忆或情感，主语常是物；recall 主语多为人（也可指物"使人想起"），evoke 情感色彩更浓

advancedExpressions.expression: even now, I can still recall ...
advancedExpressions.example: Even now, I can still recall the exact weight of his hand on my shoulder and the quiet certainty in his voice. （"even now, I can still recall"倒叙开篇 + 具体感官细节，续写回忆框架）

advancedExpressions.expression: I write to recall ... and to thank you for ...
advancedExpressions.example: I write to recall the unforgettable days of our summer camp and to thank you, most sincerely, for making them possible. （"recall...and thank"双目的并列，感谢信正式开头）

advancedExpressions.expression: we would do well to recall that ...
advancedExpressions.example: We would do well to recall that every great civilisation was built not on convenience but on sacrifice and perseverance. （"we would do well to recall that"委婉劝诫句式，议论文引历史立论）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I remember the day I won the prize.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: To this day I can vividly recall the moment my name echoed through the hall — the disbelief, the roar of applause, and the sudden, dizzying realisation that all those sleepless nights had finally been worth it. （读后续写·高光时刻·细节+心理）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: recall 替换 remember + 破折号引出三重反应(disbelief, applause, realisation) + 感官化(echoed, roar) + 用"sleepless nights"回扣前文努力

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should learn from history.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: If we pause to recall the hard-won lessons of history, we will find in them a compass reliable enough to guide us through even the darkest of times. （议论文·以史为鉴·文体升级）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: recall the lessons of history 使论点厚重 + 隐喻(a compass) + even the darkest of times 极端情境强化 + "if...we will find"条件推理结构

original_sentence: I had never seen anything so beautiful in my life. She was like an angel.

definitionEn:
(1) n. a spiritual being believed to be a servant or messenger of God, usually represented with wings and dressed in white
(2) n. a person who is very kind, good, or beautiful, or who behaves in a way that shows great goodness
(3) n. (informal) a term of endearment used to address someone you love or feel tenderly towards

posExamples.sentence: When the nurse gently wiped my fevered brow at three in the morning, she seemed less like an ordinary stranger and more like an angel sent to watch over me. （读后续写·善良·陌生人）

idioms.idiom: be on the side of the angels
idioms.example: Whatever the cost, she was determined to remain on the side of the angels, defending the weak even when it made her powerful enemies. （议论文/读后续写·正义·坚守）

idioms.idiom: fools rush in where angels fear to tread
idioms.translation: 初生牛犊不怕虎；愚者敢闯智者所惧之地
idioms.example: Fools rush in where angels fear to tread, and it was his very recklessness, oddly enough, that led him to a discovery no cautious man would ever have made. （议论文·勇气与鲁莽·辩证）

collocations.translation: 救苦救难的天使（常指护士/救助者）
collocations.example: To the wounded soldiers, the young nurse was an angel of mercy, her gentle hands the only comfort in a world of pain. （读后续写·战地·救助）

collocations.translation: 你真是个大好人（表感谢）

Behind that angelic smile, however, lay a will of iron that no obstacle could ever bend. （读后续写·人物·反差刻画）

collocations.phrase: as patient / good as an angel
collocations.translation: 像天使一样有耐心/善良
collocations.example: My grandmother was as patient as an angel, never once raising her voice in all the years she raised us. （读后续写·长辈·品格）

synonyms.example: You would need the patience of a saint to teach such a restless class, yet she never once lost her temper. （读后续写·师德·耐心）
synonyms.usage: 指品德近乎完美、极有耐心与美德的人，语气比 angel 更强调道德崇高；angel 更侧重善良、美丽或可爱

synonyms.example: The orphanage owed its very survival to an anonymous benefactor who asked for nothing in return. （议论文·慈善·无私）
synonyms.usage: 特指出钱出力帮助他人的"恩人/资助者"，正式、书面；angel 情感色彩更浓，可泛指任何善良之人

synonyms.example: 'Come here, my darling,' she said, opening her arms to the frightened child. （读后续写·亲情·爱称）
synonyms.usage: 作爱称时与 angel 类似，但 darling 更普通、更口语；angel 作爱称时带有"纯洁美好"的额外意味

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. seemed less like ... and more like an angel ...
advancedExpressions.example: In that moment she seemed less like a weary stranger and more like an angel who had wandered, by some miracle, into my hour of greatest need. （"less like...more like an angel"比较结构美化人物 + 定语从句渲染，续写升华）

advancedExpressions.expression: to us, ... were nothing short of angels

advancedExpressions.expression: the true angels among us are those who ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: The kind woman helped me and I was grateful.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The moment that gentle woman knelt to bandage my bleeding knee, I felt as though an angel had descended into the grey city street, and a warmth I had almost forgotten flooded quietly back into my heart. （读后续写·善意·比喻+情感）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 把好心人比作 angel descended + "the moment"引导时间状语聚焦画面 + as though 虚拟增文学感 + "warmth flooded back"具象化感激

sentenceUpgrade.original: Good people help others without wanting anything back.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The truest angels of this world ask for no reward and seek no applause; they simply do good in silence, and in doing so remind us of the quiet nobility of which humanity is capable. （议论文·善良·文体升级）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: angels 隐喻善良之人 + 排比否定(ask for no...seek no...) + 分号并列 + "in doing so"引出升华 + 抽象名词"nobility"拔高立意

original_sentence: My legs are just fine and dandy.
readingExamples: My legs are just fine and dandy.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. (informal, especially American English) very good; excellent; fine
(2) n. a man who is excessively concerned about his clothes and appearance; a fop
(3) adj. (dated) stylish or smart in a showy way

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 过分讲究衣着的男子，花花公子，纨绔子弟
uncommonMeanings.example: He arrived at the village fair dressed like a London dandy, his silk waistcoat and polished cane drawing amused stares from every weather-beaten farmer present. （读后续写·人物出场·反差）

posExamples.sentence: 'Everything's just fine and dandy,' the old man insisted with a brave grin, though the tremor in his hands told a very different story. （读后续写·倔强·言不由衷）
The picnic spot you recommended turned out to be absolutely dandy — sunny, sheltered and blissfully quiet — and the whole class thanks you for the wonderful suggestion. （应用文·感谢信·活动反馈）
To claim that everything in modern life is fine and dandy is to ignore, rather conveniently, the quiet anxieties gnawing beneath our polished surfaces. （议论文·批判·反讽）
Once the town's most celebrated dandy, he now sat alone in a threadbare coat, and I could not help wondering what cruel turn of fate had brought him so low. （读后续写·今昔对比·怜悯）

idioms.translation: 好得很，一切都好（有时含反讽，表示"表面没事"）
